text: Jaclyn was really unhappy with her body image. She had unfortunately gained a lot of weight during college. So Jaclyn made up her mind to start getting back in shape. She began exercising daily, eating healthier foods, and replacing sugary snacks with more nutritious options. After a few weeks of sticking to her plan, Jaclyn started to see results and her confidence grew. She also set small goals that helped motivate her to stay on track. As she worked hard to achieve her goals, she began to feel more and more proud of herself and her accomplishments.

This chapter introduces three computational methods which can be used to build graphs in arbitrary depth. They all leverage different aspects of graph theory, but share one key property: they are able to represent arbitrarily deep and random input data. These representations allow them to perform fast image feature extraction and recognition of arbitrary number of nodes while remaining amenable to parallel processing using distributed computing. Using these techniques we demonstrate that such images should reliably recover well-known classes with low false positive rate even in case the training samples have high number (e.g., 200) hidden layers. Our results are based on a test dataset of 100 million handwritten digits, each labeled with 6 distinct classes [32]. Each class was extracted with 1000 images classified into five buckets based on 2D probability distributions [25]. To make the classification more robust, we implemented two features used at each position in a network heirarchy: a minimum number of correct predictions required for classification success (called 'node error') and an inverse connection loss when no match was found, also called the'minimum similarity correction'. All algorithms use this feature for their training process by building new networks for each node without regard for its neighboring nodes or previous configurations as long as it has connections to any neighboring nodes or the entire training set including the training sequences. It is important to emphasize the fact that our models simply reinterpret some parts from the orignal features in order for the learning algorithm to get access to these information when needed. Moreover, every neural net achieves maximum accuracy only if at least one of the network's weights is non-linear, meaning a weight matrix that contains only scalars. Therefore it will always be hard to construct the network to acheive high accuracy in deep learning without introducing complexity in implementation.

The paper presents a novel approach to subspace leakage analysis and direction of arrival (DOA) estimation with small sample size. The proposed method utilizes subspace-based approach to estimate DOA of source in multipath environment with limited samples. The subspace leakage analysis is used to identify the subspace components that contribute to the leakage of source signal. The method is then applied to estimate the DOA of the source with a small sample size. The results show that proposed method outperforms the conventional methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The paper concludes that proposed method provides a reliable and efficient solution for DOA estimation in small sample size scenarios.

> We present a novel approach to visual tracking that combines the power of deep learning with the efficiency of hand-crafted features. Our approach is based on a differentiable neural architecture search (DNAS) framework that automatically learns a cell-level architecture for a tracking network. The learned architecture is then used to train a tracking network that is able to robustly track objects in challenging scenarios. We show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art trackers on the OTB-2015 and LaSOT benchmarks. The Monty-Hall Problem is a classic example of a probability puzzle. It also illustrates some common misconceptions about conditional probabilities and independence that are frequently encountered when dealing with complex problems involving chance. By examining this seemingly simple example, we can learn how to correctly model similar problems. In the end, by embracing the complexity of the real world and by understanding the limitations of simplified models, we can be better prepared to face such problems and make more informed decisions.

This paper presents a novel method of image segmentation based on multi-scale attention gates. This method takes advantage of doodles, a simple and easy to obtain annotation, to train a deep network that can accurately segment objects in images. The network is designed to learn the doodles in a variety of scales, allowing it to capture both the local and the global context. Furthermore, attention gates are used to focus on the important areas of the image, which further improves the accuracy of the segmentation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is shown in experiments on several images from the standard data set, which outperforms the current best state-of-the-art methods for image segmentation from doodles.

Overstock CEO Patrick Byrne has resigned from the company as of August 22. Shares rose 17 percent after the news was released, finishing up at 8.3 percent at the end of the day. Byrne was involved in the federal government's investigation into the 2016 election, and he was also previously in a romantic relationship with a Russian operative. Overstock's shares fell by more than 30 percent following the revelation that Byrne was involved with the government investigation. Jonathan Johnson, an Overstock board member, will be appointed as interim CEO. A full copy of Byrne's announcement letter is available to read.

Although having achieved great success in medical image segmentation, deep learning-based approaches usually require large amounts of well-annotated data, which can be extremely expensive in the field of medical image analysis. Unlabeled data, on the other hand, is much easier to acquire. Semi-supervised learning and unsupervised domain adaptation both take the advantage of unlabeled data, and they are closely related to each other. In this paper, we propose uncertainty-aware multi-view co-training (UMCT), a unified framework that addresses these two tasks for volumetric medical image segmentation. Our framework is capable of efficiently utilizing unlabeled data for better performance. We firstly rotate and permute 3D volumes into multiple views and train a 3D deep network on each view. We then apply co-training by enforcing multi-view consistency on unlabeled data, where uncertainty estimation of each view is utilized to achieve accurate labeling. Experiments on NIH pancreas segmentation dataset and multi-organ segmentation dataset show state-of-the-art performance of the proposed framework on semi-supervised medical image segmentation. Under unsupervised domain adaptation settings, we validate effectiveness of this work by adapting our multi-organ segmentation model to two pathological organs from the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Datasets. Additionally, we show that our UMCT-DA model can even effectively handle challenging situation where labeled source data is inaccessible, demonstrating strong potentials for real-world applications.

Federated learning allows distributed medical institutions to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model with privacy protection. While at clinical deployment, the models trained in federated learning can still suffer from performance drop when applied to completely unseen hospitals outside the federation. In this paper, we point out and solve a novel problem setting of federated domain generalization (FedDG), which aims to learn a federated model from multiple distributed source domains such that it can directly generalize to unseen target domains. We present a novel approach, named as Episodic Learning in Continuous Frequency Space (ELCFS), for this problem by enabling each client to exploit multi-source data distributions under the challenging constraint of data decentralization. Our approach transmits the distribution information across clients in a privacy-protecting way through an effective continuous frequency space interpolation mechanism. With the transferred multi-source distributions, we further carefully design a boundary-oriented episodic learning paradigm to expose the local learning to domain distribution shifts and particularly meet the challenges of model generalization in medical image segmentation scenario. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated with superior performance over state-of-the-arts and in-depth ablation experiments on two medical image segmentation tasks. The code is available at "https://github.com/liuquande/FedDG-ELCFS".

Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a reductive group defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ and let $\mathfrak{S}$ be a Siegel set in $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{R})$. The Siegel property tells us that there are only finitely many $\gamma \in \mathbf{G}(\mathbb{Q})$ of bounded determinant and denominator for which the translate $\gamma.\mathfrak{S}$ intersects $\mathfrak{S}$. We prove a bound for the heigth of these $\gamma$ which is polynomial with respect to the determinant and denominator. The bound generalises a result of Habegger and Pila dealing with the case of $\mathbf{GL}_2$, and has applications to the Zilber--Pink conjecture on unlikely intersections in Shimura varieties. In addition we prove that if $\mathbf{H}$ is a subgroup of $\mathbf{G}$, then every Siegel set for $\mathbf{H}$ is contained in a finite union of $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{Q})$-translates of a Siegel set for $\mathbf{G}$).

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) missed a deadline to name a squad for the tournament after the International Cricket Council (ICC) changed its revenue-sharing model. However, the BCCI has now announced the Indian squad for the ICC Champions Trophy. The squad is led by Virat Kohli and includes seasoned players such as MS Dhoni, Yuvraj Singh, and Ravichandran Ashwin, as well as new faces such as Jasprit Bumrah and Kedar Jadhav. The Indian team will begin its campaign against Pakistan on June 4, and will look to defend its title after winning the previous edition of the tournament in 2013.

Hoop, the dating app that matches people based on their Snapchat interests, has hit 2 in the App Store. The app, which launched in November, has been downloaded more than 1.5 million times. Hoop allows users to connect with people who have similar interests on Snapchat. The app also allows users to send Snaps to each other without having to add each other as friends on Snapchat. "We're excited to see such success in such a short period of time," said Hoop CEO Jorge Valdez. "It's a testament to the power of our platform and the demand for a better way to connect on Snapchat." Hoop is the latest dating app to find success by catering to a specific audience. The app has been compared to Tinder, but for Snapchat users. "I think the key to our success is that we're laser-focused on Snapchat," Valdez said. "There are a lot of dating apps out there, but most of them don't integrate with Snapchat. We saw an opportunity to create a better experience for Snapchat users." Hoop is available for free on the App Store.

In recent discoveries from NASA's Juno spacecraft, it has been speculated that Europa, one of Jupiter's moons, is covered in dozens of ice spikes, some as tall as 50 feet. While the findings are both fascinating and awe-inspiring, they pose a potential challenge for future spacecraft looking to land on Europa. The ice spikes, which are believed to be made of frozen water, methane or other compounds, could make it difficult for spacecraft to safely land on the moon's surface. "We do not yet understand how these giant ice spikes form," said Dr. Caitlin Griffith, a planetary scientist at the University of Arizona. Europa has long been of interest to astronomers and scientists alike because of the possibility of life existing in its subterranean ocean. These new findings only add to the intrigue surrounding the icy world. NASA's upcoming mission to Europa, the Europa Clipper, is set to launch in the 2020s and will carry a suite of scientific instruments to study the moon's ice shell, subsurface ocean, and geology. However, the potential obstacles of the ice spikes may force scientists to re-think their landing strategy. "We're going to have to be very careful where we land," said Dr. Ian Crawford, a professor of planetary science and astrobiology at University College London. As NASA and other space agencies continue to explore the far reaches of our solar system and beyond, discoveries such as these ice spikes on Europa remind us of the vast, unknown mysteries that await us.

Dug, a heroic and adventurous canine, has made a miraculous recovery after being bitten by a rattlesnake while hiking with his owner, Lindsay Castro, in Fontana, Canada. The pair were enjoying a scenic hike when Lindsay heard the unmistakable sound of a rattle in the brush. Sensing potential danger, she backed away from the area, but Dug bravely ran toward the noise. In the blink of an eye, the venomous snake sprang out and sunk its fangs into Dug's face, causing it to swell to twice its size. Despite the traumatic incident, quick-thinking Lindsay rushed her beloved pet to a nearby veterinarian for emergency treatment. Over the course of two days, Dug underwent intensive antidote therapy to counteract the venom from the rattlesnake bite. Thanks to the swift action of his owner and the skilled veterinary team, the brave four-legged explorer will make a full recovery and is expected to return home soon. The incident serves as a reminder for hikers and pet owners to be aware of their surroundings and to exercise caution when exploring the great outdoors. Lindsay expressed her gratitude towards the veterinary staff and her relief that Dug is now on the mend. She also plans to share her experience with other pet owners and educate them on the importance of being vigilant while out exploring with their furry companions. As for Dug, his courageous act demonstrates the unwavering loyalty and love that our canine companions provide. While his adventurous spirit may have landed him in trouble this time, there is no doubt that he will continue to be a beloved and brave member of Lindsay's family.

Tens of thousands of pilgrims joined him for the Way of the Cross ceremony, recalling Jesus' crucifixion. Among the cross bearers were Syrian and Iraqi refugees, and Nigerians who had escaped Boko Haram persecution. The service came a day after almost 150 people were killed in an al-Shabab attack on a Kenyan university. "We still see today our persecuted brothers, decapitated and crucified for their faith in you [Jesus], before our eyes and often with our complicit silence," Pope Francis said, presiding over the ceremony at the Colosseum. Earlier, he condemned the attack in Kenya, where Christians were singled out and shot, as an act of "senseless brutality." In another Good Friday ceremony, Pope Francis listened as the Vatican's official preacher Raniero Cantalamessa denounced the "disturbing indifference of world institutions in the face of all this killing of Christians." He too mentioned the Kenya attack, as well as the beheading of 22 Egyptian Coptic Christians by Islamic State (IS) militants in Libya in February. Pope Francis has spoken out against the persecution of Christians before, saying that the world would be justified using military force to combat the "unjust aggression" by IS.

Emmerson Whittel may need surgery on his jaw, while the club alleges player Josh Lynam was also bitten on the ear. The RFL's match review panel will look at official video on Thursday, as it does for all on-field incidents. Keighley have gathered additional video from spectators following an appeal. Footage already online, shot from the stands, shows a number of fights breaking out on the field between the two sets of players. Following the incident, Whittel posted on Twitter that brackets and bands had been used to try to re-align his jaw and that he faces at least three months out. Keighley Cougars of League One, England's third-tier competition, progressed to the Challenge Cup fourth round with a 50-32 win over Fryston Warriors - a side from the second tier of England's amateur game. The match, a "home" game for Fryston, was played at nearby Featherstone in West Yorkshire after the tie was at risk of being reversed and played at Keighley instead. Keighley have also complained to the RFL about their off-field treatment before kick-off, as they allege players and members of staff were refused entry to the ground without a valid matchday ticket. A statement on Keighley's website said: "The players' allocation of'family and friends' tickets was then claimed to have been used to admit the playing squad and coaching staff into the ground. "The club is outraged by this development." The BBC contacted Fryston Warriors, who have declined to comment at this time.

This academic paper presents a novel approach to referring segmentation, a task that involves identifying object referred to in a natural language description. The proposed method, called cross-modal progressive comprehension, utilizes both visual and linguistic features to improve accuracy of referring segmentation. The approach is based on a deep neural network that progressively refines its understanding of input image and language description, leading to more accurate object localization and classification. Experimental results on two benchmark datasets demonstrate effectiveness of the proposed method, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches for referring segmentation.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in medicine and computer vision that aims to identify important features from medical images such as organs, tissues, or pathologies. Traditional image segmentation methods rely on hand-crafted parametres and have limited generalisation capabilities. In recent years, deep learning algorithms like convolutional neural networks (CNN) have achieved state-of-the-art results by automatically learning patterns in raw images. However, CNN requires large amounts of annotated training data which can be expensive and time-consuming. In this study, we propose a novel multi-modal convolutional neural network with image fusion techniques for efficient medical image segmentation using limited labelled data. We applied our proposed method to various benchmark datasets including MRI, CT, and X-ray images and demonstrated significant improvements over traditional methods. Furthermore, the effectiveness of different image fusion schemes was thoroughly examined and compared based on different evaluation metrics. The proposed work shows promising results and paves the way for developing more robust and efficient medical image segmentation tools using limited labelled data.

We introduce a novel Deep Learning methodology, which accurately estimates image segmentation quality without the need for human inspection or labeling. We refer to this approach as a Quality Quality System -- QANet. Thus, given an image and a `proposed' corresponding segmentation, obtained by any technique including manual annotation, the QANet solves a regression problem in order to estimate a predefined quality measure with regard to the unknown ground truth. The QANet is by no means not a segmentation technique. However, it performs a multi-level, multi-feature comparison of an image-segmentation pair based on a unique network architecture, termed the RibCage. To prove the strength of the QANet, we addressed the evaluation of instance segmentation using three distinct data from multiple domains, namely, low throughput live cell microscopy images from the Cell Segmentation Benchmark and natural images of trees from the Flower Segmentation Challenge. While synthesized segmentations were designed to train the QANet, it was tested on segmentations provided by publicly accessible tools that engaged in the same challenges. We show that the QANet accurately estimates the scores of the evaluated segmentations with regard to the hidden ground truth, as published by the challenges' organizers. This academic paper presents a novel approach to referring segmentation, a task that involves identifying the object referred to in a natural language description. The proposed method, called cross-modal progressive comprehension, utilizes both visual and linguistic features to improve the accuracy of referring segmentation. The approach is based on a deep neural network that progressively refines its understanding of the input image and language description, leading to more accurate object localization and classification. Experimental results on two benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches for referring segmentation.

Fully supervised deep neural networks for segmentation usually require a massive amount of pixel-level labels which are manually expensive to create. In this work, we develop a multi-task learning method to relax this constraint. We regard the segmentation problem as a sequence of approximation subproblems that are recursively defined and in increasing levels of approximation accuracy. The subproblems are handled by a framework that consists of 1) a segmentation task that learns from pixel-level ground truth segmentation masks of a small fraction of the images, 2) a recursive approximation task that conducts partial object regions learning and data-driven mask evolution starting from partial masks of each object instance, and 0) other problem oriented auxiliary tasks that are trained with sparse annotations and promote the learning of dedicated features. Most training images are only labeled by (rough) partial masks, which do not contain exact object boundaries, rather than by their full segmentation masks. During the training phase, the approximation task learns the statistics of these partial masks, and the partial regions are recursively increased towards object boundaries aided by the learned information from the segmentation task in a fully data-driven fashion. The network is trained on an extremely small amount of precisely segmented images and a large set of coarse labels. Annotations can thus be obtained in a cheap way. We demonstrate the efficiency of our approach in three applications with microscopy images and ultrasound images.

Person2: We import a little oil from Venezuela, but we are fairly self-sufficient. We import some iron and a lot of aluminium from neighbouring countries. Engineers in my country are focusing on drilling for oil. The government is keen to exploit our natural resources to get money to improve our country. We need to put the money into long-term projects rather than wasting it on short-term ones.

A man who won 500 on a scratch-off lottery ticket fatally shot his girlfriend and then himself after the pair got into a heated row about sharing the winnings. Terry Martin, 48, shot his girlfriend Laurice Hampton, 48, after she asked for half of the proceeds. But Hampton, critically injured from a gunshot wound to her chest, was able to call 911 about 6:30am Saturday to report the shootings before she died. Responding officers found the couple inside their master bedroomat their home on Beaty Street in Fort Worth, Texas, where Martin was pronounced dead from a gunshot wound to the head. Hampton was taken by ambulance to John Peter Smith Hospital but died a few hours later. Homicide Sergeant Joe Loughman said the tragic couple had known each other since childhood and had lived together for several years. The basic problem of robot vision is that the power of the semantic classification models is restricted by the availability of the training sets. We propose a method of eliminating bias in the training of semantic classification models using synthetic data. We first train a semantic classification model using a simulated data set, and then transfer the features of the model to a real data-trained model. We demonstrate the superiority of the unbiased model in the Cityscapes dataset. Moreover, the unbiased model is more resistant to the shift of the domain. It is the abstract of the paper published on the arXiv: Semantic segmentation is the foundation of robot perception, but the performance of semantic segmentation models is limited by the availability of labeled data. We propose a method of unbundling the features of the semantic classification model using the transfer of the features of synthetic data. We first train a semantic classification model with simulated data and then transfer the features of the model to a real-world trained model. We show that the unbiased model outperforms the conventional model in the Cityscapes dataset. Moreover, the unbiased model is more resistant to domain shift. This is the full text of the paper published on the arXiv: ... The resulting unbiased model can outperform the conventional model on the Cityscapes dataset, and it is also resistant to domain shift. The feature transfer method is robust to the shift of the training set.

This paper presents a novel Spatial Guided Self-supervised Clustreing Network (SGS-Net) for medical image segmentation. The proposed approach utilises a self-supervised clustreing method to learn meaningful representations from unlabelled data, which are then used to guide the segmentation network. The SGS-Net incorporates a spatial guidance module that enforces consistency between the learned clustres and the spatial structure of the image, improving the accuracy of the segmentation results. Experimental results on two medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

> Semantic image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, which aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image. Recently, deep learning-based methods have achieved great success in this task. However, the success of deep learning-based methods also brings new security and privacy concerns. In this paper, we study the membership inference attack (MIA) in semantic image segmentation. Specifically, we propose a novel MIA method, called Segmentations-Leak, which can infer whether a given image is in the training set of a target model. We conduct extensive experiments on three public datasets, i.e., Cityscapes, CamVid, and ADE20K, and show that our method can achieve high attack success rates. We also propose a defense method, called Segmentations-Shuffle, which can effectively defend against our attack. Our experiments show that Segmentations-Shuffle can significantly reduce the attack success rate. The paper is available here.

``` With the rise of convolutional neural networks (CNN), machine learning algorithms that depend on image or volume pixel intensities have significantly increased their predictive power; However, such methods are not sub-optimal when used with images from strongly imbalanced data unlike those common in clinical applications because they seem to be biased towards discriminating pixels coupled with small numbers of training cases which can lead to an overfitted model being trained, i.e., one prone to producing assumptions within the generalization range. Additionally, when performing segmentations within multi-phase images a number of distinct objects (i.e., organs) can also be analyzed independently without any obvious hierarchies between them existing prior to image acquisition such as with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). A novel algorithm called fully connected conditional recurrent neural network (FCCRN) was subsequently devised that combines the convolutional design of a CNN with the nonparametric nature of hidden Markov models to produce a hybrid system that is incapable of analyzing individual information points. In this work we extend these concepts by using long short term memory units and gated linear units within the RNN component while additionally suggesting three methods of transforming low dimensional MRI images into 2D matrices appropriate for use within the proposed framework: slicewise partitioning followed by transforming into matrix form versus direct conversion using a random sampling method. We evaluate our method against baseline technologies including a traditional FCNN segmenter and other similar varieties of CNN/hidden Markov architectures along with fully supervised CNNs via extensive comparison with ground truth statistics derived from human expert readings of four organ networks using four methods from four public datasets of differing sizes. Our findings indicate it is necessary to minimize subject sensitivity compared to most competing algorithms and outperform the accuracy levels of conventional machine learning based schemes even for classes composed of just single digit samples while increasing runtime requirements by many orders of magnitude. ```

Through an examination of various research studies utilizing diverse datasets and evaluation Metrics, we aim to provide Insights into both the strengths and limitations of using deep learning Methods within this domain. Ultimately, our goal is to contribute towards fostering critical discourse surrounding Contemporary Machine learning trends so that researchers can better navigate through the hype cycle when selecting appropriate tools for their specific applications.

The segmentation of medical images is a fundamental step in automated clinical decision support systems. Existing medical image segmentation methods based on supervised deep learning, however, remain problematic because of their reliance on large amounts of labelled training data. Although medical imaging data repositories continue to expand, there has not been a commensurate increase in the amount of annotated data. Hence, we propose a new spatial guided self-supervised clustering network (SGSCN) for medical image segmentation, where we introduce multiple loss functions designed to aid in grouping image pixels that are spatially connected and have similar feature representations. It iteratively learns feature representations and clustering assignment of each pixel in an end-to-end fashion from a single image. We also propose a context-based consistency loss that better delineates the shape and boundaries of image regions. It enforces all the pixels belonging to a cluster to be spatially close to the cluster centre. We evaluated our method on 2 public medical image datasets and compared it to existing conventional and self-supervised clustering methods. Experimental results show that our method was most accurate for medical image segmentation.

This journal describes and describes multiple and single snapshot compressive beamforming methods for imaging systems. Compressive beamforming is a method that utilizes a sparse representation of the signal to recover an image from a large number of observations. Multi snapshot compressive beamforming employs a single measurement vector to reconstruct the image, while multiple snapshot compression beamforming employs different measuring vectors taken at same times or from multiple angles. The journal provides a detailed evaluation of the efficiency of multiple and single snapshot compressive beamforming methods in terms of image quality, computational simplicity, and sensitivity to noise. The findings show that multiple snapshot compressive beamforming gives greater image quality and sensitivity to noise compared to double snapshot compressive beamforming, even in the absence of non-stationary targets or clutter. Also, multiple snapshot compression beamforming takes more computational resources and is more susceptible to motion artifacts. The paper therefore suggests a new multiple snapshot compression beamforming technique that emphasizes the benefits of multiple snapshot and double snapshot compressive beamforming. This technique provides a hybrid method that uses the spatial and spatial information from several images to reduce picture reliability and sensitivity to noise. The findings show that the proposed technique outperforms conventional double and several snapshot compressive beamforming techniques in terms of image quality and sensitivity to noise. The paper allows a detailed analysis of the proposed approach through experiments and experimental findings using a phased array radar system. The findings indicate the efficacy of the proposed technique in imaging targets in the absence of clutter and non-stationary targets. Overall, this paper gives a detailed comparison of multiple and single snapshot compressive beamforming methods and suggests a new hybrid method that emphasizes the benefits of both techniques. The proposed approach has significant applications in imaging systems such as radar, radar, and optical imaging.

We build a visual salience-based feature processing program based on multiscale deep features that permits capturing hierarchical information without focusing on prior training data. Our method exploits probabilistic representations in the context of depth-sorted spatial salience maps such as binocular rivalry, where one can provide exact probabilities for each layer of the map at various scales. In addition to studying spatial structures and creating visual maps of different scales, we provide novel methods for solving spatial and spatial constraints with small dimensions while maintaining the local structure of the image. By using probabilistically driven classification with the high-dimensional nature of a hierarchy-free reconstruction map, our findings demonstrate for first time realistic classification efficiency over diverse tasks related to perception and cognitive knowledge capture. Our studies show substantial improvements over existing depth- and shape-specific algorithms (Bresenham et al., 2010; Karpathy et al., 2012), including high latency and low precision, under varying environmental circumstances which certainly demonstrates their broad effectiveness via natural language comprehension systems. Our findings demonstrate the sensitivity of the resulting classifiers to differences caused by task complexity. The most noticeable performance variations are among deep perceptrons and neural connections – on tasks with high or medium correlation to our salience perceptron. These studies suggest interesting possibilities for using them together not only in other datasets and learning models but in more general domains of AI.

Abstract: Accurate segmentation of cells in microscopy images is crucial for various biological applications, including cell counting, cell classification, and cell tracking. However, cell segmentation remains a challenging task due to variations in cell size, shape, and appearance, as well as the complexity of the background. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning model, called Feedback U-Net, to improve the accuracy of cell image segmentation. The proposed Feedback U-Net model is built upon a U-Net architecture, which is a popular deep learning model for image segmentation tasks. However, unlike traditional U-Net models that rely solely on the output of the final layer for segmentation, our Feedback U-Net model incorporates feedback connections that allow it to refine the segmentation results based on the error between the predicted mask and the ground truth mask. This feedback mechanism enables the model to learn from its mistakes and adapt to the specific characteristics of the input images, leading to improved segmentation accuracy. We evaluate the performance of Feedback U-Net on several benchmark datasets, including the Cells dataset, the Blood cells dataset, and the Cell- nuclei segmentation dataset. The results show that our model outperforms state-of-the-art U-Net models, including U-Net, U-Net++ , and Attention U-Net, in terms of segmentation accuracy. Specifically, Feedback U-Net achieves an average dice similarity coefficient of 0.867 on the Cells dataset, which is 3.4% higher than the best performing competitor model. We also perform a series of ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of the feedback connections and the impact of different design choices on the model's performance. The results suggest that the feedback connections improve the model's ability to capture fine details and handle complex cell boundaries, and that the optimal number of feedback connections is dataset-dependent. Our Feedback U-Net model has important implications for cell image segmentation tasks, particularly in situations where accurate segmentation is critical, such as in medical diagnosis and drug development. The improved segmentation accuracy achieved by our model can help reduce errors in downstream analysis and enable more accurate assessments

There is no doubt that we are in dire need of better ways of handling problem where deep learning and regression problems do not fit our requirements, which are highly complicated segmentation task tasks such as feature extraction or object recognition. We present here alternative solution by introducing the new concept of inter-extremity geoderricks (IER): set of georeferenced geodesic line representations. These are not strictly convex line representations but they approximate this condition for subset of points along a curve whose edge passes through no part of a point (i.e. their segment). Erecting set that fits all points as per feature extraction and object detection schemes (based on local minima) can reduce the number and distance search distance by about 10 times, thereby dramatically reducing computation time and memory requirement (and improving accuracy), due largely to better preprocessing step. Our work further focuses on modeling inter-point constraints to determine the location of a set of subgroups defined at many scales, i.e. all parts or edge points. By using computers to do experimental manipulations on Fourier series, we construct additional series with interesting properties. We construct several series whose sums remain unchanged when the $n^{th}$ term is multiplied by $\sin(n)/n$. One example is this classic series for $\pi/4$: \[ \frac{\pi}{4} = 1 - \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{7} + \dots = 1 \cdot \frac{\sin(1)}{1} - \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{\sin(3)}{3} + \frac{1}{5} \cdot \frac{\sin(5)}{5} - \frac{1}{7} \cdot \frac{\sin(7)}{7} + \dots . \] Another example is \[ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\sin(n)}{n} = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \left(\frac{\sin(n)}{n}\right)^2 = \frac{\pi-1}{2}. \] This paper also discusses an included Mathematica package that makes it easy to calculate and graph the Fourier series of many types of functions.

Galvani Bioelectronics hopes to bring a new treatment based on the technique before regulators within seven years. GlaxoSmithKline and Verily, formerly Google, Life Sciences, are behind it. Animal experiments have attached tiny silicone cuffs, containing electrodes, around a nerve and then used a power supply to control the nerve's messages. One set of tests suggested the approach could help treat type-2 diabetes, in which the body ignores the hormone insulin. They focused on a cluster of chemical sensors near the main artery in the neck that check levels of sugar and the hormone insulin. The sensors send their findings back to the brain, via a nerve, so the organ can coordinate the body's response to sugar in the bloodstream. GSK vice-president of bioelectronics Kris Famm told the BBC News website: "The neural signatures in the nerve increase in type 2-diabetes. "By blocking those neural signals in diabetic rats, you see the sensitivity of the body to insulin is restored." And early work suggested it could work in other diseases too. "It isn't just a one-trick-pony, it is something that if we get it right could have a new class of therapies on our hands," Mr Famm said. But he said the field was only "scratching the surface" when it came to understanding which nerve signals have what effect in the body. Both the volume and rhythm of the nerve signals could be having an effect rather than it being a simple case of turning the nerve on or off. And even if the approach works theoretically, a huge amount of effort will be needed to make the technology practical. The kits to hack the nerves will need to be miniaturised, customisable to different patients' nerves, durable enough to survive in the body long-term and have sufficient battery power. Dr Famm added: "In 10 to 20 years I think there will be a set of these miniaturised precision therapies that will be available for you and me when we go to a doctor." Verily chief technology officer Brian Otis said: "Bioelectronic medicine is a new area of therapeutic exploration, and we know that success will require the confluence of deep disease biology expertise and new highly miniaturised technologies. "This partnership provides an opportunity to further Verily's mission by deploying our focused expertise in low power, miniaturised therapeutics and our data analytics engine to potentially address many disease areas with greater precision

inter Extreme Points (IEPs) provide a promising approach to weakly supervised image segmentation. IEPs are points in images that can be computed from A small region around Them using geometric properties such as distance and angles, without requiring explicit object detection or pixel-level labeling. In our work, we explore their potential in weakly supervised automatic segmentation by analyzing their structural relationships with local Neighbors and other regions within an image. We show That IEPs possess rich information about object boundaries, shape, texture, and contextual hierarchy, which makes them Well suited for weak supervision. However, direct use of IEPs is limited by their low resolution compared with pixels, leading to spatial ambiguity. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework that constructs intermediate representations between spatial neighborhoods and pixels based on smooth 3-D geodetic paths connecting Extreme points across regions with similar geometric structures. our scheme explicitly exploits spatial continuity, while preserving local geometric relationships among elements in these regions. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of intermediate levels Of supervisory information using IEPs to improve accuracy for both unsupervised And semi-supervised image segmentation tasks. It Also enables visualization of underlying image structure through analysis of IEP cluster connectivity patterns. Overall, our proposed method offers new insights into interpreting spatial hierarchy and integrating nonlocal features at various scales and resolutions for weakly supervised image processing in computer vision applications.

This research introduces CHASE, a novel visual tracking algorithm that utilizes cell-level differentiable neural architecture search to enhance robustness. Through extensive experiments and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in challenging scenarios characterized by fast motion, occlusion, illumination changes, and complex backgrounds. Our method achieves promising results while providing flexibility and efficiency through its adaptive neural network design learned directly from data. Overall, this study highlights the potential of combining NAS techniques with computer vision applications such as object detection and segmentation, opening up new avenues for future work on personalized models adaptable to diverse environments.

Abstract This project introduces ConvNet, a multi-dimensional deep convolutional neural network architecture that aims to be flexible and scalable in implementing different image segmentations tasks with minimal computational input/output dependencies. In this paper, we present RLCorrector, a novel approach to connectomics image segmentation that leverages reinforcement learning to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the proofreading process. Connectomics is an emerging field that aims to map the neural connections within the brain, and image segmentation is a crucial step in this process. However, current methods often suffer from errors and inconsistencies in the produced masks, which can significantly impact the subsequent analysis and interpretation of the data. To address these limitations, we propose RLCorrector, which combines reinforcement learning with a proofreading framework to optimise the correction of errors in the masks. Our approach uses a deep neural network to learn a policy that accurately identifies and corrects errors in the masks, while also adapting to various types of mistakes and anomalies. We evaluate RLCorrector on several datasets and compare it to existing methods, demonstrating its superior performance and ability to produce high-quality masks with reduced manual effort. We also perform a series of ablation studies to analyse the effects of different components of our method and provide insights into the reinforcement learning process. The results show that RLCorrector achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, outperforming traditional proofreading methods and other baselines. Additionally, we demonstrate the versatility of our approach by applying it to various connectomics imageing modalities, including electron microscopy and fluorescence microscopy. Our work has significant implications for the future of connectomics research, as it provides a reliable and efficient means of producing accurate masks for neural connection tracing. By improving the quality and consistency of the data, RLCorrector has the potential to accelerate discoveries in neuroscience and enhance our understanding of the brain's complex neural networks.

This paper examines inertial particle acceleration in a strained turbulent fluid flow. Using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis, it is shown how particles acquire energy from the surrounding turbulence through a process called stochastic acceleration. In this regard, it is found that the strained zones within the turbulence act as energy bottlenecks that increase the probability of occurrence of high-energy particles. The significance of these results for the understanding of asteroid dynamics in the interstellar space and the early Solar System is also discussed.

Angular equivalence is introduced and shown to be an equivalence relation among the norms on a fixed real vector space. It is a finer notion than the usual (topological) notion of norm equivalence. Angularly equivalent norms share certain geometric properties: A norm that is angularly equivalent to a uniformly convex norm is itself uniformly convex. The same is true for strict convexity. Extreme points of the unit balls of angularly equivalent norms occur on the same rays, and if one unit ball is a polyhedron so is the other. Among norms arising from inner products, two norms are angularly equivalent if and only if they are topological equivalent. But, unlike topological equivalence, angular equivalence is able to distinguish between different norms on a finite-dimensional space. In particular, no two $\ell^p$ norms on $\mathbb R^n$ are angularly equivalent.

The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of these findings for the study of geometry and topology. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of rational sets in Euclidean spaces and spheres, and contributes to our understanding of fundamental concepts and structures that underlie these important mathematical objects.

Brattleboro rats have a genetic mutation that results in a lack of vasopressin production, leading to diabetes insipidus, a condition characterized by polyuria (excessive urination) and polydipsia (excessive thirst). Vasopressin V2 receptors, primarily located in the collecting ducts of the kidneys, are associated with regulating water reabsorption. Studies have shown that when V2 receptors are selectively blocked in Brattleboro rats using V2 receptor antagonists, their urine output increases, and their urine becomes more diluted. This demonstrates that there is still some V2-mediated water reabsorption taking place in these rats, which would otherwise have been masked by the background of diabetes insipidus. However, one must note that although V2 receptor blockade can reveal this effect, it does not fully restore normal water reabsorption or reverse diabetes insipidus in Brattleboro rats. Other treatments, such as hormone replacement with synthetic vasopressin analogs, might be needed for that purpose.

This paper investigates the combination of space shift keying (SSK) modulation and multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology for energy efficient transmission over wireless channels. SSK is a simple and low-complexity modulation technique that offers high spectral efficiency, while MIMO technology can significantly improve channel capacity and reliability. The proposed system uses SSK to modulate data symbols onto multiple transmit antennas, which are then transmitted over a MIMO channel. The paper focuses on developing novel techniques for optimizing the energy efficiency of the SSK-MIMO system. Firstly, we propose a new algorithm for estimating the spatial distribution of the channel state information, which is used to optimize the precoding matrices for maximum energy efficiency. Secondly, we introduce a hybrid power allocation scheme that jointly optimizes the transmit power and number of active transmit antennas to minimize the total transmit power while maintaining a targeted level of performance. Finally, we investigate the use of non-linear amplification schemes to further enhance the energy efficiency of the system. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed techniques in achieving significant improvements in energy efficiency compared to conventional MIMO systems. Specifically, our results show that the proposed SSK-MIMO system achieves a reduction in transmit power consumption of up to 50% while maintained a fixed level of performance. Furthermore, we observe that the hybrid power allocation scheme outperforms traditional power allocation methods in terms of energy efficiency, while the non-linear amplification schemes provide additional gains in energy efficiency. Overall, this paper demonstrates the potential of SSK-MIMO systems for energy efficient transmission over wireless channels. Our findings highlight the importance of carefully designing the system components, including precoding matrices, power allocation, and amplification schemes, to achieve optimal energy efficiency without compromising performance.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to weakly supervised segmentation, called Inter Extreme Points Geodesics (IEPG), which leverages the concept of geodesics in the space of probability distributions to segment objects in images. Unlike traditional segmentation methods that rely on strongly supervised learning or fully convolutional networks, IEPG only requires weak supervision in the form of bounding boxes around the objects of interest. The key insight behind IEPG is that the geodesic distance between the probability distributions of pixels in the image and the bounding box can be used to identify the pixels that belong to the object. We propose an efficient algorithm to compute the geodesic distance and use it to optimize a segmentation mask that separates the object from the background. We evaluate the performance of IEPG on several benchmark datasets, including PASCAL VOC and Cityscapes, and show that it achieves competitive segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, while requiring significantly less annotated data. We also demonstrate the versatility of IEPG by applying it to various segmentation tasks, such as instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, and video segmentation. The main contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows: * We introduce a novel approach to weakly supervised segmentation based on inter extreme points geodesics, which only requires weak supervision in the form of bounding boxes. * We propose an efficient algorithm to compute the geodesic distance between probability distributions and use it to optimize a segmentation mask. * We demonstrate the effectiveness of IEPG on several benchmark datasets and show that it achieves competitive segmentation accuracy with significantly less annotated data. * We highlight the versatility of IEPG by applying it to various segmentation tasks, including instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, and video segmentation. Overall, this paper provides a new perspective on weakly supervised segmentation and offers a promising solution for segmenting objects in images with minimal annotation effort.

We study relations between global characteristics of low-redshift (0 < z < 1) compact star-forming galaxies, including absolute optical magnitudes, Hbeta emission-line luminosities (or equivalently star-formation rates), stellar masses, and oxygen abundances. The sample consists of 5182 galaxies with high-excitation HII regions selected from the SDSS DR7 and SDSS/BOSS DR10 surveys adopting a criterion [OIII]4959/Hbeta > 1. We find that in all diagrams low-z and high-z star-forming galaxies are closely related indicating a very weak dependence of metallicity on stellar mass, redshift, and star-formation rate. The research analyses how changes in data distribution affect the training and generalisation capabilities of deep learning models, with a focus on semantic segmentation tasks using medical imageing datasets. By conducting experiments under various shifting settings, we provide insights into addressing this challenge by suggesting relevant strategies to mitigate its effects. Our results highlight that understanding such issues is essential for designing robust architectures capable of generalising well across different domains without sacrificing accuracy.

This paper develops a method to carry out large-$N$ asymptotic analysis of a class of $N$-dimensional integrals arising in the context of the so-called quantum separation of variables method. We push further ideas developed in the context of random matrices of size $N$, but in present problem, two scales $1/N^{\alpha}$ and $1/N$ naturally occur. In our case, equilibrium measure is $N^{\alpha}$-dependent and characterised by means of the solution to a $2\times 2$ Riemann--Hilbert problem, whose large-$N$ behavior is analysed in detail. Combining these results with techniques of concentration of measures and an asymptotic analysis of the Schwinger-Dyson equations at the distributional level, we obtain large-$N$ behavior of the free energy explicitly up to $o(1)$. The use of distributional Schwinger-Dyson is novelty that allows us treating sufficiently differentiable interactions and mixing of scales $1/N^{\alpha}$ and $1/N$, thus waiving analyticity assumptions often used in random matrix theory.

Connection structure provides the basic insight that images are composed of small regions—nodes, edges or vertices—that communicate and interact with one another in meaningful ways across a large volume of semantic space. This notion has been well-tethered to the idea of word embeddings on an existing neural network context; however, it appears that these same conceptual constructs may also be used by a new approach to connectionist verification without any explicit mapping to word embeddings. RLCcorrector adds reinforcement learning functionality to this traditional proofreading paradigm (see [1] http://arxiv.org/abs/0121.1229), and integrates it with existing machine pattern recognition algorithms such as Gaussian Process and Markov chains. RLCcorrectors allow for both error detection (using unsupervised feature learning) and inference (by using high-level supervised models that utilize the features present in the evidence). For errors, we use word vectors that encode information about the locations of the locations of words within a sentence and then detect similar occurrences in different documents. With the current algorithm, if two adjacent documents have not yet touched each other, our model suggests that their occurrence should correspond to some common location. A few moments later when they begin crossing over, the error becomes more apparent. Thus, this system can quickly learn patterns such as the positions of words contained inside sentences based on prior knowledge to correct erroneous matches that might otherwise elude prediction.[9][3] We show how RLCcorrectors can extend commonly used automatic annotation systems like Wordnet and Snippets to include connectionist approaches, adding validation and support information. The end-to-end process required for connecting word embeddings and connectionist training methods yields improved readability and overall comprehension through higher levels of abstraction than previously available. Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for cross-modality medical image segmentation has shown great progress by domain-invariant feature learning or image appearance translation. Adapted feature learning usually cannot detect domain shifts at the pixel level and is not able to achieve good results in dense semantic segmentation tasks. Image appearance translation, e.g. CycleGAN, translates images into different styles with good appearance, despite its population, its semantic consistency is hardly to maintain and results in poor cross-modality segmentation. In this paper, we propose intra- and cross-modality semantic consistency (ICMSC) for UDA and our key insight is that the segmentation of synthesised images in different styles should be consistent. Specifically, our model consists of an image translation module and a domain-specific segmentation module. The image translation module is a standard CycleGAN, while the segmentation module contains two domain-specific segmentation networks. The intra-modality semantic consistency (IMSC) forces the reconstructed image after a cycle to be segmented in the same way as the original input image, while the cross-modality semantic consistency (CMSC) encourages the synthesized images after translation to be segmented exactly the same as before translation. Comprehensive experimental results on cross-modality hip joint bone segmentation show the effectiveness of our proposed method, which achieves an average DICE of 03.91% on the acetabulum and 88.16% on the proximal femur, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. It is worth to note that without UDA, a model trained on CT for hip joint bone segmentation is non-transferable to MRI and has almost zero-DICE segmentation.

In this paper, we present a novel approach to segmenting images based on weak labels, called Points2Polygons. Our method uses adversarial networks to learn a context-based segmentation model that can accurately separate objects from their surroundings, even in cases where the object boundaries are not well-defined or there is significant background noise. Traditional image segmentation methods rely on hand-crafted features and heuristics, which often lead to suboptimal performance when dealing with complex scenes or low-quality data. Moreover, obtaining high-quality labels for training these models can be time-consuming and expensive. In contrast, our approach leverages recent advances in deep learning to learn a segments representation directly from the input data, without relying on manual feature engineering. The key insight behind Points2Polygons is to use adversarial training to learn a polygon-based representation of the image, where each polygon corresponds to a coherent region of the scene. This allows us to effectively capture object boundaries and handle irregularly shaped objects, while also propagating information across neighboring regions to produce more accurate segmentations. We evaluate Points2Polygons on several benchmark datasets, including PASCAL VOC and Cityscapes, comparing it against state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms. Our results show that our approach significantly outperforms traditional segmentation methods, especially in situations where the label quality is poor or there is significant contextual variation between training and test data. Overall, this work represents an important step towards developing robust and efficient image segmentation techniques that can operate effectively in real-world scenarios. The proposed method has broad applications in computer vision, robotics, medical imaging, and other domains where image understanding is critical.

This paper aims to explore the significance of image enhancement techniques in color image segmentation. The study presents a comprehensive analysis of different image enhancements methods, including smoothing, edge detection, intensity histogram equalization, contrast stretching, gamma correction, Gaussian filtering, median filtering, bilateral filtering, sharpening, blurring, and thresholding. The study examines their impact on the performance of various segmentation algorithms such as Otsu's Thresholding, k-Means Clustering, Watershed Transform, Simple Linear Iterative Clustering (SLIC), GrabCut, region growing, and active contour model. Conducting extensive experiments with a range of images that differ in size, color complexity, noise levels, and illumination conditions demonstrates the importance of selecting suitable pre-processing steps. The study finds that many segmentation models do not produce satisfactory results until an appropriate image enhancement technique is applied. Furthermore, it proposes a new approach which combines multiple enhancement methods to improve segmentation accuracy and robustness while reducing computational time. Overall, this research provides insights into the challenges facing segmentation systems and highlights the need for developing efficient and accurate techniques tailored towards specific applications, making these approaches more accessible to industry and researchers alike. Keywords: Image enhancement; color image segmentation; Otsu; SLIC; K-means clustering; grab cut; region growing, Active Contour Model

In this paper, we present CHASE, a novel approach to visual tracking that leverages the power of differentiable neural architecture search (NAS) to optimize the tracking performance. Unlike traditional tracking methods that rely on hand-crafted features and pre-defined architectures, CHASE uses a cell-level differentiable neural network to learn a robust and adaptive representation of the target object. The proposed method consists of two main components: a cell-level differentiable neural network, and a tracking loss function that is designed to optimize the tracking performance. The cell-level differentiable neural network is trained to learn a robust representation of the target object by optimizing a novel tracking loss function that encourages the network to produce a stable output in the presence of occlusions, illumination changes, and other challenges. The tracking loss function is designed to be differentiable with respect to the network's architecture, allowing us to use backpropagation to optimize the network's parameters. We use a combination of gradient descent and evolution strategies to search for the optimal architecture that maximizes the tracking performance. We evaluate CHASE on several challenging benchmarks, including the PASCAL Visual Object Tracking (VOT) dataset, the Temple-Color-Tracking (TCT) dataset, and the LaSalle-Color-Tracking (LCT) dataset. Our experiments show that CHASE outperforms several state-of-the-art tracking methods, including deep learning-based methods, and achieves a high success rate in various challenging scenarios. The main contribution of this paper is the introduction of a novel differentiable neural architecture search method for visual tracking, which allows the network to adapt to changing object appearance and learn a robust representation of the target object. The proposed method has important implications for a wide range of applications, including object tracking in videos, autonomous driving, and robotics.

In this work, we build a generic architecture of Convolutional Neural Networks to discover empirical properties of neural networks. Our first contribution is to introduce a state-of-the-art framework that depends upon few hyper parameters and to study the network when we vary them. It has no max pooling, no biases, only 13 layers, is purely convolutional and yields up to 95.4 and 79.6 accuracy respectively on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100. We show that the nonlinearity of a deep network does not need to be continuous, non expansive or point-wise, to achieve good performance. We show that increasing the width of our network permits being competitive with very deep networks. Our second contribution is an analysis of the contraction and separation properties of this network. Indeed, a 1-nearest neighbor classifier applied on deep features progressively improves with depth, which indicates that the representation is progressively more regular. Besides, we defined and analyzed local support vectors that separate classes locally. All our experiments are reproducible and code is available online, based on TensorFlow.

In this paper, we explore the concept of inductive types in homotopy type theory. We begin by providing an overview of type theory and its role in computer science, followed by a detailed explanation of inductive types and their significance in programming. We then delve into the specifics of inductive types in homotopy type theory, discussing their properties and how they can be used to represent complex data structures. Finally, we examine the potential applications of inductive types in homotopy type theory, including their use in programming languages and software development. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of inductive types in homotopy type theory and their potential impact on the field of computer science.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to medical image segmentation using a spatial guided self-supervised clustreing network (SGSCN). Our method leverages the inherent spatial structure in medical images to learn clustreing representations without the need for annotated data. The SGSCN model consists of a convolutional neural network (CNN) followed by a spatially-aware clustreing module. The CNN encodes the input image into a set of feature maps, which are then used to compute a spatial similarity graph. The spatially- aware clustreing module partitions the graph into distinct clustres, where each clustre corresponds to a specific class label. We evaluate our method on several publicly available medical imageing datasets, including MRI brain scans and CT lung scans. Experimental results show that SGSCN outperforms traditional supervised learning approaches, as well as state-of-the art self-supervised methods, in terms of segmentation accuracy. Furthermore, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in scenarios where annotations are limited or difficult to obtain. CGSCN has important implications for medical image analysis tasks, particularly in situations where annotated data is scarce or challenging to obtain. Our approach provides a robust and efficient way to segment medical images without relying on manual annotation effort. This can potentially accelerate the development of AI solutions for various medical applications, such as disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring.

Rome, Italy - In a move to preserve the ancient beauty of the Ponte Milvio bridge in Rome, thousands of love padlocks that have been placed on its structure over the past years are now being removed. The practice of locking a "love padlock" to the bridge has become popular among couples as a symbol of their undying love and commitment. However, authorities have recently realized that the sheer amount of these padlocks is causing damage to the bridge, which dates back to the 2nd century BC. Therefore, they have decided to take action by using bolt-cutters to remove all of them from the bridge. The mayor of Rome, Virginia Raggi, expressed her support for the initiative, saying: "We must protect our ancient heritage. The bridge has been standing for centuries, and it should continue to stand for centuries more. That's why we are taking the necessary steps to ensure that it remains strong and intact." The mayor also encouraged those who have placed love padlocks on the bridge to find other ways to express their love, such as by taking a romantic stroll along its length or writing messages of love on postcards. The removal of the love padlocks has sparked debates among local residents, with some arguing that it is an unnecessary measure while others celebrate the effort to protect the bridge. Regardless of the views, the city of Rome is now taking action to preserve one of its most beloved landmarks.

Image segmentation is a critical task in computer vision and machine learning that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions. Despite the success of recent deep learning methods, they often suffer from overfitting, which can lead to poor generalization performance. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach to image segmentation using weak shape priors. Our method incorporates shape information through a recently developed theory called hierarchical perceptual grouping (HPG), which captures statistical correlations among low-level features extracted from images. By training our model with HPG, we impose constraints on the shapes of objects within an image and effectively prevent overfitting. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art object detection and segmentation algorithms while achieving more accurate shape recognition. Overall, our work provides a new perspective on integrating weak shape priors into deep learning models and opens up avenues for future research in computer vision.

Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for cross-modality medical image segmentation has shown great progress by domain-invariant feature learning or image appearance translation. Adapted feature learning usually cannot detect domain shifts at the pixel level and is not able to achieve good results in dense semantic segmentation tasks. Image appearance translation, e.g. CycleGAN, translates images into different styles with good appearance, despite its population, its semantic consistency is hardly to maintain and results in poor cross-modality segmentation. In this paper, we propose intra- and cross-modality semantic consistency (ICMSC) for UDA and our key insight is that the segmentation of synthesised images in different styles should be consistent. Specifically, our model consists of an image translation module and a domain-specific segmentation module. The image translation module is a standard CycleGAN, while the segmentation module contains two domain-specific segmentation networks. The intra-modality semantic consistency (IMSC) forces the reconstructed image after a cycle to be segmented in the same way as the original input image, while the cross-modality semantic consistency (CMSC) encourages the synthesized images after translation to be segmented exactly the same as before translation. Comprehensive experimental results on cross-modality hip joint bone segmentation show the effectiveness of our proposed method, which achieves an average DICE of 81.61% on the acetabulum and 88.16% on the proximal femur, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. It is worth to note that without UDA, a model trained on CT for hip joint bone segmentation is non-transferable to MRI and has almost zero-DICE segmentation.

This academic paper explores the use of contextual information beyond image data for semantic segmentation. By analyzing various sources of contextual information, such as text, audio, and video, the paper demonstrates how these additional data sources can improve the accuracy and efficiency of semantic segmentation. Through a series of experiments and case studies, the paper provides evidence that mining contextual information beyond image data can lead to significant improvements in the performance of semantic segmentation models. Overall, this paper offers valuable insights for researchers and practitioners working in the field of computer vision and machine learning.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to medical image segmentation using spatial guided self-supervised clustering network (SG-SCN). The SG-SCN model combines strengths of self-supervised learning and spatial guidance to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation. Self-supervised learning has emerged as a promising approach to medical image segmentation, as it can learn useful features from unlabelled data. However, self-supervised learning methods often suffer from problem of trivial solutions, where model learns irrelevant or redundant features that do not generalize well to new data. Spatial guidance, which incorporates prior knowledge about spatial structure of data, has been shown to improve performance of self-supervised learning models. The SG-SCN model proposed in this paper combines self-supervised learning with spatial guidance to overcome the limitations of traditional self-supervised learning methods. The model consists of a spatial guidance module that incorporates prior knowledge about the spatial structure of data, and a self-supervised clustering module that learns to cluster the data into meaningful segments. The spatial guidance module is designed to provide the self-supervised clustering module with spatial information, such as location and size of organs or tissues, which helps the model to learn more accurate and meaningful features. We evaluate the performance of SG-SCN model on several publicly available medical image datasets, including brain MRI, lung CT, and liver CT. The results show that the SG-SCN model outperforms several state-of-the-art self-supervised learning methods, and achieves competitive performance compared to fully supervised models. The segmentation task, where a model outputs semantics-aware masks given an image input, has had tremendous success in recent years with new breakthroughs appearing every few months. For instance, fully labeled images are still extremely expensive to label manually and therefore very difficult to amass at sufficient depth required by deep learning models. Additionally, while fine labels such as per object masks allow models to extract the right objects themselves, there exist various levels of labeling that can be provided: e.g., a coarse label can provide mask labels only at the scene level (either global or foreground) without specific information about where certain objects can appear. We propose Lifting, a framework capable of mining any level of available labeling - fine or crude - to lift contextual knowledge within visual representations when performing semantic segmentation on unlabeled data. In our experiments, we use simple heuristic assumptions to effectively mine labeling of varying fidelity. The contributions that this work make include: • A novel technique (LIFTING), which leverages low quality supervision signals to generate meaningful high quality features used for semantic prediction. This demonstrates that even partial ground truth can help increase overall accuracy across all layers of a vision network; • Experimental results showing how LIFT combines the advantages of both weakly and strongly correlated datasets through transferability between datasets generated using different techniques. All training procedures run efficiently under parallel computing power and thus are practical. from https://thenewstack.io/image

> We propose a novel weakly supervised segmentation method that uses a geodesic distance between the extreme points of the ground truth and the predicted segmentation. The geodesic distance is computed using the Inter Extreme Points (IET) distance, which is a generalization of the Intersection over Union (IoU) metric. In this study, we propose a new validity index that can be used to assess the quality of clustering results in fuzzy set theory. We use possibilistic c-means (PCM) algorithm as an example and define several measures related to internal index (data compression ratio), external index (cluster stability), and global validity index using entropy measure based on uncertainty principle. The proposed invalidities are compared with two well-known clustering evaluation methods of silhouette analysis and Davies-Bouldin Index (DBI). Extensive simulation studies demonstrate the ability of our approach to identify the optimized number of clusters and reveal its outperformance over other evaluation methods. This work contributes significantly to the development of fuzzy clustering algorithms by providing a novel method to evaluate their performance.

This paper describes a novel method to image segmentation based on the histogram of depth (HOD) and its application in driver distraction prevention. Existing techniques for picture segmentation are typically restricted by their dependence on hand-crafted features or their ability to handle complex sequences with varying lighting conditions. In comparison, the HOD technique uses the depth information of the scene to compute a histogram of depth values, which can be applied to segment the picture into meaningful areas. The proposed technique is evaluated on a database of driving scenes and demonstrates improved efficiency compared to conventional image segmentation approaches. Also, the HOD technique is designed to identify vehicle distraction, which is a key task for maintaining road safety. The proposed method recognizes distraction events with low precision and outperforms existing approaches that depend on hand-crafted features or machine learning algorithms. The major contributions of this paper are: 1. A novel method to picture segmentation based on the histogram of depth, which can handle complex scenes with varying lighting conditions. 2. An application of the HOD technique in vehicle distraction prevention, which can enhance road safety by identifying distraction events with low precision. 3. An implementation of the proposed technique on a database of driving scenes, showing its efficiency compared to conventional photo segmentation approaches. Overall, this paper provides a novel and effective approach to image segmentation and its application in vehicle distraction prevention, which can contribute to the advancement of advanced vehicle assist systems (ADAS) and autonomous vehicle systems.

We then used these gaze patterns as input to a deep learning model, which was trained to predict the corresponding segmentation masks. The performance of our Gaze2Segment approach was evaluated against traditional image segmentation methods, and the results were compared using several metrics.
