In this paper, we present a novel approach for super-realtime facial landmark detection and shape fitting using deep regression of shape model parameters. Existing methods for facial landmark detection are often limited by their reliance on hand-crafted features, slow processing times, and lack of accuracy. Our proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to overcome these limitations, achieving state-of-the-art performance in real-time. We introduce a deep neural network architecture that directly regresses the parameters of a 3D shape model from raw image data. This allows for the simultaneous detection of facial landmarks and fitting of a 7D shape model, all in a single, efficient step. Our network is trained on a large dataset of images and uses a combination of convolutional and fully connected layers to learn the mapping between images and shape model parameters. We evaluate our method on several challenging datasets, including variations in pose, illumination, and expression. Our results show that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and speed. We achieve an average processing time of under 34 milliseconds per frame, making our method suitable for real-time applications such as virtual try-on, avatar creation, and facial animation. In addition, we demonstrate the versatility of our method by applying it to a variety of applications, including facial animation, avatar creation, and 3D face reconstruction. Our results show that our method can generate highly realistic and personalized avatars, as well as accurate 3D face reconstructions from a single RGB image. Overall, our paper makes a significant contribution to the field of facial landmark detection and shape fitting, and demonstrates the potential of deep learning for real-time computer vision applications.

The home secretary wrote to cabinet colleagues in December seeking approval to "reduce significantly" one type of stop and search, Newsnight has learned. Despite setting a 12 December deadline, the changes are yet to be announced. Downing Street said the prime minister accepted reforms needed to take place. However, officials have refused to say when any decisions might be taken. Critics say stop and search unfairly targets the black community. In November, the Equality and Human Rights Commission said that, overall, black people were six times more likely than white people to be stopped, with Asian or other ethnic minority groups two times more likely to be stopped. On 4 December, Home Secretary Theresa May wrote seeking approval from the cabinet's home affairs committee to a "package of measures." This included a plan to "amend section 60 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 so that the test for the power's use is'necessary' and'expedient', (to prevent incidents involving serious violence)." Under Section 60, police can stop and search someone for weapons in a designated area, for a specific time, without suspicion that the individual is involved in wrongdoing. However, a senior officer must hold a reasonable belief that violence has happened or may occur in the area. Mrs May told cabinet colleagues she intended to "raise the level of authorisation to a senior officer who must reasonably believe that violence'will' take place (as opposed to'may ." She continued: "I expect this to reduce significantly the number of stop and searches under section 60. Section 60 is only one kind of stop and search." One minister told Newsnight's chief correspondent Laura Kuenssberg that "we all want to get on" with the changes. But sources told her they feared "there's just a lack of will, a fear of looking soft on crime." The Liberal Democrats agree with the proposals and Labour has offered cross party talks to push the policy forward. Shadow home secretary Yvette Cooper said: "Instead of internal rows over this, Theresa May should accept our offer to work together to change stop and search." In this paper, we present a novel approach for image segmentation and anatomical landmarking Using deep geodesic learning. Our method leverages the concept of geodesics, which are curves that Traverse the image space and preserve the underlying structure of the data. By learning a deep Representation of the geodesics, we can effectively capture the spatial relationships between image pixels and enforce anatomical consistency in The segmentation process. We propose a two-stage framework that first learns a geodesic embedding of the Image data and then uses this embedding to perform segmentation and landmarking. In the first stage, we use a variational autoencoder to learn a probabilistic embedding of the geodesics, which captures the spatial and structural information of the data. In the second stage, we use a conditional random field to refine the segmentation and landmarking, where the Geodesic embedding serves As The conditioning variable. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets, including brain MRI and CT scans, and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that deep geodesic learning can accurately segment complex anatomical structures and identify subtle patterns that are not easily captured by traditional image segmentation techniques. Our work has important implications for a wide range of Medical imaging applications, including disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and image-guided interventions. By providing a more accurate and robust approach to image segmentation And landmarking, we can improve The accuracy and efficiency of these applications, ultimately leading To better patient outcomes.

The English alphabet is derived from the Latin alphabet, which in turn was derived from the Greek alphabet. The letter U in the Latin alphabet was derived from the Greek letter (upsilon), which was derived from the Phoenician letter Waw. The letter Q in the Latin alphabet was derived from the Greek letter (kappa), which was derived from the Phoenician letter Qoph. In the early days of the Latin alphabet, there was no distinction between the letters U and V, which were both represented by the letter V. Over time, the shapes of the letters U and V began to diverge, and by the Middle Ages, they had become distinct letters. However, the order of the letters in the alphabet remained the same, with U coming after T and before V.

In this paper, we propose a new method for estimating parameters in spatial point processes using quasi-likelihood. Spatial point processes are widely used to model events that occur at specific locations in space and time, such as earthquakes, disease outbreaks, and crime incidents. Accurate estimation of the parameters of these models is crucial for understanding the underlying mechanisms and making predictions about future events. Traditional methods for parameter estimation in spatial point processes rely on likelihood functions, which can be computationally intensive and may not be well-suited for complex models or large datasets. Quasi-likelihood methods offer a more efficient alternative by approximating the likelihood function with a simpler function that captures the essential features of the data. The proposed quasi-likelihood method for spatial point processes is based on a novel combination of spatial smoothing techniques and non-parametric approximation of the score function. The resulting estimate is consistent and asymptotically normal under mild regularity conditions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through simulation studies and application to real-world datasets. In comparsion to existing methods, our quasi-likelihood approach offers several advantages. Firstly, it allows for faster and more reliable estimation of parameters compared to traditional maximum likelihood methods. Secondly, it provides a flexible framework for modeling complex dependencies between observations without requiring explicit specification of the connection structure. Finally, it enables quantification of uncertainty in the estimates through bootstrapping and Bayesian inference. Overall, this paper introduces an innovative approach to parameter estimation in spatial point processes that combines the strengths of quasi-likelihood methods with the unique characteristics of spatial data. Our findings have important implications for various fields where spatiotemporal data is prevalent, including epidemiology, geostatistics, environmental science, and criminal justice research.

The onset of anesthesia-induced loss of consciousness is a complex process that involves the disruption of brain networks. In this study, we investigated the structure and dynamics of brain lobe's functional networks at the onset of anesthesia-induced loss of consciousness. We used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to measure brain activity in healthy volunteers during the onset of anesthesia-induced loss of consciousness. We then analyzed the functional connectivity between different brain regions using a network analysis approach. Our results showed that the onset of anesthesia-induced loss of consciousness was associated with a decrease in functional connectivity between different brain regions. Specifically, we found that the connectivity between the default mode network (DMN) and the sensory processing network (SPN) decreased significantly during the onset of anesthesia-induced loss of consciousness. We also found that the connectivity between the DMN and the motor network (MN) decreased significantly during the onset of anesthesia-induced loss of consciousness. These findings suggest that the disruption of functional connectivity between different brain networks is a key mechanism underlying the onset of anesthesia-induced loss of consciousness.

The "bag-of-frames" approach, which is based on analyzing individual audio frames of an urban soundscape in isolation, has been widely used to study urban noise pollution. However, this approach Has several limitations that limit its usefulness for fully capturing the complex and dynamic nature of urban soundscapes. Specifically, It does not consider relationships between nearby sound sources or temporal patterns of sound over time, both of which are important Factors for understanding and mitigating noise pollution in cities. To Address these shortcomings, alternative approaches such As spectral analysis, source location methods, and temporal segmentation techniques can be used instead. These Approaches provide more comprehensive information about the spatial and temporal characteristics of urban soundscapes and offer better tools for addressing noise reduction strategies in densely populated areas.

> Medical image segmentation is a fundamental task in medical image analysis. It is a challenging task due to the large variability of the anatomical structures and the limited amount of training data. In this paper, we propose a novel self-supervised clustering network for medical image segmentation. The proposed network is composed of two main components: a spatial guided self-supervised clustering module and a segmentation module. The spatial guided self-supervised clustering module is designed to learn the spatial information of the input image and generate pseudo labels for the unlabeled data. The segmentation module is designed to learn the segmentation task with the generated pseudo labels. The proposed network is trained in a self-supervised manner, which does not require any manual annotations. The experimental results on the public datasets demonstrate that the proposed network achieves state-of-the-art performance in medical image segmentation. I'm presenting TorusNET, an new toolkit in the vein of U-Net and LIGNEAT: TorusNET provides a high-level architectural model combining several types of networks: TorusNetwork : A network consisting entirely of trees on the grid; this is used to train models that are trained by simply using the number of nodes of such network as input (e.g., "training with nodes and 4 features and train to see if there's anything not working"). The tree structure implies direct scaling of the network size so that it doesn't matter how efficient (in terms of number of neurons) each feature may be. Trainsenvornet : A network composed of both trees and regular grids; this network can be fed images which are segmented into pixels through standard training or supervised classification procedures (it consists only of image segments). It trains faster than the other type becuase it has more weights attached towards higher dimensionality of data and thus allows the weight calculations to be optimized without sacrificing performance (e.g., by finding better connections between sparse elements). Unfortunately, the tree structure makes use of special ways to describe weights, hence prehearing of these features will need extra effort on the part of the user. There is also much less memory usage of trainees. Training also uses an effective way of determining what types of images we might expect, based on their content/information and context. Finally, it is possible to add some preprocessing on top at runtime—for example, an audio layer or image segmenting. EnveloperNetwork : Similer in concept but different overall design. It consists of two seperate systems with small variations in each component. One system contains nodes for encoding the objects and components, and another provides a simple binary representation of the encoded object and its component information. Semantic segmentation is a critical task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image based on its semantic meaning. While recent advances in deep learning have led to significant improvements in image-based semantic segmentation, there are still challenges in accurately segmenting objects in complex scenes with ambiguous or occluded regions. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to mining contextual information beyond image for semantic segmentation. Our approach leverages additional contextual information such as textual descriptions, 3D models, and user feedback to enhance the accuracy of semantic segmentation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on several benchmark datasets and show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art image-based semantic segmentation methods. Our work paves the way for more accurate and robust semantic segmentation in complex scenes.

Confessions had been forced from the Muslim men after they were beaten up in custody, a rights activist said. They were among a group of people arrested late last year. Homosexual acts are illegal in the West African state under both Islamic and secular law - the latter was tightened earlier this year. Same-sex marriages, gay groups and shows of same-sex public affection are now banned throughout Nigeria. Another Muslim man also received 20 lashes in January after the Islamic court in Bauchi convicted him of homosexual offences. Most states in the predominantly Muslim north of Nigeria have adopted Islamic law, known as Sharia, since the end of military rule in 1999. The BBC's Ishaq Khalid in Bauchi says details about the latest case are sketchy, but court officials have confirmed the whippings. It seems the court wanted to avoid publicity after an angry crowd disrupted proceedings last month, demanding the death sentence for the four, our reporter says. The judge did not impose the death penalty because the homosexual offences had taken place a long time ago, and the men had repented, he says. Where is it illegal to be gay? The men, aged between 20 and 22, were also ordered to pay a fine of 120 (PS70) each, Dorothy Aken'Ova, a rights activist with the Nigeria-based International Centre for Reproductive Health and Sexual Rights, told the Associated Press news agency. Rights groups were trying to raise the money - otherwise, they will remain in prison, she said. The men should not have been convicted because they were beaten up and their confessions forced, she said. Their families, mainly subsistence farmers, turned down an offer of legal representation because they preferred to negotiate with the judge and get the case behind them, Ms Aken'Ova said. Nigeria is a deeply conservative country, where most people - Christian and Muslim - are opposed to homosexuality.

Spotify has bought The Ringer, a podcast-centric media company owned by Bill Simmons. Simmons and his employees will all be absorbed in the deal. The Ringer has around 30 titles, ranging from an NBA chat show to a show devoted to rewatching old movies. Neither company disclosed a sale price for the deal, which is expected to close in the first quarter of this year. Spotify did not make Gimlet Media's podcasts exclusive to its platform when it purchased the company last year, so The Ringer's podcasts should still be available on all platforms. This is the fourth podcast company Spotify has acquired in the last 12 months.

Suicide substrates have been employed to uncover characteristics of the homology-dependent stages in the process of integrative recombination of bacteriophage lambda. The "suicide probes" or "suicide substrates" are altered forms of the typical DNA substrates used in recombination reactions. These are engineered in a way that initiates recombination, but cannot finish it. This is often caused by chemical alterations that render them susceptible to being broken down by restriction enzymes or other nucleases. Researchers have used suicide substrates in experiments involving the bacteriophage lambda system to better understand the molecular aspects of homology-dependent stages of recombination. These stages include the need for similar DNA sequences, the importance of protein-protein interactions, and the specifics of strand exchange. Experiments that utilize suicide substrates have demonstrated that the lambda integrase protein plays a crucial role in initiating the pairing of homologous DNA sequences, and a DNA annealing activity that is dependent on homology is necessary for successful occurrence of the recombination process. The process also involves the critical participation of other proteins including lambda Xis protein and host integration host factor (IHF), as shown by these studies. To put it briefly, the use of suicide substrates has been beneficial in delving into the complex molecular aspects of integrative recombination in bacteriophage lambda with a focus on homology-dependent stages. This has resulted in an improved comprehension of the key biological processes involved.

Title: Rethinking BiSeNet For Real-time Semantic Segmentation Abstract: The recent advancements in deep learning methods have led to significant improvements in computer vision technology, including semantic segmentation. While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are being increasingly used for real-time image processing applications such as autonomous vehicles and medical imaging systems, they face several challenges such as computational efficiency and real-time processing requirements. To address these issues, a bi-stream CNN architecture called Binary Stream Convolutional Network (BiSeNet) was introduced to improve accuracy while reducing computational complexity for semantic segmentation tasks. In this work, we revisit BiSeNet's design and propose modifications that can further optimize its performance without significantly sacrificing precision or speed. Our proposed design utilizes techniques like depthwise separable convolutions and skip connections to enable faster prediction with high accuracy for diverse datasets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed improvement on challenging datasets such as COCO and AUC-VOC, achieving comparable results to state-of-the-art models with lower memory usage and computation time. Overall, our contributions highlight the importance of efficient architectures for real-world applications and provide practical recommendations for future research studies.

This paper presents a comprehensive modeling and control study of an active constrained layer (ACL) beam subject to two voltage sources, with and without consideration of magnetic effects. The ACL beam is a type of smart structure that utilizes piezoelectric materials to introduce intelligence and adaptability in structural systems. It consists of a constraint layer sandwiched between two piezoelectric layers, which are excited by voltage sources. By modeling the electromechanical behavior of the ACL beam using a combination of theoretical and numerical methods, we investigate the effectiveness of different control strategies in regulating its vibration response. We also examine the influence of magnetic effects on the behavior of the system, particularly when operating in a high-frequency regime. Our results demonstrate the ability to accurately predict and manipulate the behavior of the ACL beam under various conditions, including the presence of magnetic fields, and highlight the potential advantages of incorporating magnetic effects into the control strategy. These findings hold significant implications for the design and operation of intelligent structures, such as those used in vibrations isolation, energy harvesting, and nanopositioning applications.

This paper presents Separable Convolutional LSTM (SCLVM), a novel model that employs convolutional layers to improve the processing speed of traditional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks in video segmentation tasks. The proposed model is based on separable neural network architectures that split philtres into smaller, spatially separate components and multiply them with learnable weights. By exploiting the reparametrisation trick, SCLVM significantly reduces both computational complexity and memory usage by performing weighted elementwise operations between input data and small kernels instead of large matrices. Furthermore, this study shows that the use of 1D convolution operation allows SCLVM to handle dense sequential information inherent in LSTM while maintaining superior performance. Empirical results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of efficiency and achieves comparable accuracy in various video segmentation benchmarks.

In this paper, we propose a semiparametric extension of the stochastic block model (SBM) for longitudinal networks, which are networks that evolve over time. The SBM is a popular model for network data, but it assumes that the network structure is fixed over time, which can be a limitation when analyzing longitudinal data. Our proposed model, called the semiparametric longitudinal stochastic block model (SLSBM), allows for time-varying network structures while still incorporating the clustering and community structure captured by the traditional SBM. The SLSBM model is based on a parametric model for the probability of a tie between two nodes at a given time, which allows for time-varying edge probabilities. We also introduce a semiparametric component to the model, which allows for the estimation of time-varying network effects that are not captured by the parametric component. This allows for greater flexibility in modeling complex network dynamics. We propose an estimation method for the SLSBM using a combination of maximum likelihood estimation and Bayesian inference. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of the model through simulations and applications to real-world longitudinal network data. Our results show that the SLSBM outperforms traditional SBMs in terms of model fit and predictive accuracy, and is able to capture time-varying community structures and network effects that are not captured by traditional models. Overall, the SLSBM provides a powerful tool for analyzing longitudinal network data, and can be used to study a wide range of phenomena, such as social networks, communication networks, and economic networks. The model's ability to capture time-varying network effects and community structures makes it particularly useful for understanding dynamic network processes and predicting future network behavior.

This paper proposes a novel hierarchical random walk (HRW) segmentation model to handle large-scale biomedical image Analysis. The HRW method uses a combination of adaptive Thresholding and conditional density functions, resulting in an efficient and accurate unsupervised classification technique. By incorporating hierarchical processing into the system, it identifies significant features that are representative of smaller sections of images. Furthermore, this technique Improves the accuracy of volumetric data by eliminating artifacts caused by differences in contrast between regions or voxel intensities. In this study, we applied the proposed HRW algorithm on two Public domain datasets: Alzheimer's Disease magnetic resonance imaging volume and T1-weighted contrast-enhanced breast Cancer MRI volumes. we demonstrated that the HRW approach can accurately detect abnormal structures as compared to other state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, our algorithm outperformed traditional methods Like level set thresholding in terms of robustness against noise and tissue variability while achieving similar computational performance. Overall, our results Provide clear evidence that hierarchical random walk segmentation is a valuable tool for biomedical image analysis. It offers improved robustness, accuracy, and efficiency in handling larger volumetric images with complex structural features, making it ideal for applications such as tumor detection, volume estimation, and morphological analysis.

Microvascular decompression (MVD) is a surgical procedure used to treat hemifacial spasm, a condition characterized by involuntary muscle contractions on one side of the face. While MVD is generally an effective treatment for hemifacial spasm, there are potential risks and complications associated with the procedure, including hearing loss. Hearing loss, particularly high-frequency hearing loss, is a possible complication after MVD surgery. The reported incidence of postoperative hearing loss varies widely across different studies, ranging from 0 to 46. High-frequency hearing loss occurs when a patient has difficulty hearing sounds at higher frequencies, typically above 2000 Hz. It is important to note that the risk of hearing loss after MVD is generally considered to be low. Several factors can influence the risk of hearing loss after MVD, including the surgical technique, the surgeon's experience, and the patient's individual anatomy. Preservation of hearing function is usually a priority during MVD surgery, and surgeons take various measures to minimize the risk of hearing loss, such as using intraoperative monitoring of auditory function and gentle microsurgical techniques to protect the facial and cochlear nerves, which are responsible for facial movements and hearing, respectively. Despite the risk of high-frequency hearing loss after MVD, the procedure is generally considered safe and effective for treating hemifacial spasm, resolving symptoms in the majority of patients. Patients considering MVD should discuss the potential risks and benefits of the surgery with their healthcare team to make an informed decision about treatment.

This paper investigates the elastic properties of mono- and polydisperse two-dimensional crystals of hard--core repulsive Yukawa particles. The study utilizes molecular dynamics simulations to analyze these systems under compressional strain, shear strain, and bending strain conditions. Results show that monolayers exhibit isotropic behavior in all directions, while multilayer structures display anisotropy due to interlayer correlation effects. Intriguingly, the presence of disorder promotes plastic deformation through dislocation formation in a threshold manner. These findings have implications for understanding the mechanical behavior of soft matter materials in confinement and the potential applications of such systems as actuators and sensors.

This paper presents a survey of data mining methods for social media analysis. Due to the tremendous increase in the use of social media and the increasing number of data, there is a need to develop efficient methods for mining these data, including clustering, classification, association rule mining, and anomaly detection. This paper also discusses the challenges and difficulties associated with the use of social media data, such as the protection of privacy and the need for real-time analysis, and concludes with research trends and opportunities in social media data mining.

Soft and rigid collars can both provide restriction in the cervical range of motion; however, they serve different purposes and offer varying degrees of restriction. Rigid collars generally provide more significant motion restriction than soft collars. Soft collars are usually used for less severe injuries or for a short period, such as during the initial phase of injury recovery. They may provide some support, comfort, and pain relief, but they do not offer the same extent of motion restriction that rigid collars do. Rigid collars, on the other hand, are designed to provide more robust immobilization of the cervical spine. They are commonly used for more severe injuries or post-surgery recovery, where greater restriction in motion is necessary to allow proper healing. During the fifteen activities of daily living, soft and rigid collars will provide some limitation in cervical range of motion, but rigid collars will generally offer a greater degree of restriction. The specific level of restriction will vary depending on the type and design of each collar, and the specific activities being performed. However, it's important to note that rigid collars may be less comfortable to wear for extended periods and may interfere more with daily activities compared to soft collars. In conclusion, both soft and rigid collars can provide cervical motion restriction during activities of daily living, but rigid collars typically offer a higher degree of immobilization than soft collars. The choice between the two should be based on the severity of the injury, the required level of restriction, and the comfort and compatibility with the patient's needs.

This journal proposes a new approach to structured learning of tree potentials in Conditional Random Field (CRF) models for image segmentation. The proposed approach provides an optimal algorithm that quickly learns the values needed for accurate tree potential computation, which is useful for improving the efficiency of CRF models in this task. The technique requires a mix of regularization techniques and randomization methods to provide efficient tree size selection during training. Results show that the proposed approach greatly outperforms existing techniques, improving state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmark datasets for image segmentation. Overall, our work provides a viable avenue for increasing the reliability and reliability of CRF models for image segmentation by structuring the learning process of tree potentials.

> By combining degree-four sum-of-square relaxations and linear systems, Yi (2016) gave algorithms that solve exact constraint satisfaction and max-cut problems on dense 2D grids within polynomial time. We improve these exponential-time techniques by extending them to exact semidefinite programming over grid graphs with larger constant factors. For k-coloring, we give an algorithm running in O\left({n^5}\right)\exp{\left({\mathrm{poly}(k)}\right)}+\exp{\left(O\left(\sqrt{\log n}/n^{3/8} \right) \right)}$ where n\in N is the number of nodes in our model with edge density bounded away from one. This improvement extends the approach of Chlamtac et al.\cite{chitnis2013}. Previously, such improvements have been proven only for graph classes with stronger structural properties or were given only heuristic implementations without specific guarantees on their approximation ratio. We further study how the results extend to other combinatorial max cut settings as well as extensions involving quadratic modular constraints and unweighted constraints arising out of multicommodity flow network cuts which are closely related to knapsack inequalities. We also discuss practical implementation details of this algorithm for graph coloring problems including optimizations through the use of block encoding and the efficient computation of semi-definiteness conditions using randomized techniques like ROT. Combined together with various reduction rules, our practical implementation runs in under the same runtime, often producing high quality solutions when the problem does not have unique optimal solution and can therefore be extended even beyond exact solving.

The conventional approach to real-time semantic segmentation has been focused on designing lightweight architectures with reduced complexity. However, recent studies have shown that exploiting spatial and channel dependencies can result in improved accuracy without significant increases in computational cost. This study proposes a novel revision of Bilateral Spatial Pyramid Pooling (BiSeNet) architecture by incorporating dual path refinements along both horizontal and vertical directions through dense connections, thereby enhancing feature extraction capabilities at multiple scales. Extensive experiments were conducted using CAMVID, Cityscapes, and COCO datasets which demonstrated superior performance when compared to state-of-the-art models while maintaining competitive inference times. The proposed model achieves an impressive tradeoff between accuracy and speed making it suitable for various applications such as autonomous driving or robotics where real-time processing is essential. Overall, this work provides new insights into network design strategies for efficient yet accurate semantic segmentation tasks.

In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning-based object detection method for efficient clustering initialization. Clustering is a fundamental problem in machine learning that involves grouping similar objects together, and its efficiency heavily relies on the quality of the initial cluster assignments. Traditional clustering methods rely on hand-crafted features and heuristics, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. In contrast, deep learning-based methods can learn rich representations of data and have shown promising results in various applications. Our proposed method leverages a state-of-the-art object detection algorithm to initialize clusters, which we term as Deep Clustering Initialization (DCI). DCI consists of two stages: (1) object proposal generation, and (4) cluster assignment. In the first stage, we use a deep learning-based object proposal generation algorithm to generate a set of high-quality object proposals that capture the spatial and semantic information of the input data. In the second stage, we design a novel cluster assignment algorithm that groups the object proposals into clusters based on their similarity. We evaluate the effectiveness of DCI using several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art clustering methods. Our results show that DCI achieves better clustering performance than traditional methods, including K-means and hierarchical clustering, while also providing more interpretable cluster assignments. We also demonstrate the versatility of DCI by applying it to various computer vision tasks, such as image segmentation and object tracking. Our main contributions can be summarized as follows: * We propose a novel deep learning-based method for efficient clustering initialization, which leverages object detection algorithms to generate high-quality cluster seeds. * We design a novel cluster assignment algorithm that groups object proposals into clusters based on their similarity, leading to better clustering performance and interpretability. * We demonstrate the effectiveness and versatility of our method on various benchmark datasets and computer vision tasks. Overall, our work has important implications for a wide range of applications that rely on clustering, such as image and video analysis, data mining, and machine learning.

This study presents TransClaw U-Net, a novel deep learning architecture that combines the strengths of both transformers and U-Nets for medical image segmentation. The proposed model utilises transformer blocks to capture long-range dependencies in the input data while maintaining the traditional convolutional structure of a U-Net to extract local features. Through extensive experiments on two public datasets, we demonstrate the superior performance of TransClaw U-Net compared to state-of-the-art methods, achieving accurate segmentations with fewer parametres and computations. Overall, this work provides a promising solution for efficient and accurate medical image segmentation using transformer models.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance in many different 2D medical image analysis tasks. In clinical practice, however, a large part of the medical imaging data available is in 3D. This has motivated the development of 3D CNNs for volumetric image segmentation in order to benefit from more spatial context. Due to GPU memory restrictions caused by moving to fully 3D, state-of-the-art methods depend on subvolume/patch processing and the size of the input patch is usually small, limiting the incorporation of larger context information for a better performance. In this paper, we propose a novel Holistic Decomposition Convolution (HDC), for an effective and efficient semantic segmentation of volumetric images. HDC consists of a periodic down-shuffling operation followed by a conventional 3D convolution. HDC has the advantage of significantly reducing the size of the data for sub-sequential processing while using all the information available in the input irrespective of the down-shuffling factors. Results obtained from comprehensive experiments conducted on hip T1 MR images and intervertebral disc T2 MR images demonstrate the efficacy of the present approach.

There has recently been great progress in automatic segmentation of medical images with deep learning algorithms. In most works observer variation is acknowledged to be a problem as it makes training data heterogeneous but so far no attempts have been made to explicitly capture this variation. Here, we propose an approach capable of mimicking different styles of segmentation, which potentially can improve quality and clinical acceptance of automatic segmentation methods. In this work, instead of training one neural network on all available data, we train several neural networks on subgroups of data belonging to different segmentation variations separately. Because a priori it may be unclear what styles of segmentation exist in the data and because different styles do not necessarily map one-on-one to different observers, the subgroups should be automatically determined. We achieve this by searching for the best data partition with a genetic algorithm. Therefore, each network can learn a specific style of segmentation from grouped training data. We provide proof of principle results for open-sourced prostate segmentation MRI data with simulated observer variations. Our approach provides an improvement of up to 23% (depending on simulated variations) in terms of Dice and surface Dice coefficients compared to one network trained on all data.

This paper presents a network-agnostic knowledge transfer approach for medical image segmentation. The proposed method enables the transfer of knowledge learned from one network architecture to another, without requiring access to The source network's parameters or architecture. This is achieved through the use of a feature extraction module, which is trained to extract Features from the input image that are relevant to the segmentation task. These features Are then used to guide the training of a target network, which is initialized with the weights of the source network. Experimental results on two medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness Of the proposed Method, achieving state-of-the-art performance with significantly reduced training time and computational resources.

Each time the explorers and viewers anticipate discovering a new and remarkable world, the filmmakers inexplicably divert their attention with contrived emergencies or false alarms, preventing them from doing so. This often causes a disruption to the feeling of amazement and involvement that could have been accomplished. Despite the frustrating narrative choice, the movie's impressive visuals succeed in creating a feeling of immense wonder and admiration for the unexplored regions. The lead actors deliver emotionally-charged scenes that make us invested in their well-being despite the chaotic explorations occurring around them, resulting in solid performances. The soundtrack is a skillfully designed complement to the visuals, frequently adding the emotional impact that the strained tension lacks. It expertly matches the challenges experienced by the characters by gracefully alternating between ambition, tension, and melancholy. Regrettably, the distractions mentioned earlier produce an artificial feeling of drama, which actually harms the movie by overshadowing the impressive efforts of the cast, the visual team, and the score. It's hard not to wish for a more subtle method of storytelling that keeps the audience interested without using gimmicks. To sum up, while this movie has some moments of brilliance, its lack of ability to sustain actual tension ultimately brings it down. Although it is praiseworthy in other aspects, the frequent use of false alarms and distractions creates a significant disconnection from the plot and characters which reduces the possibility of an extraordinary experience.

BoxNet: Deep Learning Based Biomedical Image Segmentation Using Boxes Only Annotation Accurate segmentation of biomedical images is crucial for various medical applications, including disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring. Deep learning techniques have shown promising results in image segmentation tasks, especially with the availability of large annotated datasets. However, annotating medical images is a time-consuming and expensive process, and obtaining high-quality annotations is challenging. In this paper, we propose BoxNet, a deep learning model for biomedical image segmentation that utilizes boxes only annotation. BoxNet is designed to learn from bounding boxes that surround the objects of interest, rather than pixel-level annotations. We employ a novel loss function that combines the advantages of both pixel-level and box-level annotations, enabling the model to learn from limited annotations. Our experiments on several publicly available biomedical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of BoxNet in segmenting various organs and tissues. Compared to state-of-the-art segmentation methods, BoxNet achieves competitive performance with significantly less annotation effort. We also show that BoxNet can adapt to different annotation styles and outperform fully supervised models when only a limited number of annotations are available. The main contributions of this paper are: 5. BoxNet, a deep learning model for biomedical image segmentation using boxes only annotation. 2. A novel loss function that combines the advantages of pixel-level and box-level annotations. 3. Experimental validation of BoxNet on several publicly available biomedical image datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability to different annotation styles. BoxNet has the potential to significantly reduce the annotation effort required for biomedical image segmentation, making it a valuable tool for medical image analysis tasks.

The projection from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) shows a far-reaching shift in the balance of graduate numbers, with the rising Asian economies accelerating ahead of the United States and western Europe. The forecasts for the shape of the "global talent pool" in 2020 show China as rapidly expanding its graduate numbers - set to account for 29 of the world's graduates aged between 25 and 34. The biggest faller is going to be the United States - down to 11 - and for the first time pushed into third place, behind India. The US and the countries of the European Union combined are expected to account for little more than a quarter of young graduates. Russia is also set to decline - its share of the world's graduates almost falling by half since the beginning of the century. Indonesia, according to the OECD's projections, will rise into fifth place. Is this an end-of-empire moment? Higher education has become the mirror and magnifier of economic performance - and in the post-World-War-II era, universities in the US, western Europe, Japan and Russia have dominated. The US in particular has been the university superpower - in wealth, influence and until recently in raw numbers. Up until 2000, the US still had a share of young graduates similar to China. And Japan had as big a proportion of young graduates as India. Now China and India are the biggest players. Their rise in graduate numbers reflects their changing ambitions - wanting to compete against advanced economies for high-skill, high-income employment. Instead of offering low-cost manufacture, they are targeting the hi-tech professional jobs that have become the preserve of the Westernised middle classes. As the OECD figures show, this is not simply a case of countries such as China expanding while others stand still. Across the industrialised world, graduate numbers are increasing - just not as quickly as China, where they have risen fivefold in a decade. The OECD notes that by 2020, China's young graduate population will be about the same as the total US population between the ages of 25 and 64. This changing world map will see Brazil having a bigger share of graduates than Germany, Turkey more than Spain, Indonesia three times more than France. > A conditional random field (CRF) has been widely used to deal with labeling problems. Given an image dataset, each training data consists a segmented map as the ground truth, along with the corresponding original image and labeled map that are obtained by some unsupervised methods such as normalized cuts or watershed transformation. In this work we design the local potentials in a structured output framework of CRM-influenced tree Boltzmann machine. Our approach is efficient because it only needs scaled matrix multiplication rather than full matrix inversion. Besides, one additional weight constraint makes our method feasible to be trained under gradient based backpropagation algorithm. It offers flexibility to optimize different objective functions. We also show that incorporating regularization loss term helps improving accuracy at a small cost of speed. Experimental results demonstrate the proposed model successfully models tree probability distributions.

Bordered Floer homology is a powerful tool for exploring the geometry of manifolds with boundary. In this paper, we introduce a new method to computing bordered Floer homology for manifolds with torus boundary using immersed curves. Our approach builds on recent work in the field and gives a new insight on the relation between bordered Floer homology and other invariants of 3-manifolds. We prove many important findings and establish the validity of our method through a series of examples. Overall, our paper creates a useful new tool for exploring the geometry of 3-manifolds with torus boundary.

The Hierarchical Continuously Monitored Bouchard (Cont-Bouchaud) Model is a novel approach that provides an enhanced understanding of financial markets by incorporating information flow and investor sentiment into asset pricing. This hierarchical framework allows analysts to measure risk at multiple levels, from individual assets to entire portfolios, providing greater flexibility in modeling complex investment strategies. By utilizing continuous monitoring techniques, this model can better capture market dynamics while also accounting for behavioral biases such as overconfidence and herding behavior. Overall, the use of hierarchies within the context of behavioural finance offers great potential towards improving our comprehension of speculative bubbles formation as well as portfolio optimization issues in dynamic environments with limited attention and informational processing capacity.

Recent years have seen tremendous progress in still-image segmentation; however the na\"ive application of these state-of-the-art algorithms to every video frame requires considerable computation and ignores the temporal continuity inherent in video. We propose a video recognition framework that relies on two key observations: 1) while pixels may change rapidly from frame to frame, the semantic content of a scene evolves more slowly, and 2) execution can be viewed as an aspect of architecture, yielding purpose-fit computation schedules for networks. We define a novel family of "clockwork" convnets driven by fixed or adaptive clock signals that schedule the processing of different layers at different update rates according to their semantic stability. We design a pipeline schedule to reduce latency for real-time recognition and a fixed-rate schedule to reduce overall computation. Finally, we extend clockwork scheduling to adaptive video processing by incorporating data-driven clocks that can be tuned on unlabeled video. The accuracy and efficiency of clockwork convnets are evaluated on the Youtube-Objects, NYUD, and Cityscapes video datasets.

I had always been wary of the gypsy camp on the edge of town, but I never expected to cross paths with the gypsies in a way that would bring their wrath down on me. It started when I was walking through the market and spotted an old gypsy woman selling herbs and potions. She caught my eye - perhaps because of her striking blue eyes - and I stopped to look at her wares. Unfortunately, I wasn't paying attention to where I was going and bumped into her table, spilling some of her potions. I apologized profusely, but it didn't seem to make an impression on her. In fact, she seemed to get angrier with each passing second, until finally she screamed a curse at me in a language I didn't understand. At first, I thought it was just an empty threat. But then strange things started happening. Everywhere I went, the old gypsy woman seemed to be following me, muttering more curses and pointing her finger at me as if she were casting spells. My life quickly became a living nightmare. I couldn't go anywhere without feeling like I was being watched, and I was constantly worried about what kind of ridiculous curse the gypsy had put on me. I tried to get away from her, but no matter how hard I tried, she kept finding me. Finally, I decided to take matters into my own hands. I found an old book of magical recipes and spent hours studying it, trying to find a way to break the gypsy's curse. After much trial and error, I eventually figured out a spell that would lift the curse - and it worked! The gypsy woman disappeared from my life, never to be heard from again. While I was glad to be free of her curses, I can't help but feel a bit of sadness when I think back to that day. Because even though she brought a lot of misery into my life, I can't help but admire the power of her magic.

A new way to solve non linear segmentations. It can be used as an additional tool with different methods for general classification [1]. There is no doubt that we are in dire need of better ways of handling the problem where deep learning and regression problems do not fit our requirements, which are highly complicated segmentation task tasks such as feature extraction or object recognition. The current data processing models implemented in standard distributed algorithms are not suited well enough for these problems. A good example for simple and parallel application was shown by Gao et al., who applied convolutional networks and DNNs respectively on a 2D dataset. We present here an alternative solution by introducing the new concept of inter-extremity geoderricks (IER): a set of georeferenced geodesic line representations. These are not strictly convex line representations but they approximate this condition for a subset of points along a curve whose edge passes through no part of a point (i.e. their segment). Erecting a set that fits all points as per feature extraction and object detection schemes (based on local minima) can reduce the number and distance search distance by about 10 times, thereby dramatically reducing computation time and memory requirement (and improving accuracy), due largely to better preprocessing step. Our work further focuses on modeling inter-point constraints to determine the location of a set of subgroups defined at many scales, i.e. all parts or edge points. This approach could become useful when performing sparse feature selection and multi-object localization tasks. [1] http://arxiv.org/abs/1706.02211

The paper "A Thorough View of Exact Inference in Graphs from the Degree-4 Sum-of-Squares Hierarchy" presents comprehensive analysis of exact inference in graphs using degree-4 sum-of-squares (SOS) hierarchy. This work builds upon previous research that established SOS hierarchy as powerful tool for solving graphical models, and provides a thorough understanding of its capabilities and limitations. The authors demonstrate that the degree-4 SOS hierarchy can be used to perform exact inference in various classes of graphs, including bounded-degree graphs, planar graphs, andgraphs with excluded minors. They provide explicit bounds on the computational complexity of exact inference using the SOS hierarchy for these classes of graphs, and show that it can be performed in polynomial time for many interesting cases. The paper also explores connections between SOS hierarchy and other approaches to exact inference, such as belief propagation and linear programming relaxations. The authors show that SOS hierarchy can be seen as alternate formulation of these methods, providing new insights into their strengths and weaknesses. Finally, the authors investigate relationship between the SOS hierarchy and the statistical properties of graphs. They prove lower bounds on the size of smallest witnesses required by the SOS hierarchy to refute independence claims in certain families of graphs, and provide evidence for the conjecture that SOS hierarchy is optimal for testing independence in some regimes. Overall, this work provides a thorough view of the power and limitations of degree-4 SOS hierarchy for exact inference in graphs, and establishes it as fundamental tool for future research in this area.

Adaptive Morphological Reconstruction for Seeded Image Segmentation Abstract: Image segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision and has numerous applications in various fields. Seeded image segmentation is a popular method for image segmentation, which involves selecting a set of seed pixels and then propagating the labels to the neighboring pixels. However, the performance of seeded image segmentation depends on the quality of the seed pixels. In this paper, we propose an adaptive morphological reconstruction method for seeded image segmentation. Our method uses a combination of morphological operations and machine learning techniques to improve the quality of the seed pixels. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and speed. Our method can be easily integrated into existing seeded image segmentation algorithms and can significantly improve their performance.

The paper investigates use of Diophantine approximations in the study of translation surfaces and planar resonant sets. The authors introduce a new approach to approximating translation surfaces using Diophantine equations, which allows for analysis of the distribution of points on the surface. They also explore the relationship between translation surfaces and planar resonant sets, showing that latter can be used to approximate former. The paper provides several examples and applications of these results, including the study of dynamics of chaotic systems on translation surfaces. Overall, paper demonstrates the power of Diophantine approximations in analysis of complex geometric objects and provides new insights into the structure and behavior of translation surfaces and planar resonant sets.

What the theory of consistency makes available is a standard way of measuring how close one can come to certain desirable outcomes in statistical inferences and machine learning problems, such as data clustering. A number of measures have been proposed for the Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering method. Each measure has its own merits, but none of them covers all situations perfectly satisfactorily. In this thesis, an in-depth study is conducted of the existing measures in terms of their mathematical properties and the relationship they have with other popular performance indicators that are not themselves consistency measures, but are widely used. Finally, promising directions that may lead to improved consistency measures are indicated and need further investigation, either by numerical simulations or through empirical studies.

Flexible grid optical networks allow a better exploitation of fiber capacity, by enabling a denser frequency allocation. A tighter channel spacing, however, requires narrower filters, which increase linear intersymbol interference (ISI), and may dramatically reduce system reach. Commercial coherent receivers are based on symbol by symbol detectors, which are quite sensitive to ISI. In this context, Nyquist spacing is considered as the ultimate limit to wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) packing. In this paper, we show that by introducing a limited-complexity trellis processing at the receiver, either the reach of Nyquist WDM flexi-grid networks can be significantly extended, or a denser-than-Nyquist channel packing (i.e., a higher spectral efficiency (SE)) is possible at equal reach. By adopting well-known information-theoretic techniques, we design a limited-complexity trellis processing and quantify its SE gain in flexi-grid architectures where wavelength selective switches over a frequency grid of 12.5GHz are employed.

Fully supervised deep neural networks for segmentation usually require a massive amount of pixel-level labels which are manually expensive to create. In this work, we develop a multi-task learning method to relaxe this constraint. We regard the segmentation problem as a sequence of approximation subproblems that are recursively defined and in increasing levels of approximation accuracy. The subproblems are handled by a framework that consists of 1) a segmentation task that learns from pixel-level ground truth segmentation masks of a small fraction of the images, 2) a recursive approximation task that conducts partial object regions learning and data-driven mask evolution starting from partial masks of each object instance, and 3) other problem oriented auxiliary tasks that are trained with sparse annotations and promote the learning of dedicated features. Most training images are only labelled by (rough) partial masks, which do not contain exact object boundaries, rather than by their full segmentation masks. During the training phase, the approximation task learns the statistics of these partial masks, and the partial regions are recursively increased towards object boundaries aided by the learned information from the segmentation task in a fully data-driven fashion. The network is trained on an extremely small amount of precisely segmented images and a large set of coarse labels. Annotations can thus be obtained in a cheap way. We demonstrate the efficiency of our approach in three applications with microscopy images and ultrasound images.

Disappointing film with Walter Pidgeon as a hunter who goes to Germany to assassinate Hitler, "The Fuhrer's Prey" ultimately fails to deliver on its exciting premise. While the concept of a manhunt for the most feared dictator is enthralling, the execution is lackluster. Pidgeon tries his best to carry the film with his charisma but falls short in the face of uneven pacing, unconvincing supporting characters, and wildly inaccurate historical elements. The film starts off strong, with Pidgeon's character being recruited by British Intelligence for this secret mission due to his sharpshooting skills. However, upon arriving in Germany, the plot begins to meander. The film wastes valuable time showcasing extraneous subplots that bear no relevance to the main story. The budding romance between Pidgeon's character and a local German woman feels forced and distracts from the primary objective. Furthermore, the supporting cast leaves much to be desired. The bond between Pidgeon's character and his fellow operative is not effectively conveyed, making their partnership feel superficial and hollow. Additionally, the film's depiction of Hitler, portrayed as an incompetent buffoon, does not elicit the sense of urgency and danger required for this clandestine operation. "The Fuhrer's Prey" is further marred by blatant historical inaccuracies, undermining its credibility as a WWII spy thriller. These inaccuracies not only detract from the viewing experience but are also insulting to the actual events and legacies of those involved in WWII. Despite Pidgeon's laudable performance, "The Fuhrer's Prey" is ultimately an unsatisfying and disengaging film. The potentially thrilling narrative is squandered by poor pacing, weak supporting characters, and a lack of respect for historical accuracy. One can only hope that future films with similar premises will learn from this disappointment and succeed where "The Fuhrer's Prey" falters.

The paper "SUSAN: Segment Unannotated image Structure using Adversarial Network" presents a novel approach for segmenting unannotated images using adversarial networks. The proposed method involves training a generative adversarial network (GAN) to generate synthetic images with similar structure to the input image, and then using this generated image to segment the original image. The GAN is trained to minimize the difference between the generated image and the input image, while also maximizing the difference between the generated image and a noise image. This allows the GAN to learn the underlying structure of the input image, which can then be used to segment the image. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method on several benchmark datasets, and shows that it can achieve state-of-the-art performance on some tasks.

Behavior planning is known to be one of the basic cognitive functions, which is essential for any cognitive architecture of any control system used in robotics. At the same time most of the widespread planning algorithms employed in those systems are developed using only approaches and models of Artificial Intelligence and don't take into account numerous results of cognitive experiments. As a result, there is a strong need for novel methods of behavior planning suitable for modern cognitive architectures aimed at robot control. One such method is presented in this work and is studied within a special class of navigation task called smart relocation task. The method is based on the hierarchical two-level model of abstraction and knowledge representation, e.g. symbolic and subsymbolic. On the symbolic level sign world model is used for knowledge representation and hierarchical planning algorithm, MAP, is utilized for planning. On the subsymbolic level the task of path planning is considered and solved as a graph search problem. Interaction between both planners is examined and inter-level interfaces and feedback loops are described. Preliminary experimental results are presented.

Crystalline Fe3O4/NiO bilayers were grown on MgO(001) substrates using reactive molecular beam epitaxy to investigate their structural properties and their morphology. The film thickness either of the Fe3O4 film or of the NiO film has been varied to shed light on the relaxation of the bilayer system. The surface properties as studied by x-ray photo electron spectroscopy and low energy electron diffraction show clear evidence of stoichiometric well-ordered film surfaces. Based on the kinematic approach x-ray diffraction experiments were completely analyzed. As a result the NiO films grow pseudomorphic in the investigated thickness range (up to 34nm) while the Fe3O4 films relax continuously up to the thickness of 50nm. Although all diffraction data show well developed Laue fringes pointing to oxide films of very homogeneous thickness, the Fe3O4-NiO interface roughens continuously up to 1nm root-mean-square roughness with increasing NiO film thickness while the Fe3O4 surface is very smooth independent on the Fe3O4 film thickness. Finally, the Fe3O4-NiO interface spacing is similar to the interlayer spacing of the oxide films while the NiO-MgO interface is expanded.

This paper presents a novel approach to edge detection using structured forests, which are ensembles of decision trees that are trained to detect edges in images. The proposed method, called Fast Edge Detection Using Structured Forests (FEDS), leverages the efficiency and accuracy of structured forests to acheive state-of-the-art performance in edge detection tasks. Existing edge detection methods suffer from either high computational complexity or low accuracy, particularly in the presance of noise or complex structures. FEDS addresses these limitations by exploiting the hierarchical structure of decision trees to efficiently detect edges at multiple scales. The method first generates a set of candidate edges using a simple and efficient algorithm, and then applies a novel edge classification scheme to refine the edges and remove false positives. The proposed edge classification scheme combines both local and global features to accurately distinguish between true edges and false positives. Local features capture the properties of the image intensity values around each candidate edge, while global features capture the spatial relationships between neighboring edges. The scheme uses a set of decision trees to learn the optimal weights for these features and classify the candidate edges as true edges or false positives. FEDS is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, including the Berkeley Segmentation Dataset, the Stanford Background Dataset, and the MSRA10K Dataset. The results show that FEDS outperforms several state-of-the-art edge detection methods, including the Canny edge detector, the Sobel operator, and the Laplacian of Gaussian (LoG) filter, in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The key contributions of this paper are: * A novel edge detection method called Fast Edge Detection Using Structured Forests (FEDS) that combines the efficiency and accuracy of structured forests to acheive state-of-the-art performance. * A novel edge classification scheme that combines local and global features to accurately distinguish between true edges and false positives. * An efficient algorithm for generating candidate edges that reduces the computational complexity of the edge detection process. Overall, FEDS offers a significant improvement over existing edge detection methods, and demonstrates the potential of structured forests for solving computer vision tasks.

Supposedly, an abstract of a research paper entitled, “Holes and cracks in rigid foams,” would read something like this: “This paper investigates the formation and propagation of holes and cracks in rigid foams. Through a combination of theoretical modelling and experiments, we study the mechanism by which these defects are formed and the effect they have on the mechanical properties of the film. We find that the formation of holes and cracks is strongly influenced by the production process, especially the temperature and pressure conditions at which the film is manufactured.” We also show that the presence of holes and cracks can significantly reduce the mechanical strength and stability of the film, making it more prone to failure under stress. These results have important implications for the production and application of rigid foams in various industries, including packaging, construction, and aeronautics. The understanding and control of the formation of holes and cracks will allow manufacturers to optimize their production process and obtain a better-quality film with improved performance and service life.”

This paper presents a novel Spatial-guided Self-supervised Clustering (SGS) neural network for the automatic segmentation of medical images. The SGS-net relies on a self-supervised clustering method to learn a meaningful representation from unlabeled data to guide the segmentation network. The SGS-net also includes a spatial-guided clustering module, which ensures consistency between the learned clusters and the spatial structure of the image, which improves the accuracy of the segmentation. The experiments on two medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method over other approaches.

To improve the classification performance in the field of hyperspectral image processing, many works have been developed based on two common strategies: the integration of spatial and spectral information and the use of neural networks. However, these strategies usually require more training samples than classic classification methods, and they also increase the shortage of labeled samples. In this paper, we propose a novel framework that organically combines the spectrum-based deep learning model and the conditional random field. The deep metric learning model, with the assistance of the loss center, is used to learn the spectrum-based features. The conditional random field, which is firstly proposed for image segmentation, is used to classify the hyperspectral image based on the spatial distance of the two corresponding points and the Euclidean distance between the features of the deep learning model. The proposed framework trains spectral features at the deep metric learning stage and uses half-manually created spatial features at the conditional random field stage. This arrangement partially alleviates the shortage of training samples. Two real hyperspectral images are used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, both in terms of classification accuracy and calculation efficiency.

This survey paper provides overview of high-level prior-based loss functions used in medical image segmentation. These loss functions incorporate prior knowledge about the image structure and context, which can improve the accuracy and robustness of segmentation algorithms. The paper discusses advantages and limitations of different prior-based loss functions and provides a comprehensive review of recent advancements in this field. Overall, this survey paper aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of high-level prior-based loss functions and their potential applications in medical image segmentation.

Lee Clark has today left his position as manager of Scottish Premiership side Kilmarnock, after agreeing a compensation package with League One side Bury. Clark joined Kilmarnock in October 2017 and is credited with helping to keep the club in the top division. He had been in charge for just over a year, having previously been in charge at Blackpool and Birmingham City. The former Newcastle United midfielder was appointed by the Shakers following the resignation of Ryan Lowe last month. The club have been searching for a replacement since then, and after weeks of negotiations, have finally concluded a deal to bring in Clark. Bury chairman Steven Dale said: "We're delighted to welcome Lee Clark as our new manager. His track record speaks for itself and he will be a great asset to the club. We look forward to working with him to help take Bury back to where they belong - in the Championship." Kilmarnock chairman Jim Mann said: "We are sorry to see Lee go, but we understand that the lure of managing in the English leagues was too strong to resist. We wish him all the best in his new role and thank him for his hard work and dedication during his time at Kilmarnock." Clark is expected to be in the dugout for his first game in charge of Bury next Saturday when the club travel to Oxford United.

A large labeled dataset is a key to the success of supervised deep learning, but for medical image segmentation, it is highly challenging to obtain sufficient annotated images for model training. In many scenarios, unannotated images are abundant and easy to adquire. Self-supervised learning (SSL) has shown grat potentials in exploiting raw data information and representation learning. In this paper, we propose Hierarchical Self-Supervised Learning (HSSL), a new self-supervised framework that boosts medical image segmentation by making good use of unannotated data. Unlike the current literature on task-specific self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning, we utilize SSL to learn task-agnostic knowledge from heterogeneous data for various medical image segmentation tasks. Specifically, we first aggregate a dataset from several medical challenges, then pre-train the network in a self-supervised manner, and finally fine-tune on labeled data. We develop a new loss function by combining contrastive loss and classification loss and pretrain an encoder-decoder architecture for segmentation tasks. Our extensive experiments show that multi-domain joint pre-training benefits downstream segmentation tasks and outperforms single-domain pre-training significantly. Compared to learning from scratch, our new method yields better performance on various tasks (e.g., +0.69% to +18.60% in Dice scores with 5% of annotated data). With limited amounts of training data, our method can substantially bridge the performance gap w.r.t. denser annotations (e.g., 10% vs.~100% of annotated data).

Background: Chase is a system that supports real-time, visual tracking through spatial gradient information. Chasing uses neural networks to learn predictive models of path directions and trajectories given location of each cell in 3D scene. A recent set of papers provides evidence for recurrent network architectures which can provide adequate framework for both deep learning and supervised and unsupervised hierarchical clustering tasks; however these hierarchies are poorly understood (see [22], [23], [25] ). In this work we address one critical issue which has prevented previous approaches: When given a training dataset composed solely of target cells at known position coordinates, why does neural net converge well on a consistent representation? We propose to solve this problem using dynamic coding with low temporal resolution and by identifying differentially active neurons along each branch of the tree. The resulting model enables visual localization capabilities as large or larger than those used in traditional linear image sequence classification. Our implementation achieves high accuracy within 30 seconds during tests on simple indoor images (e.g., outdoor images). RLCorrector is a novel approach to improving the accuracy of image segmentation in connectomics. This method uses reinforcement learning to correct errors made by automated segmentation algorithms. The algorithm is trained on a dataset of images with known ground truth segmentations, and uses a reward function to encourage the algorithm to make more accurate predictions. The results of RLCorrector show significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to traditional methods, and demonstrate the potential of reinforcement learning for improving the accuracy of image segmentation in connectomics.

Video moment retrieval is to search the moment that is most relevant to the given natural language query. Existing methods are mostly trained in a fully-supervised setting, which requires the full annotations of temporal boundary for each query. However, manually labeling the annotations is actually time-consuming and expensive. In this paper, we propose a novel weakly-supervised moment retrieval framework requiring only coarse video-level annotations for training. Specifically, we devise a proposal generation module that aggregates the context information to generate and score all candidate proposals in one single pass. We then devise an algorithm that considers both exploitation and exploration to select top-K proposals. Next, we build a semantic completion module to measure the semantic similarity between the selected proposals and query, compute reward and provide feedbacks to the proposal generation module for scoring refinement. Experiments on the ActivityCaptions and Charades-STA demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

The journal "A Thorough View of Exact Inference in Graphs from the Degree-4 Sum-of-Squares Hierarchy" provides a detailed study of exact inference in graphs using the degree-4 sum-of-squares (SOS) structure. This work expands on recent research that established the SOS structure as a robust tool for solving graphical models, and gives a detailed understanding of its capabilities and constraints. The researchers demonstrate that the degree-4 SOS hierarchy can be used to perform exact inference in many classes of graphs, including bounded-degree graphs, planar graphs, andgraphs with excluded minors. They offer explicit limits on the mathematical complexity of exact inference using the SOS hierarchy for these classes of graphs, and demonstrate that it can be done in polynomial time for certain interesting situations. The paper additionally demonstrates the relationships between the SOS hierarchy and other methods to exact inference, such as belief propagation and linear programming relaxations. The researchers show that the SOS hierarchy can be viewed as an alternative formulation of these techniques, offering new insights into their strengths and limitations. Meanwhile, the researchers investigate the relation between the SOS hierarchy and the mathematical properties of graphs. They prove lower limits on the length of the smallest witnesses provided by the SOS hierarchy to prove independence claims in different families of graphs, and provide justification for the hypothesis that the SOS hierarchy is adequate for testing independence in some regimes. Overall, this work gives a comprehensive view of the power and constraints of the degree-4 SOS hierarchy for approximate inference in graphs, and establishes it as a crucial tool for future study in this area.
