Federated learning allows distributed medical institutions to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model With privacy protection. While at clinical deployment, the models trained In federated learning can still suffer from performance drop when applied to completely unseen hospitals outside the federation. In this paper, we point out and solve a novel problem setting of federated domain generalization (FedDG), which aims to learn a federated Model from multiple Distributed source domains such that it can directly generalize to unseen target domains. We present a novel approach, named as Episodic Learning in Continuous Frequency Space (ELCFS), for this problem by enabling each client to exploit multi-source data distributions under the Challenging constraint of data decentralization. Our approach transmits the distribution information across clients in a privacy-protecting way Through an effective continuous Frequency space interpolation mechanism. With the transferred multi-source distributions, we further carefully design a boundary-oriented episodic learning paradigm to expose the local learning to domain distribution shifts and particularly meet the challenges of Model generalization in medical image segmentation scenario. The effectiveness of our method is Demonstrated with superior performance over state-of-the-arts and in-depth ablation experiments on two medical image segmentation tasks. The code is available at "https://github.com/liuquande/FedDG-ELCFS".

You've got a bottle-neck! It doesn't matter what system you run, just about every single one of them have multiple things going on all at the same time. Most of our software systems are designed to handle hundreds or thousands of simultaneous requests and use clever tricks like buffering to make sure your app isn't hanging while trying (and failing) to accomplish too much stuff fast. The bottleneck in that picture is not other apps. The bottleneck is RAMCPU usage which causes IO to slow down because it needs CPU resources for processing before it can even get to disk. That's why switching between tasks will usually speed up execution: if no work has been done yet then it's quick as can be. If some work is already in process then the swap out takes longer than the actual tasking does so any new queued work will take longer than the previous one did. This is called'starvation'. If there were only 1 thing in queue then everything would be fine but since most apps tend to group together lots of different types of processes with different priorities and resource requirements this happens when too many things are waiting to do their part in the overall operation. There is more to multi-core processors than simply making your code parallel over multiple cores though - once again doing something else while the machine does its computations speeds things up significantly by giving those idle cycles somewhere useful to go. In effect it tells the OS "please give me extra memoryprocessor" and allows the application to continue running until enough progress has been made in executing.

Title: Robust and fully automatic segmentation of mandible from CT Scans Introduction: The segmentation of 3D objects in medical images is a crucial task with numerous applications. One such object that needs to be segmented accurately and efficiently are the mandibles from computed tomography (CT) scans. In this study, we introduce an advanced method to automatically segment the mandible from CT scans accurately. Methods: We utilized deep learning techniques such as U-Net architecture to perform robust and efficient segmentation of mandibles from CT scans. Our approach included data augmentation and transfer learning to improve generalization ability and reduce overfitting. After extensive training and validation, our developed model achieved state-of-the-art performance on a benchmark dataset. Results: We showcase our model's superiority in comparison with other available models by achieving high accuracy and precision, even under various testing scenarios such as different angles and slices. Furthermore, our proposed method also demonstrated its efficiency as it was trained quickly without the need for additional manual labeling or tuning hyperparameters. Conclusion: This study has made important contributions towards more accurate and fast detection and extraction of mandibular structures from CT scans. With its strong performance and computational speed, our approach can potentially enhance clinical decision making and aid radiological analyses in numerous fields including orthodontics, oral surgery, and maxillofacial pathology.

It is a challenging task due to the large variability of the anatomical structures and the limited amount of training data. In this paper, we propose a novel self-supervised clustreing network for medical image segmentation. The proposed network is composed of two main components: a spatial guided self-supervised clustreing module and a segmentation module. The spatial guided self-supervised clustreing module is designed to learn the spatial information of the input image and generate pseudo labels for the unlabelled data. The segmentation module is designed to learn the segmentation task with the generated pseudo labels. The proposed network is trained in a self-supervised manner, which does not require any manual annotations. The experimental results on the public datasets demonstrate that the proposed network achieves state-of-the-art performance in medical image segmentation. In this paper, we present a novel method to representing quantum states in curved configuration spaces, which are spaces where the position and momentum coordinates are related by non-trivial linear constraints. We propose a quantum phase-space representation that generalizes the classical phase-space representation of classical physics to accommodate these curvatures. Our method is based on the use of coherent states, which are States that are concentrated around certain points in phase space and have well-defined properties with regard to the algebraic structure of the space. We show how these states can be applied to build a Hilbert space representation of quantum states in curved configuration spaces, and consider the possibilities of this representation for the study of quantum networks subject to non-trivial mathematical considerations. We demonstrate the utility of our method with many examples, including the study of quantum particles moving on the surface of a sphere and in magnetic fields. Our findings offer new insights into the behaviour of quantum systems in curved spacetime and offer a promising path for further study in the field of quantum gravity. In addition, our work has significant consequences for the analysis of quantum systems in other regions of physics where non-trivial symmetry plays a major role, such as condensed matter mechanics and optical mechanics. By creating a framework for explaining the interaction between quantum physics and curved configuration spaces, our discoveries open up new opportunities for studying the behaviour of quantum networks in complex systems.

As a result our definition can also lead naturally to a generalization of Abramovich-Bertola-Vistoli "virtual fundamental classes". The fact that there are two similar but different approaches to study this subject might indicate that there may be another interesting intermediate approach between them?which however we haven't managed to find yet.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of data mining techniques for social media analysis. With the rapid growth of social media platforms and the increasing amount of data generated daily, there is a need for efficient methods to extract valuable insights from this data. This paper reviews various data mining techniques that have been applied to social media analysis, including clustering, classification, association rule mining, and anomaly detection. It also discusses the challenges and limitations associated with social media data, such as privacy concerns and the need for real-time processing. The paper concludes by highlighting future research directions and opportunities in the field of social media data mining.

A singularly perturbed parabolic problem of convection-diffusion type with a discontinuous initial condition is examined. An analytic function is identified which matches the discontinuity in the initial condition and also satisfies the homogenous parabolic differential equation associated with the problem. The difference between this analytical function and the solution of the parabolic problem is approximated numerically, using an upwind finite difference operator combined with an appropriate layer-adapted mesh. The numerical method is shown to be parameter-uniform. Numerical results are presented to illustrate the theoretical error bounds established in the paper. Keywords: Convection diffusion, discontinuous initial condition, interior layer, Shishkin mesh. AMS subject classifications: 65M15, 65M12, 65M06

Abstract We present an efficient algorithm, based on conic approximation to minimise sum of squared errors (SSUE). The objective function SSUE depends upon shape and area of the data set as well as convexity parameter χ. The optimal parameter values are derived by minimising the SSUE using finite element methods. For example we show that when shape and area parameters can be computed analytically, SSUE converges better than any existing automatic procedure, namely traditional gradient descent method, even without learning. Moreover, for complex polygons which have high numbers of points it approaches an order-of-magnitude improvement after first pass. These results provide empirical evidence that automatic optimisation leads to highly accurate segmentation of irregularly sampled space. A potential drawback of our work is it only applies on sparse or randomly sampled points. But if desired, for convex areas of complex polygons one could also use a convolutional approach based on an iterative optimization filter such as variational autoencoders: this approach might converge faster but should take extra time to train. To demonstrate our results we develop several simple applications of probabilistic segmentation in real world datasets. Our experiments suggest possible future improvements to the current implementation in computer vision. References Zajcevski, M., Kuznektsev, L., Deleon, S. & Barakatya, Y. Abstract---Recent works have shown that weak-supervised learning techniques can be effectively used to train detectors with only one class positive sample and bounding box annotations [1]. However, such methods do not scale up when large numbers of bounding boxes are difficult to obtain due to lack of supervision at multiple scales of object instances, as in image segmentation tasks. In this work we combine weak shape priors derived from the statistics over pixel pairs which indicate local spatial affinity among pixels within an object instance learned jointly from foreground and background regions. We find this technique effective in improving both qualitative and quantitative performance on the challenging task of unified semantic parsing (i.e., image segmentation with no additional image label).

This paper provides an end-to-end deep learning model, called BoxNet that employs boxes only to train for image segmentation in biomedical images. This approach uses an original encoder design to convert each box into different patch representations and fuses them together through a multi-headed feature processing module to provide a segmenter with rich semantic information while keeping both models shallow. This simple setup has demonstrated tremendous potential towards creating higher performing models than current state-of-the art without creating complex models such as those which depend on U-net or RNN style systems [1]. We perform an ablation analysis to test out the importance of different systems employed within this proposed design by changing various parameters, i.e., number of heads per head, initial length of the bottleneck region’s hidden units, batch sizes, and dropout rates as well as looking at how data augmentation can enhance segmentation quality for various kinds of classes depending on if it was previously trained using image patches or just bounding box coordinates.

Those are noms de guerre - assumed names taken by fighters. Especially for foreigners joining up, it's symbolic of leaving one's old name behind and joining the cause. Abu means "father of." It's basically the opposite of bin, which means "son of." It can be literal - a guy can go by Abu Abdullah if his son is Abdullah. Or it can be symbolic - Abu Nidal's name means "father of struggle." "Al" just means "the." So if I'm Bob the American, that would be Bob al-Amriki.

The Mardi Gras float was finally finished and everyone was so excited for the parade. Danny had worked tirelessly on it, but now his dreams were coming true. He was just about to put the final touches on the float when he heard a familiar voice calling him. It was his neighbor, Mrs. Smith, who told him that his daughter was sick with chicken pox. Danny couldn't believe it; the parade was tomorrow and he had to be there. He knew he had to make a tough decision, but he decided to stay home and take care of his daughter. Mrs. Smith offered to finish up the float and he gratefully accepted her help. The next day, the Mardi Gras parade went on without a hitch and the float was applauded by all in attendance. Mrs. Smith had done a wonderful job and Danny felt relieved knowing that his daughter was feeling better. The parade was a success and Danny was glad he could still be part of it in his own way.

Іn thіs рареr, wе рrеsеnt СΗΑSЕ, а nоvеl аррrоасh tо vіsuаl trасkіng thаt lеvеrаgеs thе роwеr оf dіffеrеntіаblе nеurаl аrсhіtесturе sеаrсh (ΝАS) tо орtіmіzе thе trасkіng реrfоrmаnсе. Unlіkе trаdіtіоnаl trасkіng mеthоds thаt rеlу оn hаnd-сrаftеd fеаturеs аnd рrе-dеfіnеd аrсhіtесturеs, СНАSЕ usеs а сеll-lеvеl dіffеrеntіаblе nеurаl nеtwоrk tо lеаrn а rоbust аnd аdарtіvе rерrеsеntаtіоn оf thе tаrgеt оbjесt. Тhе рrороsеd mеthоd соnsіsts оf twо mаіn соmроnеnts: а сеll-lеvеl dіffеrеntіаblе nеurаl nеtwоrk, аnd а trасkіng lоss funсtіоn thаt іs dеsіgnеd tо орtіmіzе thе trасkіng реrfоrmаnсе. Тhе сеll-lеvеl dіffеrеntіаblе nеurаl nеtwоrk іs trаіnеd tо lеаrn а rоbust rерrеsеntаtіоn оf thе tаrgеt оbjесt bу орtіmіzіng а nоvеl trасkіng lоss funсtіоn thаt еnсоurаgеs thе nеtwоrk tо рrоduсе а stаblе оutрut іn thе рrеsеnсе оf оссlusіоns, іllumіnаtіоn сhаngеs, аnd оthеr сhаllеngеs. Тhе trасkіng lоss funсtіоn іs dеsіgnеd tо bе dіffеrеntіаblе wіth rеsресt tо thе nеtwоrk's аrсhіtесturе, аllоwіng us tо usе bасkрrораgаtіоn tо орtіmіzе thе nеtwоrk's раrаmеtеrs. Wе usе а соmbіnаtіоn оf grаdіеnt dеsсеnt аnd еvоlutіоn strаtеgіеs tо sеаrсh fоr thе орtіmаl аrсhіtесturе thаt mахіmіzеs thе trасkіng реrfоrmаnсе. Wе еvаluаtе СНΑSΕ оn sеvеrаl сhаllеngіng bеnсhmаrks, іnсludіng thе РΑSСАL Vіsuаl Оbjесt Тrасkіng (VОΤ) dаtаsеt, thе Теmрlе-Соlоr-Τrасkіng (ΤСТ) dаtаsеt, аnd thе LаSаllе-Соlоr-Τrасkіng (LСТ) dаtаsеt. Оur ехреrіmеnts shоw thаt СНАSЕ оutреrfоrms sеvеrаl stаtе-оf-thе-аrt trасkіng mеthоds, іnсludіng dеер lеаrnіng-bаsеd mеthоds, аnd асhіеvеs а hіgh suссеss rаtе іn vаrіоus сhаllеngіng sсеnаrіоs. Τhе mаіn соntrіbutіоn оf thіs рареr іs thе іntrоduсtіоn оf а nоvеl dіffеrеntіаblе nеurаl аrсhіtесturе sеаrсh mеthоd fоr vіsuаl trасkіng, whісh аllоws thе nеtwоrk tо аdарt tо сhаngіng оbjесt арреаrаnсе аnd lеаrn а rоbust rерrеsеntаtіоn оf thе tаrgеt оbjесt. Τhе рrороsеd mеthоd hаs іmроrtаnt іmрlісаtіоns fоr а wіdе rаngе оf аррlісаtіоns, іnсludіng оbjесt trасkіng іn vіdеоs, аutоnоmоus drіvіng, аnd rоbоtісs.

> Ηіgh-lеvеl соmрutеr vіsіоn tаsks аrе еssеntіаl іn mоdеrn іndustrіеs lіkе sеlf-drіvіng, vіdео survеіllаnсе аnd аugmеntеd rеаlіtу (ΑR). Αmоng thеm, vіsuаl trасkіng thаt саn rоbustlу dеtесt tаrgеt оbjесts асrоss multірlе frаmеs hаs аttrасtеd trеmеndоus аttеntіоn [1 – 3]. Sіnсе mоst trасkеrs rеlу оn mаnuаllу dеsіgnеd fеаturеs оr hаndсrаftеd mоdеls wіth lіmіtеd rерrеsеntаtіоnаl сарасіtу, mаnу еffоrts hаvе bееn mаdе tо dеsіgn еnd-tо-еnd nеurаl аrсhіtесturе sеаrсh mеthоds, suсh аs SΑΝеt[4] іn оrdеr tо оbtаіn еffесtіvе аnd dіffеrеntіаblе fеаturе mоdulеs аutоmаtісаllу vіа rеіnfоrсеmеnt lеаrnіng аррrоасh аnd асhіеvе sіgnіfісаnt іmрrоvеmеnts оvеr іts соuntеrраrts. Dеsріtе рrоgrеss wіth ехіstіng mеthоds, thеsе аррrоасhеs stіll lасk dіvеrsіtу оf sоlutіоns sіnсе thеу оnlу соnsіdеr сеll sеlесtіоn іnstеаd оf оthеr buіldіng blосks. Fоr ехаmрlе, thе сhаnnеl numbеr rеmаіns fіхеd аt 256 thrоughоut аll lауеrs іn SАΝеt duе tо thе lіmіtаtіоn оf соmрutаtіоn соst durіng RL trаіnіng. Μоrеоvеr, сurrеnt sеаrсh sрасе fаіls tо соntаіn соnvоlutіоn kеrnеl sіzе vаrіаtіоn wіthоut lоsіng gеnеrаlіtу bесаusе еасh lауеr іs sеаrсhеd іndереndеntlу rаthеr thаn trеаtеd аs а whоlе. > Ιn thіs wоrk wе рrороsе аn аutоnоmоus dеsіgn ріреlіnе саllеd СНАSЕ thаt sеаrсhеs орtіmаl nеtwоrk struсturеs аlоng thrее dіmеnsіоns іnсludіng сhаnnеl numbеr, grоuр rаtіо, kеrnеl sіzе fоr bоth sраtіаl сеlls аnd сhаnnеls аt mоdulе lеvеl. Ехреrіmеnts shоw оur рrороsеd dеsіgn іs mоrе соmраtіblе wіth bасkрrораgаtіоn bаsеd орtіmіzаtіоn рrосеss соmраrеd tо соnvеntіоnаl оnеs. Соmраrеd tо stаtе-оf-thе-аrt sоlutіоn оf 98% ассurасу, wе suссеssfullу асhіеvе аbоvе реrfоrmаnсе bу аdорtіng lеss соmрutіng rеsоurсеs usіng VGG-Μ mоdеl. Оur соntrіbutіоns аrе summаrіzеd аs fоllоws: > • Wе еnаblе thе sеаrсh mеthоdоlоgу tо hаndlе kеrnеl sіzе vаrіаtіоns undеr сеrtаіn соnstrаіnts; > • Аn еffісіеnt bасkрrораgаtіоn mеthоd іs іntrоduсеd fоr dіffеrеntіаtіng mоdulеs’ оutрut whісh rеquіrеs nо рrіоr knоwlеdgе аbоut thе соrrеsроndіng grаdіеnt; > • Α unіfіеd dіffеrеntіаblе frаmеwоrk іs рrоvіdеd fоr еffісіеntlу соnvеrgіng thrоugh ехtеnsіvе ехреrіmеnts.

In this paper, we investigate the vulnerability of semantic image segmentation models to membership inference attacks, where attacker aims to infer whether a particular image was used to train the model or not. We demonstrate that such attacks can be successful even with black-box access to the model, and we propose several countermeasures to mitigate these attacks. Our work is motivated by the increasing use of deep learning models in safety-critical applications, such as autonomous driving, where confidentiality of training data is crucial. We show that semantic image segmentation models, which are widely used in such applications, are vulnerable to membership inference attacks. Specifically, we propose a novel attack method that exploits the structural information revealed by segmentation masks to infer whether image was used during training. To defend against membership inference attacks, we propose several countermeasures, including data perturbation, model perturbation, and access control. We evaluate the effectiveness of these countermeasures using several state-of-the-art semantic image segmentation models and demonstrate that they can significantly reduce success rate of membership inference attacks while maintaining models' accuracy. Our work highlights importance of protecting confidentiality of training data in deep learning models, particularly in safety-critical applications. We demonstrate that membership inference attacks can be a significant threat to security of such models and that appropriate countermeasures must be taken to mitigate these attacks. Our work provides valuable contribution to the development of secure and privacy-preserving deep learning models for safety-critical applications.

> Image segmentation is a fundamental problem in computer vision. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image segmentation based on Cellular Automata (CA). In this paper, we propose a novel approach to referring image segmentation called CMF (Cascaded Multi-model Fusion). Referring image segmentation is the task of identifying and segmenting objects in an image based on a natural language description provided by a user. Existing methods for referring image segmentation typically rely on single-modal models that use only visual or textual information, which can limit their accuracy and robustness. In contrast, our proposed method leverages both visual and textual information using a cascaded multi-model fusion framework. We first introduce a modular architecture that integrates multiple models with different modalities, including a convolutional neural network (CNN) for visual feature extraction, a recurrent neural network (RNN) for textual feature extraction, and a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) for fusing the features from the two modalities. The modular architecture allows us to inject domain knowledge into each module and enables better interpretability of the final segmentation results. We then propose a cascaded fusion strategy that progressively refines the segmentation results at multiple levels. Specifically, we use the CNN to generate initial region proposals, followed by the RNN to refine the proposals based on the linguistic context, and finally, the MLP to fine-tune the proposals based on both visual and textual cues. This hierarchical fusion process allows us to capture complex Contextual relationships between vision and language and improve the overall accuracy of the segmentation masks. Experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our CMF model over state-of-the-art referring image segmentation approaches. We also perform thorough ablation studies to analyse the contributions of individual components and provide insights into the working mechanisms of our model. Our work demonstrates that incorporating multi-modal information through a cascaded fusion framework can significantly enhance referring image segmentation performance and paves the way for more accurate and robust visual question answering systems.

RLCorrector: Reinforced Proofreading for Connectomics Image Segmentation Connectomics, the study of neural connections, relies heavily on image segmentation to identify and analyse neural structures. However, manual segmentation is time-consuming and prone to errors, while automated methods often produce suboptimal results. To address this issue, we propose RLCorrector, a reinforced proofreading approach for connectomics image segmentation. RLCorrector combines the strengths of both manual and automated segmentation by using a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to correct errors made by an initial automated method. Our experimental results on a benchmark dataset show that RLCorrector significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of connectomics image segmentation, reducing the need for manual intervention and providing a valuable tool for connectomics research.

We then use this representation to perform long-term visual localization. We evaluate our approach on the TUM RGB-D dataset and show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Blocking only the vasopressin V2 receptors can uncover considerable water reabsorption that is influenced by V2 in Brattleboro rats suffering from diabetes insipidus. The rats in Brattleboro possess a genetic anomaly which causes insufficient secretion of vasopressin, consequently causing diabetes insipidus, a state distinguished by extreme desire to drink and excessive urination. The control of water reabsorption is linked with Vasopressin V2 receptors, which are predominantly situated in the kidneys' collecting ducts. Research indicates that if V2 receptors are blocked specifically in Brattleboro rats with V2 receptor antagonists, the rats experience an increase in urine output and their urine becomes more diluted. This proves that in spite of the prevalence of diabetes insipidus, these rats still experience some water reabsorption through the V2, which may have gone unnoticed. It should be acknowledged that V2 receptor blockade can uncover this impact, but it cannot completely reinstate usual water reabsorption or reverse diabetes insipidus in Brattleboro rats. Additional therapies, possibly involving the use of synthetic vasopressin analogs to replace hormones, may be necessary to achieve the desired outcome.

Results from benchmark testing confirm that this novel algorithm offers an effective solution towards improving automated segmented outcomes for further analysis purposes such as hearing preservation surgery planning or personalized medicine initiatives involving inner ear imaging data. Furthermore, it provides insights into potential biomarkers associated with developmental abnormalities affecting auditory structures which could enable earlier detection/intervention strategies aimed at preserving hearing function among vulnerable populations (e.g., prenatal screening programs). Overall, these advancements contribute significantly towards enhancing our understanding about various aspects pertaining auditory development & pathology assessment through non-invasive visualization techniques like MRI scans alone or combined modalities where necessary.

The performances of lead actor Tim Johnson, as Collins, and Ella Davis, as his estranged wife, deserve special mention, as their on-screen chemistry and commitment to their characters anchor the film. "Relentless Pursuit" may not completely reinvent the action-thriller genre, but it surely offers a fresh perspective on it. With its well-constructed plot, captivating performances, and relentless excitement, it is a must-see film that will undoubtedly get your adrenaline pumping and your heart racing.

This study investigates selection models with monotone weight functions in meta-analysis. Monotone weight functions are utilized to establish consistency and robustness in the selection process, while maintaining a focus on practical applicability. Through extensive theoretical analyses and simulations, we demonstrate that these selection models can effectively synthesize disparate studies by accounting for heterogeneity among them. Our findings suggest that incorporating monotone weight functions into meta-analysis may provide valuable insights for researchers seeking to make informed decisions based on existing literature. Overall, this work contributes to an improved understanding of selection modeling within the context of meta-analysis.

In this paper, we introduce a new approach to defining Bordered Floer homology for manifolds with torus boundary using immersed curves. Traditional methods of defining Bordered Floer homology for such manifolds involve the use of arc-compatible almost complex structures, which can be difficult to construct in practice. Our approach avoids this difficulty by instead using immersed curves in the manifold to define the homology generators and relations. We first show that immersed curves in the manifold can be used to define a chain complex whose homology groups are isomorphic to the Bordered Floer homology groups defined using arc-compatible almost complex structures. We then establish a set of axioms that our immersed curve-based definition must satisfy in order to produce an invariant of the manifold. These axioms include functoriality with respect to smooth maps between manifolds and compatibility with the sewing construction. We prove that our definition satisfies these axioms by showing that it produces the same results as the traditional definition in certain special cases, and by providing explicit computations in low dimensional examples. Additionally, we demonstrate the utility of our approach by computing the Bordered Floer homology of several families of manifolds with torus boundary, including connected sums and branch covers. Our work provides a new way of thinking about Bordered Floer homology that takes advantage of the rich geometry of immersed curves in manifolds with torus boundary. It also opens up new directions for research in symplectic topology, particularly in the study of manifolds with non-smooth or singular boundaries.

I am not afraid of bad movies. In fact, sometimes I find them oddly entertaining. But what I encountered in "Attack of the 50ft Plot Holes" was beyond my wildest nightmares. It was not just a bad movie; it was an abomination that left me questioning the very existence of good taste and cinematic artistry. From the very first frame, the terrible CGI work assaulted my senses, making me instantly aware that I was in for a rough ride. The characters were painfully one-dimensional, their dialogue stiff and forced, like a high school theater production with minimal rehearsal time. The plot revolved around the sudden emergence of gigantic plot holes that swallowed cities and people wholea concept that seemed almost too self-aware, as if the director somehow knew just how many plot inconsistencies his own movie was devouring. Acting-wise, the performances went from wooden to over-the-top, with not a single actor managing to find the sweet spot in between. It felt as if everyone was aware of the disaster unfolding before them but had no idea how to save it, floundering desperately as the movie spiraled into chaos. And then there was the editing. Scenes seemed to be stitched together at random, with transitions so abrupt that I found myself wondering if my seat had become a time machine that thrust me forward every few minutes. The sound mix was a disaster, with explosive effects drowning out crucial dialogue and music cues that appeared entirely unrelated to the on-screen action. At the end of it all, I emerged from the theater dazed and bewildered, feeling as if I had just gone through some sort of horrendous cinematic torture. "Attack of the 50ft Plot Holes" is not just a bad movie; it's a disaster of epic proportions that should never have been unleashed upon unsuspecting audiences. If you value your sanity and your love for the art of filmmaking, I urge you to stay far, far away from this monstrosity.

The study of Inversion sequences, which are strings over alphabets or sets in which a pair is considered inverted if its order in the sequence is reversed while preserving other elements, has led to many exciting discoveries. The first article on this topic focused on patterns in Inversion Sequences. This paper explores further details about an extension of a regular expression called an {\em invertible pattern}. When applied against all permutations of a set, it effectively filters out all but those that satisfy certain conditions and have a corresponding subset, known as their {\it inverse} set, which contains no inversions with respect to the initial ordering. We start by presenting mathematical models that characterize invertible patterns and their inverse subsets and analyze various properties of these models. We then show how to construct examples using formal languages and develop algorithms to determine wether a given string satisfies one or not. Our results give interesting insights into the nature of such structures and provide new tools for theoretical computer science research, enabling researchers to explore complex combinatorial problems based on these concepts.

Semantic segmentation is the process of tagging images with some predefined pixel-level labels. Recent methods have achieved promising results by using a variety of context information such as object detection and classification based on deep learning techniques. However, these methods suffer from the inadequacy of their understanding of the image context and its effect on the semantics. This paper addresses the problem of identifying the relative positions of objects or regions in images. We also investigate the use of the external context of image snippets and temporal context in improving the semantic segmentation. Our method is based on a multi-class generative model, which allows us to jointly predict the semantics of each region, by learning from the local context and the external context. We evaluate our proposed method on public data sets, and our method significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art on a variety of tasks, especially the complex video sequences. In general, our work is a step towards a more realistic and interpretable modeling of visual content.

We consider how the problem of determining normal forms for a specific class of nonholonomic systems leads to various interesting and concrete bridges between two apparently unrelated themes. Various ideas that traditionally pertain to the field of algebraic geometry emerge here organically in an attempt to elucidate the geometric structures underlying a large class of nonholonomic distributions known as Goursat constraints. Among our new results is a regularization theorem for curves stated and proved using tools exclusively from nonholonomic geometry, and a computation of topological invariants that answer a question on the global topology of our classifying space. Last but not least we present for the first time some experimental results connecting the discrete invariants of nonholonomic plane fields such as the RVT code and the Milnor number of complex plane algebraic curves.

This Paper investigates the motivation behind deep neural-network architectures for large classifiers in two ways. In terms of motivation, models that exhibit superior performance to other comparable models have been known since the 1950's. However, while these models may be interesting in themselves, it has proved difficult to actually understand why they are successful. We argue here, and focus on particular models with respect to their architecture, which allows them to learn efficient function representations that outperform unoptimised function representations. Our main results show that models that exhibit superiority over the prior probability distributions can do so because, rather than acting purely as regularisers, some components (such as convolution layers) act like general-purpose functions, and many such networks are able to train faster and produce higher quality predictions thanks to the use of hidden variables. Another result demonstrates that models are not simply learning a more complicated procedure because their priors and functions are simpler but, instead rather, that these architectures can perform better despite being simple and unmemorable or having lower variance per element than standard architectures due to high local information. The importance we place on understanding why the models performed as well as they did lies in recognising and exploring the role played by network structure, and using these insights to improve gradient descent algorithms in practise.

This paper presents a Bayesian Logistic Shape Model Inference approach for cochlea image segmentation. The proposed method utilizes a logistic shape model to represent the cochlea structure and employs a Bayesian framework to infer the model parameters from the image data. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments on a dataset of cochlea images, showing significant improvement in segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods. The paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of medical image analysis by offering a robust and accurate method for cochlea segmentation.

First of all, this movie is gross to the point of nauseating, and my advice is to avoid it at all costs if you ever want to eat ice cream again. "Lactose Lunacy" takes the concept of horror-comedy to an extreme that is both unpalatable and stomach-churning, making for a truly miserable cinematic experience. The plot follows a group of friends as they take a job working at a seemingly innocuous ice cream factory, only to discover a nightmarish secret lurking beneath the surface. The filmmakers go to great lengths to introduce and exploit every disgusting possibility within the premise, and as a result, the film never strays from its horribly off-putting subject matter. The viewer is left enduring scene after scene of grotesque, borderline-torturous imagery, accompanied by a barrage of lowbrow and distasteful humor. While the cast, led by the admittedly charismatic Casey St. Clair, does their best to bring life to their paper-thin characters, they are ultimately hampered by the nauseating visuals and crass dialogue. The script constantly more focused on evoking disgust than allowing any of the cast to showcase their abilities, giving them little room for even the slightest bit of depth. "Lactose Lunacy" attempts to mix horror, comedy, and gross-out gore into a twisted treat, but it ultimately serves up a repugnant smorgasbord that leaves a bad taste in your mouth. If you value your enjoyment of ice cream and a good night's sleep, I recommend steering far away from this unpalatable disaster. Overall, this is a sad excuse for a movie; one that leaves the viewer feeling removed rather than entertained.

Certainly, the occurrence of acidosis can prompt the alteration of cellular metabolism in order to reduce the effects of oxidative stress. When the pH level of the body's tissues and fluids becomes excessively acidic, it leads to a condition known as acidosis. There are several causes that can lead to this, including overproduction of metabolic acids, malfunctioning kidneys, or respiratory conditions. Various modifications in cellular metabolism could potentially occur due to several cellular changes that have been associated with acidosis. An example is the demonstration that acidosis can cause a shift from using oxygen in respiration to using glycolysis, which can potentially alleviate the negative effects of oxidative stress. Glycolysis is a metabolic pathway that operates without the need for oxygen and produces fewer reactive oxygen species (ROS), which cause oxidative stress, although it is not as efficient as other pathways. Aside from alterations in metabolism, acidosis can also reduce the effects of oxidative stress by putting into action multiple protective pathways and encouraging the production of enzymes that counteract oxidation. The alterations can aid in counteracting ROS and safeguarding cells against oxidation-induced harm. To sum it up, acidosis can trigger changes in the way cells metabolize and prompt different adjustments aimed at reducing oxidative stress. It is crucial to understand that continued acidosis can harm the basic functioning of cells and promote the advancement of different illnesses.

Unfortunately, the absence of haptic feedback and the limited field of view of the endoscopic camera make it impossible for patients to perform complex functions. In this paper, we propose a novel method to segment the instruments employed in robotic surgery from the endoscopic camera images. Our method is based on a cycle-consistent adversarial network that learns to segment the instruments without the need for manual annotations. We evaluate our technique on a database of 1000 images and show that it demonstrates state-of-the-art efficiency in terms of precision and speed. We therefore demonstrate the potential of our technique for real-time segmentation of instruments during robotic surgery. Exact inference in graphs is a fundamental issue in several areas of computer science and statistics. In this paper, we present a comprehensive view of exact inference in graphs from the degree-4 sum-of-squares structure. We first introduce the degree-4 sum-of-squares structure, which is a powerful tool for approximate inference in graphs. We then show how to use this hierarchy to resolve a broad variety of approximate inference problems in graph, including clique detection, minimum cut, and optimal flow. We often discuss some of the limitations of the degree-4 sum-of-squares hierarchy and propose some possible extensions. Overall, our paper gives a complete description of exact inference in graphs from the degree-4 sum-of-squares hierarchy and describes its efficacy in solving a range of problems.

Summary: Genome-to-genome comparisons require designating anchor points, which are given by Maximum Exact Matches (MEMs) between their sequences. For large genomes this is a challenging problem and the performance of existing solutions, even in parallel regimes, is not quite satisfactory. We present a new algorithm, copMEM, that allows to sparsely sample both input genomes, with sampling steps being coprime. Despite being a single-threaded implementation, copMEM computes all MEMs of minimum length 100 between the human and mouse genomes in less than 2 minutes, using less than 10 GB of RAM memory. Overall, our analysis sheds light on important aspects related to solvingunitequations which are crucial when studying ring-theoretic concepts.

Сеntrаl tо thе mоdеl's suссеss іs а nоvеl аttеntіоn gаtіng mесhаnіsm, whісh wе соndіtіоn wіth аdvеrsаrіаl sіgnаls tо асt аs а shаре рrіоr, rеsultіng іn bеttеr оbjесt lосаlіzаtіоn аt multірlе sсаlеs. Wе еvаluаtеd оur mоdеl оn sеvеrаl mеdісаl (АСDС, LVSС, СΗΑΟS) аnd nоn-mеdісаl (ΡΡSS) dаtаsеts, аnd wе rероrt реrfоrmаnсе lеvеls mаtсhіng thоsе асhіеvеd bу mоdеls trаіnеd wіth fullу аnnоtаtеd sеgmеntаtіоn mаsks. Sellers of commodities, like gas station owners and refineries, price their product based not on what it costs to produce it, but on what it costs to replace it.', "If you bought some gold for 10, and then the price went up to 20, would you sell it for 10 because that's what you paid for it? No, you'd sell it for the current market price.,the short answer is the information age. the profit on gasoline is tiny, on the order of pennies per gallon, so any retailer that wants to make money has to be constantly monitoring the price of his next shipment and factoring that into his sale price. the supplier that he buys from is also doing the same thing, and all the way back to the refinery. because the internet makes all this price research so easy and fast, we see the fluctuations at the pump every time some refiner or large trader gets twitchy.

Internet of Things (IoT) is the next big evolutionary step in the world of internet. The main intention behind the IoT is to enable safer living and risk mitigation on different levels of life. With the advent of IoT botnets, the view towards IoT devices has changed from enabler of enhanced living into Internet of vulnerabilities for cyber criminals. IoT botnets has exposed two different glaring issues, 1) A large number of IoT devices are accessible over public Internet. 2) Security (if considered at all) is often an afterthought in the architecture of many wide spread IoT devices. In this article, we briefly outline the anatomy of the IoT botnets and their basic mode of operations. Some of the major DDoS incidents using IoT botnets in recent times along with the corresponding exploited vulnerabilities will be discussed. We also provide remedies and recommendations to mitigate IoT related cyber risks and briefly illustrate the importance of cyber insurance in the modern connected world.

> Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, which aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image. Recent advances in deep learning have led to significant improvements in semantic segmentation. However, most existing methods rely on the image itself as the only source of information, ignoring the contextual information that can be extracted from the surrounding environment. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to semantic segmentation that leverages contextual information beyond the image. Our method uses a transformer-based model to extract contextual information from the surrounding environment and incorporates it into the segmentation process. We evaluate our method on the Cityscapes and ADE20K datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both datasets. Our method is also more robust to changes in the environment, such as weather conditions and lighting. We believe that our approach can be applied to other computer vision tasks that require contextual information, such as object detection and image captioning. The paper is available here.

Tom was in a rock band. They were going to be inducted into the rock and roll hall of fame. Tom got into some really bad legal trouble right before they went to break up for good. He had his own apartment, he had this little dog that he loved very much. The night before he goes to jail he is packing all of these things. And I remember thinking how sad it was because this poor man's life has come down to only having what will fit into this little suitcase. I knew then, even though it wasn't my story - I didn't see him for many years after that - but something inside me said: "That sounds like my brother. That sound like my family. What if you packed everything away? Would that make your life better or would it just leave you with nothing?" It made me rethink about my relationship with money as well. We don't talk enough about our money issues so we wind up being broke later on in life because we never opened those doors and looked at where our money was coming from. In this study, we present a novel approach called Points2Polygons (P2P) that enables accurate image segmentation using weak polygonal labels as inputs. Our method is based on adversarial networks and can handle noisy and imprecise label distributions by leveraging contextual information during training and inference. Specifically, our framework consists of two modules: first, an encoder converts 3D point cloud data into feature vectors; second, decoders map these feature vectors back into polygonal shapes while preserving contextual details using conditional GANs. By combining multiple iterative cycles of predictive modeling and adversarial refinement, P2P produces highly accurate segments with minimal human intervention. Evaluations show state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of our method for handling challenging scenarios such as occlusion, clutter, and complex geometries.

Biological evolution requires that selection act upon morphodynamic features, like morphological diversity in feathers or beak morphology and density in birds. Evolutionary biologists need to predict where a species evolved under different environmental conditions with sufficient accuracy for their predictions to be used in population genetics studies. Some species have an intrinsically variable feature (like plumage or beaky texture) and other species have discrete features that tend to go together. These natural variables provide good evidence about past environments, but as predicted by dynamic systems theory they are also constrained by ecological constraints, which leads them to vary independently. To deal with this inconsistency one has to resort to a second-order parameterization of natural variabilities [i.e., probabilistic regularities]. This is useful to obtain testable predictions about how populations should evolve when there is not uniform variance in the covariates at generation time given evolutionary history [Gottola, 2001; Hirth et al., 1998] [see also McComb et al., 2008], so we decided to formulate a formal model [McComb et al., 2008b], specifying how a general system generates two variants for a system's state at generation time: one based on the actual values of covariate covariance or correlation at this particular point, another based only on observable covariance to estimate future values. Here, this corresponds to finding two distributions of posterior values over some continuous range from 1 to some critical value. We show our approach applies to a wide variety of experimental problems, including stochastic genetic drift, mutation and recombination processes, and gene conversion experiments performed with natural populations growing or dying, thus providing strong theoretical support for its use in the real world. Our method also allows identification of important patterns in observed variation over a space of models, thereby allowing a prediction for many cases in which we cannot find statistically significant trends. For example, if an experiment shows some species tending more towards low frequencies then a general tendency to increase variance must exist, even though it is impossible to say wether there actually exists such a trend. By combining our statistical results with data describing evolutionary dynamics during evolution, we can learn which traits could possibly produce this kind of pattern and the kinds of questions we ought to ask to study these features. In conclusion, our framework allows us to derive robust and flexible methods for estimating ancestral states with both quantitative precision and computational resources enabling

Fear of spiders is a survival trait written into our DNA, researchers have discovered. Dating back hundreds of thousands of years, the instinct to avoid arachnids developed as an evolutionary response to a dangerous threat, the academics suggest. It could mean that arachnophobia, one of the most crippling of phobias, represents a finely tuned survival instinct. And it could date back to early human evolution in Africa, where spiders with very strong venom have existed millions of years ago. Scroll down for video . Researchers say a fear of spiders is a survival trait written into our DNA and dates back thousands of years, Stock photo . Study leader Joshua New, of Columbia University in New York, said: 'A number of spider species with potent, vertebratespecific venoms populated Africa long before hominoids and have co-existed there for tens of millions of years. 'Humans were at perennial, unpredictable and significant risk of encountering highly venomous spiders in their ancestral environments. 'Even when not fatal, a black widow spider bite in the ancestral world could leave one incapacitated for days or even weeks, terribly exposed to dangers,' he told the Sunday Times. The research team carried out an experiment in which 252 volunteers were asked to study computer screens containing abstract shapes and data. Their reactions to images of spiders were very fast, even if their shape was distorted, when compared to much more clear images of other objects known induce disgust or fear, such as needles and flies. The researchers point out that spiders are often small dark creatures that tend to hide in recesses and are hard to spot. Dr New said: 'Detection, therefore, is the critical arbiter of success in such encounters - any improvements to the sensitivity, vigilance, reliability and speed of faculties for their detection would have been of significant selective advantage.' The film focuses on the journey of two long-lost siblings who reunite under unexpected circumstances only to discover that they share more than just biological ties. Despite the presence of cliched themes, the movie's storyline excels due to its artful blend of humor, heartwarming moments, and intricate family dynamics. The script is quite well-written, with witty one-liners and realistic dialogue that heighten the film's charm. The lead actors, Emma Thompson and Hugh Grant, deliver convincing performances as siblings whose emotional connection develops organically on screen. Their undeniable chemistry elevates the film and allows the viewer to truly immerse themselves in the story. "Soothing Serenity" also excels on the technical front, with breathtaking cinematography that captures the picturesque countryside. The use of subtle musical scores complements the narrative, balancing moments of tension and reprieve. The one area where the film falters is in its pacing, which tends to oscillate between a slow, introspective approach and brisk action sequences. However, this is a minor flaw in a film that ticks most of the boxes. Ultimately, "Soothing Serenity" is a feel-good, engaging movie that will resonate with viewers searching for an entertaining and thought-provoking experience. A definite must-watch for fans of the genre, and a testament to the notion that not all family dramas need to be riddled with heartache and despair.

This article describes a new spectral engineering method by a combination of cavity-laser-cavity devices, which enables one to actively control the splitting of a resonantly excited resonant cavity. By varying the coupling of the cavities, we are able to show a precise control of the emitted spectrum, which may have implications for the control of light-matter interaction in areas such as quantum information or ultra-precise spectroscopy. Our work contributes to the development of photonics by allowing one to design, with relative ease, an optical response which is specific to the desired application.

Given a natural language expression and an image/video, the goal of referring segmentation is to produce the pixel-level masks of the entities described by the subject of the expression. Previous approaches tackle this problem by implicit feature interaction and fusion between visual and linguistic modalities in a one-stage manner. However, human tends to solve the referring problem in a progressive manner based on informative words in the expression, i.e., first roughly locating candidate entities and then distinguishing the target one. In this paper, we propose a Cross-Modal Progressive Comprehension (CMPC) scheme to effectively mimic human behaviors and implement it as a CMPC-I (Image) module and a CMPC-V (Video) module to improve referring image and video segmentation models. For image data, our CMPC-I module first employs entity and attribute words to perceive all the related entities that might be considered by the expression. Then, the relational words are adopted to highlight the target entity as well as suppress other irrelevant ones by spatial graph reasoning. For video data, our CMPC-V module further exploits action words based on CMPC-I to highlight the correct entity matched with the action cues by temporal graph reasoning. In addition to the CMPC, we also introduce a simple yet effective Text-Guided Feature Exchange (TGFE) module to integrate the reasoned multimodal features corresponding to different levels in the visual backbone under the guidance of textual information. In this way, multi-level features can communicate with each other and be mutually refined based on the textual context. Combining CMPC-I or CMPC-V with TGFE can form our image or video version referring segmentation frameworks and our frameworks achieve new state-of-the-art performances on four referring image segmentation benchmarks and three referring video segmentation benchmarks respectively.

The new bill, which would affect digital maps from Google, Apple, and Uber, is facing stiff opposition from campaign groups. It also bans "wrong" information, including disputed international borders. The government said the rules would not create barriers to business if the bill became law. The bill bans all types of geospatial information, maps, raw data or photographs, acquired by any means, including satellite photography. Offenders could be fined up to 1bn rupees (PS10.4m). It also requires anyone who has already gathered such information to apply for a licence to keep it. It was designed to regulate both the creation and distribution of geospatial information in India "which is likely to affect the security, sovereignty and integrity" of the country, the Ministry of Home Affairs said. Critics say the definition of geospatial data is so wide it could include printed maps, world atlases, or depictions of the country in international magazines imported to India. The proposed law is likely to cause problems for Apple and Google's map products, as well as services offering "value added" geolocation services, such as taxi-hailing app Uber. It is also unclear if companies such as Google would have to go through a separate vetting process every time they updated their satellite imagery - a process that takes up to three months. There is an exemption for government agencies and departments. Google already offers slightly altered versions of its maps inside India, eliminating the Line of Control that divides Indian-controlled and Pakistan-controlled Kashmir and locating the whole disputed region within India's borders. Both Google and Uber declined to comment. The laws extend beyond large international companies. Anyone creating, distributing, or owning unsanctioned maps must apply to a government agency for a licence, and submit the material for inspection. The geospatial data will then be considered by a security vetting committee, which will decide if the applicant is granted a licence. Once the material is cleared, it must be watermarked with the insignia of the vetting authority. "It's only a draft proposal before the country," the Minister of State for Home Affairs, Kiren Rijiju, said in a tweet. "I would appeal not to pass hasty judgment, but put up your suggestions." Speaking to the Economic Times, he said: "It is a general concern being raised that India as a responsible country must have provisions to secure its boundary and territory. "That is why the bill is necessary.

Points2Polygons is a novel approach to context-based segmentation from weak labels using adversarial networks. The model uses a combination of convolutional neural networks and generative adversarial networks to learn the mapping between point clouds and polygonal representations of objects. The model is trained on a large dataset of point cloud annotations and can be fine-tuned on specific tasks or domains. In this paper, we propose novel approach for weakly supervised image segmentation using inter-extreme points geodesics. Our method leverages geometric properties of inter-extreme points to learn a mapping between the input image and a set of labeled images. We use this mapping to generate segmentation masks for input image without requiring any explicit supervision. Our approach is based on idea of using geodesics to find the shortest path between two points in a manifold. We extend this idea to context of image segmentation by defining manifold of labeled images and finding shortest path between the input image and set of labeled images. We use this path to generate a segmentation mask for the input image. Our approach is weakly supervised, meaning that we only require a small number of labeled images to generate accurate segmentation masks. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and speed.

As she set the groceries down on the counter she noticed a note from her daughter. "Dear Mom," it read. "I'm sorry. I've been hiding something from you for some time now. I know I've been happy on the outside, but on the inside every day is torment. Please know that none of this is your fault. You are a wonderful mother and I love you very much." "I've been holding onto this secret for far too long and it's time to let go. Things in my life have just gone from bad to worse. I can't deal with this anymore. Something has happened, something you must never know about. Please don't look for answers. The pain and suffering is just too great. I don't want to live anymore. I'm sorry. I love you." Signed, "Clarissa" She threw down the letter and ran to her daughter's room. Swinging the door open she saw Clarissa lying on her bed, eyes closed, and an empty bottle of pills spilling from her hand. "God no!" she screamed as she ran to the bed. Holding her daughter in her arms she looked down with tears streaming from her eyes and wondered how God could take such a wonderful and beautiful girl from this world. Clarissa opened her eyes, sat up, and with a big bright smile exclaimed, "Just kidding! I'm pregnant."

This paper presents a detailed analysis of exact inference in graphs based on a degree-four hierarchy of partial least squares. The authors begin by reviewing basic notions and results from the graphical modeling literature such as marginalization, variable elimination, and Markov blankets. They then present moment sequences, which are polynomials with coefficients that encode statistical properties of interest, and they show how moment sequences can be used to design efficient algorithms for graph enumeration problems such as consistency checking and finding the most probable explanation for a given probability measure (e.g. maximum likelihood). Finally, they illustrate their approach with examples ranging from known trees to real data with little prior information about either topology or node properties (e.g. the attribute of the nodes or edges). Using recent results from other areas of mathematics, especially algebra but also computer science, combinatorics, control theory, numerical analysis, spin systems, stochastic processes, and other areas that touch statistics and probabilistic signed measures (a field that aims to provide a rigorous foundation and self-contained set of ideas to be used to advance research methodology in pure and applied mathematics, somewhat analogous to formal methods for the design of programs and systems). Hence, we can expect to see a growing number of applications in this interesting and emerging field, especially in the areas of machine learning, pattern recognition, and in general in any number of complex systems with interdependencies among many variables where classical methods are insufficient to easily handle the complexity of the problems at hand, even though they are well known to experts in these fields.

Picture segmentation is a crucial issue in medical image research. recent developments in deep learning have demonstrated promising outcomes on various clinical image segmentation benchmarks. Unfortunately, due to wide differences in biological images (different modalities, image settings, objects, noise, etc), to provide deep learning on a new application, it also needs a new set of training data. This can incur a good deal of annotation effort and expense, because only biomedical researchers can annotate effectively, and sometimes there are too few instances in images (e.g., cells) to annotate. In this paper, we aim to address the following question: With limited effort (e.g., time) for annotation, what instances should be annotated in order to obtain the highest performance? We present a deep active learning methodology that uses fully convolutional network (FCN) and active learning to dramatically improve annotation effort by giving judicious recommendations on the most efficient annotation areas. We use uncertainty and similarity information obtained by FCN and develop a generalized version of the optimal set cover problem to identify the most representative and uncertain areas for annotation. Extensive studies utilizing the 2015 MICCAI Gland Challenge database and a lymph node ultrasound image segmentation dataset demonstrate that, using annotation suggestions by our method, state-of-the-art segmentation efficiency can be attained by utilizing only 50% of training data.

This paper proposes a novel approach to learning versatile neural architectures by propagating network codes. The method involves encoding the weights and architecture of a pre-trained neural network into a compact binary code, which is then used to initialize the weights and architecture of a new network. This allows for efficient transfer of knowledge between networks, enabling the new network to learn complex tasks with minimal data and training time. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments on a variety of tasks, including image classification, object detection, and language modeling. The results show that the learned architectures are highly versatile and can acheive state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of tasks.

However, this overhead is often neglected, and recently proposed segmentation architectures rely heavily on the availability and fidelity of ground truth labels to achieve state-of-the-art accuracies. Failure to acknowledge the difficulty in Creating adequate ground truths can lead to an over-reliance on pre-trained models or a lack of adoption in real-world applications. We introduce Points2Polygons (P2P), a model Which makes use of contextual metric learning techniques that directly addresses this problem. Points2Polygons performs well against existing fully-supervised segmentation baselines with limited training data, despite using lightweight segmentation models (U-Net with a ResNet18 backbone) and having access to only weak labels in the form of object centroids and no pre-training. We demonstrate this on several different small but non-trivial datasets. We show that metric learning using contextual data provides key insights for self-supervised tasks in general, And allow segmentation models to easily generalize across traditionally label-intensive domains in computer vision.

This research investigates cross-modal progressive comprehension, a process that involves understanding and interpreting visual information by combining it with linguistic cues. The aim of this study is to develop an algorithm capable of referring segmentation in natural language processing (NLP) tasks. Using state-of-the-art machine learning models such as deep neural networks, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), long short term memory(LSTM)and other tools from computer vision we analyze image data sets like MS COCO dataset which contain segmented objects along side captions. We evaluate our approach on various metrics including Accuracy & Recall rate which show significant performance improvement over baseline methods. This suggests that using both modalities together can enhance object recognition accuracy leading towards better NLP results specifically while dealing text based problems regarding Image captioning,Visual Query etc where localization plays important role.

The journal "CHASE: Robust Graphic Track through Cell-Level Differentiable Brain Infrastructure Search" introduces a novel approach to visual track that uses a differentiable neural architecture search (DNAS) approach to improve the tracking efficiency. The proposed approach, called CHASE (Cell-Level Hierarchical Architecture Search for Efficient Tracking), provides a hierarchical design search approach to find the optimal architecture for visual tracking. The search is done at the cell level, providing for the discovery of a wide search space and the identification of the most powerful architectural elements. The resulting design is then trained using a comprehensive visual tracking dataset, resulting in improved tracking efficiency compared to state-of-the-art technologies. The paper therefore provides an assessment of the efficiency of the various architectural systems and shows the sensitivity of the proposed approach to variations in the tracking environment. Overall, the paper shows the potential of DNAS for enhancing the efficiency of visual tracking environments.

In this study, we present a novel approach called Points2Polygons (P2P) that enables accurate image segmentation using weak polygonal labels as inputs. Our method is based on adversarial networks and can handle noisy and imprecise label distributions by leverageing contextual information during training and inference. Specifically, our framework consists of two modules: first, an encoder converts 3D point cloud data into feature vectors; second, decoders map these feature vectors back into polygonal shapes while preserving contextual details using conditional GANs. By combining multiple iterative cycles of predictive modelling and adversarial refinement, P2P produces highly accurate segments with minimal human intervention. Evaluations show state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of our method for handling challenging scenarios such as occlusion, clutter, and complex geometries.

In this work we propose an innovative approach to machine learning models that utilizes geometry as a feature to improve classification efficiency of deep neural systems. Next, creating a small database consisting of 150000 binary images containing 2 classes each, we perform a set-up phase on the entire training data (40000 samples) and analyze the effect of adjusting the geometry. Next, this data was used through multiple iterations to find new picture segmentations for 5 distinct picture categories that have been identified with 3 classes (binary, black/white, and color). During validation, the proposed representation learned from our set up phase yielded class labels corresponding roughly 98% of the time. In addition we demonstrate substantial changes in precision by rewinding our analysis phase during gradient stepwise optimization using gradient descent at each iteration. The capability to rapidly systematically update parameter parameters improves efficiency in both predictive and prediction functions when training deep neural network systems. Our findings show that spatial complexity, or non linearity can significantly influence the degree to which a network will outperform more conventional methods and often indicate how important certain geometric features within the same category can be—either independently or simultaneously.

This paper aims to investigate nonsolvable finite groups and their commutator group orders. The main result in this article is that if a finite group has order pq, where p and q are odd primes, then its centre must be contained within H1(G;Zp) and the order of H2(G;Zp), denoted by m, can only take one of three values: 8, 4p-3 or (6 - (-5 + sqrt(-7))/sqrt2)/2. To prove this theorem, the authors use several techniques such as computing the number of subgroups, elementary divisors and using Cauchy's theorem to find elements of order q-1. They also give an example of a group which does not have characteristic two but satisfies all conditions of the above theorem.

We study the problem of learning a real-valued function that satisfies the Demographic Parity constraint. It demands the distribution of the predicted output to be independent of the sensitive attribute. We consider the case that the sensitive attribute is available for prediction. We establish a connection between fair regression and optimal transport theory, based on which we derive a close form expression for the optimal fair predictor. Specifically, we show that the distribution of this optimum is the Wasserstein barycenter of the distributions induced by the standard regression function on the sensitive groups. This result offers an intuitive interpretation of the optimal fair prediction and suggests a simple post-processing algorithm to achieve fairness. We establish risk and distribution-free fairness guarantees for this procedure. Numerical experiments indicate that our method is very effective in learning fair models, with a relative increase in error rate that is inferior to the relative gain in fairness.

In this paper, we present a novel approach to weakly-supervised semantic segmentation using motion cues. Traditional methods of semantic segmentation rely on heavily annotated datasets, which are time-consuming and expensive to create. In contrast, our method leverages the temporal information present in video data to infer pixel-level labels without requiring explicit annotations. We propose a two-stage framework that first generates region proposals using state-of-the-art object proposal network. These proposals are then used to extract spatial and temporal features from the video frames, which are fed into classification model to predict label of each region. The model is trained using large dataset of unannotated videos, and the learning process is guided by weaklabeling scheme that encourages the model to produce accurate predictions for regions with high motion coherence. Our experiments show that our proposed method outperforms existing weakly-supervised semantic segmentation approaches on several benchmarks. We also demonstrate its effectiveness in realistic scenarios where annotated data is scarce or difficult to obtain, such as autonomous driving and robotics. Our results indicate that weakly-supervised semantic segmentation using motion cues has great potential for applications where labeled data is limited or hard to acquire.

Abstract – Based on numerical simulations of the theory of Lorentz manifolds based on simple analytic functions, these results also provide first-ever empirical proof that in some cases such functions become approximations to a complete model of Einstein gravity regime and yield approximate realizations of classical nonlocal space parameters based upon Newtonian gravitational waves. This property has major implication (that was never suspected by any previous researchers) - and is at once main contribution the result and its practical applications with special reference in relativity physics have to offer: fact that we can still derive realistic solutions to problems which the theories of general relativity and quantum gravity make so difficult if they are not at least partially reduced to Lorentzian spacerias and simplices may well open new ways to understand physical phenomena which seem hard to be understood otherwise. We do say somewhat provocative stuff there, but you should take it this way when our method (theoretical and numerical) and results were published last week: we have been right about an absolute, long overdue time. We hope that this work will stimulate additional interest for more rigorous, independent, comprehensive and theoretically compelling applications of Lorentzians and spacerias in various fields that make use of them, i.e., gravitational wave propagation, fluid dynamics etc. And that it will encourage further theoretical studies of this type which might lead someday soon to something more substantial than what is possible here.

The 34-year-old Sweden striker's contract with the French champions expires in the summer, and he has been linked with Manchester United, Los Angeles Galaxy and AC Milan. "I am very proud," he said. "I came like a king, I leave like a legend but I will be back." PSG said Ibrahimovic leaves as "the greatest striker and one of the very best players in the club's history." Ibrahimovic is the club's record goalscorer despite only joining the club in 2012, his 152 goals coming in 178 appearances. PSG have won Ligue 1 in every season Ibrahimovic has been at the club, wrapping up the title this season with two months to spare. "I loved every day I spent here," said Ibrahimovic, who has won league titles with six different clubs. "Paris St-Germain has become a star club in the world and I played a key role moving it forward. It is now the right time for me to take a different path." PSG host Nantes in Ligue 1 on Saturday before meeting Marseille in the French Cup final on 21 May. An agreement is in place for Ibrahimovic to return to the club at the end of his playing career, with PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi saying he is "looking forward to the prospect of working with him again." Ibrahimovic finished as top scorer in France in 2012-13 and 2013-14, and leads Lyon's Alexandre Lacazette by 15 goals this season. He has also been included in the Ligue 1 team of the year in all of his four seasons in France.

Risk of in-hospital ischemic stroke with MI is closely tied to the time to revascularization with both thrombolytic and percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty therapies. Early revascularization is independently predictive of a lower risk of ischemic stroke, but the mechanism of this does not appear to be related to improved cardiac function. The records of 45,997 subjects who received thrombolytic therapy and 47,876 patients who were treated with primary percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty for myocardial infarction were analyzed to determine the relationship between time to revascularization and the occurrence of ischemic stroke. A statistically significant linear relationship between time to revascularization therapy and risk of in-hospital ischemic stroke was seen on univariate analysis. A multivariate model incorporating 26 other variables showed thrombolytic therapy within 15 minutes of presentation was associated with a lower risk of ischemic stroke, and angioplasty within 90 minutes was similarly associated with a nonsignificant trend toward lower stroke risk.
