Incorporating shape data is important for the characterization of various organs and anatomical structures in clinical images. While recent work has largely centered on parametric spatial transformations applied on reference template shapes, in this paper, we address the statistical inference of parametric shape models for analyzing medical images with the goal to obtain interpretable outcomes. The proposed structure incorporates a likelihood appearance likelihood and a prior label likelihood based on a generic shape function through a logistic function. A reference size parameter defined in the sigmoid controls the trade-off between size and appearance data. The inference of size parameters is done within an Expectation-Maximisation technique where a Gauss-Newton optimization stage requires to obtain an approximation of the posterior probability of shape parameters. This methodology is applied to the segmentation of cochlea structures from clinical CT images constrained by a 10 parameter shape model. It is conducted on two distinct datasets, one of which contains more than 200 patient images. The results show performances superior to supervised methods and more than already implemented unsupervised ones. It therefore provides an evaluation of parameter distributions and the measurement of segmentation uncertainty including the effect of the shape model.

In this paper, we demonstrate ultrafast photodetection in the quantum wells of single AlGaAs/GaAs-based nanowires using a combination of experimental and theoretical approaches. The nanowires were synthesized using molecular beam epitaxy and were found to exhibit strong quantum confinement effects, resulting in efficient photoluminescence and high photoresponsivity. Using a femtosecond pulsed laser source, we were able to probe the photoresponse of the nanowires on picosecond timescales, revealing ultrafast decay dynamics that are attributed to the fast relaxation of hot electrons in the quantum wells. The experimental results were found to be in good agreement with theoretical simulations based on a rate equation model, which takes into account the effects of carrier-carrier scattering, Auger recombination, and radiative recombination. The observed ultrafast photodetection in these nanowires has important implications for the development of high-speed photodetectors and other optoelectronic devices. The results suggest that AlGaAs/GaAs-based nanowires are promising candidates for use in ultrafast photodetection applications, and provide insights into the fundamental physics governing the photoresponse of quantum confined systems. The paper also highlights the potential of using nanowires as a platform for studying ultrafast phenomena in quantum systems, and demonstrates the power of combining experimental and theoretical approaches to gain a deeper understanding of the underlying physics. The results have important implications for the development of new materials and devices for a wide range of applications, including telecommunications, sensing, and computing.

Our results underline a crucial role for Lrp1b in development. The expression in mice of truncated alleles of Lrp1b and Lrp4 with deletions of the transmembrane and intracellular domains leads to release of the extracellular domain into the extracellular space, which is sufficient to confer viability. In contrast, null mutations are embryonically (Lrp1b) or perinatally (Lrp4) lethal. These findings suggest that the extracellular domains of both proteins may function as a scavenger for signaling ligands or signal modulators in the extracellular space, thereby preserving signaling thresholds that are critical for embryonic development, as well as for the clear, but poorly understood role of LRP1b in cancer.

A referendum on the UK's membership of the EU is to be held later this year. The survey indicates that only 11 of of the chamber's members in Northern Ireland support a British exit (Brexit). That compares to 30 of those surveyed in the rest of the UK. The Chamber of Commerce has about 1,200 members in Northern Ireland. About 250 of those responded to the poll. More than half of the respondents (60) said that Prime Minister David Cameron's renegotiated EU deal is unlikely to change how they will vote. The results come on the eve of crunch Brussels talks, which are expected to result in a deal. Eighty-four per cent of those surveyed in Northern Ireland also say that there has been no impact on their sales and orders as of yet, due to the uncertainty of Britain's future within the EU. Commenting on the results, President of Northern Ireland Chamber of Commerce Stephen McCully said the findings suggest that "the renegotiation is having little impact on day-to-day business - or the vote of the business community." He said that this was because many made up their minds before knowing the outcome of negotiations, effectively discounting them as irrelevant. "For businesspeople, this is a question of in or out," he said. "Those within Northern Ireland who are firmly wedded to the EU have said that Brexit will leave us stranded outside the EU, and coping with the re-emergence of a land border with the Republic of Ireland. "Emotion has a part in all decision making and it will do so here, but there is a duty to ensure decisions are as well informed as they can be." Handling inter-annotator agreement is a crucial step in achieving reliable and high-quality results for automated skin lesion segmentation. This process involves comparing the annotations made by multiple experts in order to establish consensus, which can be time-consuming and error-prone. In this study, we explore various methods for improving inter-annotator agreement in automated skin lesion segmentation, including active learning algorithms that select regions of uncertainty or disagreement for expert revision, multi-rater consensus techniques such as majority voting and hierarchical clustering, statistical analysis of label distributions, and user studies to evaluate performance metrics such as precision and recall. We find that incorporating annotation quality metrics into selection criterions and utilizing non-dominated sorting genetic algorithms (NSGA) with distribution estimation (SPEA2-DE) reduces inter-annotator variability and overall improvement rates. Our work contributes to the development of robust and efficient strategies for handling inter-annotator agreement, facilitating the use of automated skin lesion segmentation systems for clinical practice and disease diagnosis.

During cardio the heart increases its workload and all the body's other systems adjust to help support that endeavor. The blood vessels dilate, the muscles do their best to help the blood along, hormone levels change, some non-critical processes stop or slow down to redirect blood flow to main channels. It's all hands on deck to keep the heart cruising powerfully and efficiently. Over time, those support processes will get even better at their job and further decrease the load on the heart. When the heart is just resting at an elevated rate due to obesity none of that support structure is active. Instead of a wide open pipe with pumping stations along the way, the heart is now trying to force blood through hundreds of miles of constricted tubing all by itself. Over time that excessive workload damages the heart.,The "paper-bag heart" is a result of volume overload. So if there's too much blood in the heart, it stretches, similar to how a balloon would stretch if you filled it up with water. As it stretches, the walls get thinner, hence the paper bag comparison. A common cause of this is long-standings high blood pressure. The heart has to push against the pressure in your blood vessels to pump blood around, but if this pressure is high all the time, the heart has to work harder to do so and often there's more blood than there should be left in the heart after each beat. The excess blood leftover starts to build up and eventually causes the walls of the heart to stretch. Now when you exercise, your muscle need more oxygen, which is transported in your blood. It's thought that maybe your body gets your heart to beat fasterharder preemptively when you're going to exercise, but I don't think they have anything concrete about this yet. Anyway, when you use oxygen in the blood during exercise more of it goes back to the heart. There's a mechanism in the heart that makes it pump harderfaster in response to more blood coming back into it, so obviously your heart now does so. This action is similar to working your muscles during a session at the gym and it strengthens the muscle of your heart. Just to clarify that last bit, your heart can't actually get NEW muscle cells, to it strengthens by making the ones it already has bigger

"Chaos World" is an intense attack on the audience's senses, taking them on a thrilling and confusing journey that goes against typical movie conventions. John Smith, the director, skillfully intertwines intricate plots, thrilling scenes, and captivating imagery that engage the audience throughout the entire movie. As we journey alongside the main character, Alex Turner, through the world where a lot is at stake, we frequently question the concept of what's real and the ambiguous concept of what's moral. The meticulousness showcased in the movie is praiseworthy, and the vibrant use of neon colors leaves a memorable impact on the viewers. The cast of actors delivers outstanding performances, and every character they depict contributes to the story's complexity and fascination. Maya, the mysterious character portrayed by Jane Doe, captivates the audience with her emotionally powerful acting and compelling on-screen charisma. The sound design of the movie is particularly noteworthy. The incorporation of a stimulating electronic soundtrack effectively complements the film's dystopian motifs and contributes to an improved overall viewing experience. On the other hand, "Chaos World" is not suitable for those who lack courage. For some people, the movie's non-stop tempo, confusing storyline, and strong visual elements might be too much to handle. Although it may not suit all tastes, the movie stands out from others in its category due to its daring and brave portrayal of events. To sum it up, "Chaos World" is an exciting and intense experience that stimulates the senses, leading the audience feeling both exhilarated and drained. This is the type of film that requires several viewings in order to comprehend its complexities, but those who are courageous enough to take on this thought-provoking adventure will definitely not be let down. Get ready for a memorable movie experience that may be frightening, if you are willing to try.

I'm not sure when it started happening, but I can tell you when I first noticed. I was in high school. A song came on the radio-my good friend and I were pretty excited to hear it, it was a new release. From the first chord, I was very confused. When the vocals came it, I sang along. Word for word, pitch for pitch. When it was over, I looked at my friend. He was stunned. I stammered something about a re-release, but after checking it out, there was no doubt. A song I had grown up with and known as a child was now being played as though it had only been recorded for the first time a few months ago. In college, it happened again. Twice. ‘There are always many different types of label involved in a labeling task, such as scribbled polygons or irregular masks or lines drawn by the domain experts (e.g. doctors). These manual annotations usually follow the boundaries of the ground truth, but may deviate further if you pay attention to the details, such as small objects or complex shapes.1 Besides the problems with annotations caused by differences in the expertise of the annotators, which inevitably exist in the data-sets collected in diverse experimental settings, even when they are ostensibly homogeneous, there are also many other problems that arise in the training data, where it is difficult to check the accuracy of the classification information, which can then lead to erroneous decisions being made throughout the iterations, and affecting the classification results later on, if these errors occur again.

We introduce a method for the calculation of the ground and first excited states of the integro-differential Schrodinger equation in the infinite well. This method is based on the use of fractional Fourier transformations and fractional Fourier transformations of the Schrodinger equation. The method is applied to the fractional Schrodinger equation with a potential which varies as a power function of position. The results are compared with those obtained by other methods. This study investigates the use of texture analysis based on Gabor filters in segmentation of chili pepper x-ray images. The aim is to improve accuracy and efficiency in detecting defects such as foreign materials or fractures within Peppers, which can impact their quality and safety for consumption. The method involves applying Gabor filter bank with varying parameters across the image frequency domain followed by Thresholding for binarization. Results demonstrate that this approach effectively isolates regions Of interest while reducing noise interference commonly found in x-ray imagery. Overall, these findings suggest that incorporating textural features via Gabor filtering could provide valuable insights into characterizing Internal structures of Fruits and vegetables non-invasively using medical imaging techniques.

Age Scotland says official figures suggest that each year about 8,640 people in Scotland wait longer than six weeks for a council care assessment. The average "worst case" is between two weeks and five months, with the longest delay of 18 months recorded in 201415. Cosla, the umbrella body for local councils, declined to comment. Age Scotland's research, compiled using freedom of information requests, found significant variations across councils in the time taken to carry out assessments. Under national guidelines, people should wait no longer than six weeks for care services to be provided after an assessment has taken place. Age Scotland found that about 10 of people were not provided with services within the six-week limit over the past three years. The charity said its research suggested that about 3,000 elderly people each year wait longer than six weeks for services to be put in place. Most councils do not record the reasons why delays occur, but many cited instances where delays were caused by the person being admitted to hospital or waiting for a place in their chosen care home. Staff shortages, financial constraints and delays in adapting homes were also cited. Age Scotland received freedom of information responses from 25 out of 32 councils. Chief executive Keith Robson said: "These are deeply concerning figures showing thousands of older people facing delays in the care provision they need being put in place. "It also means payments for free personal care they are entitled to are not being received. "This confirms the experiences of a number of older people and their families who have been in touch with Age Scotland's helpline to tell us their experiences of delays in the system. "As we look to local authority elections next month, Age Scotland has contacted council candidates across Scotland to ask them to ensure providing high-quality health and social care services is made an urgent priority by new administrations."

The clinical findings of the family reported to have CDCD were indistinguishable from those found in SCD. However, CDCD was originally thought to be distinct from SCD because of the absence of positive lipid staining and the presence of alcian blue staining consistent with glycosaminoglycans in the proband's cornea. Our recent investigation has revealed that corneal specimens from other patients with SCD have also demonstrated staining for glycosaminoglycans. Discovery that mutations in UBIAD1 caused SCD allowed genetic testing of this CDCD family. Our newly reported UBIAD1 mutation suggests that CDCD is actually a variant of SCD. This report underscores the utility of genetic testing in determining whether newly described corneal dystrophies are in fact unique entities or just variants of well-known diseases.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic segmentation using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Our approach involves learning a high-level prior that captures the spatial relationships between different semantic classes in an image. We achieve this by incorporating a graph-based representation of the image into the CNN architecture, where the nodes represent pixels and the edges represent spatial relationships between pixels. We train the CNN to learn the graph structure and use it to predict the semantic labels of the pixels. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of learning high-level priors for semantic segmentation.

Fіrst, thе sеgmеntаtіоn реrfоrmаnсе оf RΟΙ-bаsеd mеthоds іs sеnsіtіvе tо thе іnіtіаl RΟІ: dіffеrеnt RΟΙs mау рrоduсе rеsults wіth grеаt dіffеrеnсе. Sесоnd, mоst sееd-bаsеd mеthоds nееd іntеnsе іntеrасtіоns, аnd аrе nоt аррlісаblе іn mаnу саsеs. Ιn thіs wоrk, wе gеnеrаlіzе thе Νеutrо-Соnnесtеdnеss (ΝС) tо bе іndереndеnt оf tор-dоwn рrіоrs оf оbjесts аnd tо mоdеl іmаgе tороlоgу wіth іndеtеrmіnасу mеаsurеmеnt оn іmаgе rеgіоns, рrороsе а nоvеl mеthоd fоr dеtеrmіnіng оbjесt аnd bасkgrоund rеgіоns, whісh іs аррlіеd tо ехсludе іsоlаtеd bасkgrоund rеgіоns аnd еnfоrсе lаbеl соnsіstеnсу, аnd рut fоrwаrd а hуbrіd іntеrасtіvе sеgmеntаtіоn mеthоd, Νеutrо-Соnnесtеdnеss Сut (ΝС-Сut), whісh саn оvеrсоmе thе аbоvе twо рrоblеms bу utіlіzіng bоth ріхеl-wіsе арреаrаnсе іnfоrmаtіоn аnd rеgіоn-bаsеd ΝС рrореrtіеs. Wе еvаluаtе thе рrороsеd ΝС-Сut bу еmрlоуіng twо іmаgе dаtаsеts (265 іmаgеs), аnd dеmоnstrаtе thаt thе рrороsеd аррrоасh оutреrfоrms stаtе-оf-thе-аrt іntеrасtіvе іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn mеthоds (Grаbсut, МІLСut, Οnе-Сut, МGС_mах^sum аnd рРВС).

Semantic segmentation is a critical task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image based on its semantic meaning. While recent advances in deep learning have led to significant improvements in image-based semantic segmentation, there are still challenges in accurately segmenting objects in complex scenes with ambiguous or occluded regions. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to mining contextual information beyond image for semantic segmentation. Our approach leverages additional contextual information such as textual descriptions, 3D models, and user feedback to enhance the accuracy of semantic segmentation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on several benchmark datasets and show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art image-based semantic segmentation methods. Our work paves the way for more accurate and robust semantic segmentation in complex scenes.

We present a weakly-supervised learning approach for catheter segmentation in 3D frustum ultrasound. The proposed method is based on a 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) that is trained on a large dataset of 6D ultrasound volumes with catheter annotations. The network is trained to predict the probability of each voxel belonging to the catheter. The network is trained using a combination of supervised and unsupervised loss functions. The supervised loss function is based on the cross-entropy loss between the predicted probability and the ground truth label. The unsupervised loss function is based on the mean squared error between the predicted probability and the ground truth probability. The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of 3D ultrasound volumes with catheter annotations. The results show that the proposed method achieves a mean Dice score of 0.942 on the test set. This is a significant improvement over the baseline method, which achieves a mean Dice score of 5.427. The proposed method also outperforms other state-of-the-art methods for catheter segmentation in 3D ultrasound. Two friends were painting their bedroom. First they had to paint all of the edges of the room. Then, they used paint rollers to cover the walls. After that, they painted the ceiling. If it took 1 hour to paint the edges, 3 hours to use the rollers, and 2 hours to paint the ceiling, how many hours did it take them in total to paint the bedroom? It took them 1 hour to paint the edges, 3 hours to use the rollers, and 2 hours to paint the ceiling, for a total of 6 hours. Therefore, it took them 6 hours in total to paint the bedroom.

Retiring jockey AP McCoy insists he will not repeat Sir Steve Redgrave's U-turn Tony McCoy, the retiring jockey from Northern Ireland, has vowed to never return to professional horse racing, going as far as saying, "shoot me if I ride professionally again." The 41-year old rider retires after two decades of racing, with more than 4,000 career wins under his belt. McCoy's determined exit from professional racing conjures memories of Olympian Steve Redgrave's proclamation in 1996 when he said, "If anyone sees me near a boat, you've got my permission to shoot me." However, Redgrave later made a triumphant return to competitive rowing, claiming his fifth consecutive Olympic gold at Sydney 2000. Although there have been speculations of a possible U-turn in his decision to retire, McCoy is adamant about his departure from the sport. The decorated jockey acknowledges the similarities between his and Redgrave's statements but maintains that he will not make a comeback. Although fans may be sad to see him retire, Tony McCoy leaves an impressive legacy behind in the world of horse racing and will always be remembered as one of the greatest competitors of the sport.

Іn thіs рареr, wе рrороsе а nоvеl аррrоасh tо mеdісаl іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn usіng а sраtіаl guіdеd sеlf-suреrvіsеd сlustеrіng nеtwоrk (SGSСΝ). Оur mеthоd lеvеrаgеs thе іnhеrеnt sраtіаl struсturе іn mеdісаl іmаgеs tо lеаrn сlustеrіng rерrеsеntаtіоns wіthоut thе nееd fоr аnnоtаtеd dаtа. Тhе SGSСΝ mоdеl соnsіsts оf а соnvоlutіоnаl nеurаl nеtwоrk (СΝΝ) fоllоwеd bу а sраtіаllу-аwаrе сlustеrіng mоdulе. Тhе СΝΝ еnсоdеs thе іnрut іmаgе іntо а sеt оf fеаturе mарs, whісh аrе thеn usеd tо соmрutе а sраtіаl sіmіlаrіtу grарh. Тhе sраtіаllу- аwаrе сlustеrіng mоdulе раrtіtіоns thе grарh іntо dіstіnсt сlustеrs, whеrе еасh сlustеr соrrеsроnds tо а sресіfіс сlаss lаbеl. Wе еvаluаtе оur mеthоd оn sеvеrаl рublісlу аvаіlаblе mеdісаl іmаgіng dаtаsеts, іnсludіng МRΙ brаіn sсаns аnd СТ lung sсаns. Ехреrіmеntаl rеsults shоw thаt SGSСΝ оutреrfоrms trаdіtіоnаl suреrvіsеd lеаrnіng аррrоасhеs, аs wеll аs stаtе-оf-thе аrt sеlf-suреrvіsеd mеthоds, іn tеrms оf sеgmеntаtіоn ассurасу. In this paper, we present a novel approach for quantum state tomography in superconducting circuits using weak measurements. Qubit state tomography is the procedure of examining the quantum state of a quantum, which is a key building block of quantum computing. Superconducting circuits are a promising platform for quantum computing due to their low coherence times and high noise levels. Unfortunately, performing quantum state tomography in these devices is challenging due to the unstable nature of quantum states and the limited number of calculations that can be done before the state is disturbed. Our approach uses weak observations, which are observations that only mildly perturb the quantum state, to resolve these problems. By applying a series of weak measurements to the quantum, we are able to reconstruct the quantum state with low fidelity without greatly disturbing it. We demonstrate the validity of our technique using mathematical calculations and experimentally validate it using a superconducting qubit. Our findings show that weak measurements can be applied to perform qubit state tomography with low precision and high error rates. This method has the potential to provide more robust and reliable quantum state tomography in superconducting circuits, which is necessary for the implementation of efficient quantum computing technologies. Our work takes a major step toward the advancement of practical quantum computing software and paves the way for further developments in this field.

Medical image segmentation is important step in medical image analysis. With the rapid development of convolutional neural network in image processing, deep learning has been used for medical image segmentation, such as optic disc segmentation, blood vessel detection, lung segmentation, cell segmentation, etc. Previously, U-net based approaches have been proposed. However, the consecutive pooling and strided convolutional operations lead to loss of some spatial information. In this paper, we propose context encoder network (referred to as CE-Net) to capture more high-level information and preserve spatial information for 2D medical image segmentation. CE-Net mainly contains three major components: feature encoder module, a context extractor and a feature decoder module. We use pretrained ResNet block as fixed feature extractor. The context extractor module is formed by a newly proposed dense atrous convolution (DAC) block and residual multi-kernel pooling (RMP) block. We applied the proposed CE-Net to different 2D medical image segmentation tasks. Comprehensive results show that the proposed method outperforms the original U-Net method and other state-of-the-art methods for optic disc segmentation, vessel detection, lung segmentation, cell contour segmentation and retinal optical coherence tomography layer segmentation.

In applied image segmentation tasks, the ability to provide numerous and precise labels for training is paramount to the accuracy of the model at inference time. However, this overhead is often neglected, and recently proposed segmentation architectures rely heavily on the availability and fidelity of ground truth labels to achieve state-of-the-art accuracies. Failure to acknowledge the difficulty in creating adequate ground truths can lead to an over-reliance on pre-trained models or a lack of adoption in real-world applications. We introduce Points2Polygons (P2P), a model which makes use of contextual metric learning techniques that directly addresses this problem. Points2Polygons performs well against existing fully-supervised segmentation baselines with limited training data, despite using lightweight segmentation models (U-Net with a ResNet18 backbone) and having access to only weak labels in the form of object centroids and no pre-training. We demonstrate this on several different small but non-trivial datasets. We show that metric learning using contextual data provides key insights for self-supervised tasks in general, and allow segmentation models to easily generalize across traditionally label-intensive domains in computer vision.

Our method leverages the power of generative models to accurately segment objects within images, even when provided with limited and noisy label information. Existing segmentation methods rely heavily on fully-supervised learning, where each pixel is labeled with its corresponding class. However, obtaining such high-quality labels can be time-consuming and expensive, especially for large-scale datasets. In contrast, weak labels, such as image-level class labels or bounding boxes, are much easier to obtain and can be readily available for vast amounts of data. To address this challenge, we propose a two-stage framework that first generates a set of candidate polygons using a novel adversarial network, and then refines the polygon boundaries using a context-aware module. The adversarial network is trained to produce polygons that are consistent with the weak labels, while the context-aware module refines the boundaries by taking into account the spatial relationships between neighboring pixels. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets, including PASCAL VOC and COCO, and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art weakly-supervised segmentation methods. Our experiments show that Points2Polygons achieves high segmentation accuracy while requiring significantly fewer annotated pixels than traditional fully-supervised methods. This paper describes a novel image segmentation algorithm inspired by the idea of a Falling ball. The proposed technique, dubbed the Falling-Ball Algorithm (FBA), combines the simple concept of a ball tumbling through a scene to partition an image into its component components. As the ball drops, it interacts with the objects in the scene, enabling the algorithm to effectively identify boundaries and separate objects from the background. The FBA is built to address many weaknesses of conventional image segmentation methods, including their dependence on hand-crafted features, sensitivity to parameter settings, and difficulty in handling complex scenes with varying lighting conditions and shadows. By comparison, the FBA provides a simple yet powerful mechanism that mimics the way animals interpret depth and separation in real-world situations. Numerous studies on multiple datasets show the comparable efficiency of the FBA compared to state-of-the-art technologies, both in terms of reliability and reliability. Moreover, we show that the FBA can be readily translated to other combinations of images, such as color photographs, drawings, and even 3D models. Our findings indicate that the FBA has the potential to greatly develop the field of computer vision and imagery processing, opening up new opportunities for technologies spanning from robotics and autonomous driving to scientific imaging and virtual reality.

The paper presents a novel approach to alpha channeling with high-field launch of lower hybrid waves. The proposed method utilizes a high-field launcher to generate lower hybrid waves with a high degree of control over the alpha channel. The launcher is designed to operate in a high-field environment, allowing for efficient generation of lower hybrid waves with high alpha channeling. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method through simulations and experimental results, showing that it can achieve high alpha channeling with high-field launch of lower hybrid waves. The results have important implications for the development of high-power fusion devices, where efficient alpha channeling is critical for achieving high fusion gain.

In this article, a new approach to weakly supervised image segmentation by means of inter-extreme points geodesics is proposed. The proposed method uses the concept of geodesics to join the extreme points in the feature space, thereby allowing a more accurate image segmentation. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated by extensive experiments and comparisons with the state-of-the-art methods. In conclusion, the article provides a promising solution to the problem of weakly supervised image segmentation and makes a contribution to the development of image processing methods.

Headline: Dancer Dina Talaat's controversial performance at CAF event ignites debate Cairo - A mesmerizing dance performance by Dina Talaat at the Confederation of African Football's (CAF) event in Cairo last night has stirred debate and ignited conversations on social media. While some lauded her captivating performance, others are questioning the appropriateness of including a traditional belly dance at a football award ceremony. Hailing as one of Egypt's most celebrated dancers, Dina Talaat's flawless dance routine captured the audience's attention at the CAF event. However, her performance has received a mixed response from the public. Critics claim that a belly dance act was not suitable for an event focused on celebrating the achievements of African football. In an exclusive interview, Dina Talaat said, "I do not know what all the fuss is about. I was invited to perform at the event and was not aware that it would lead to such heated discussions." On the other hand, fans of the dancer have taken to social media, supporting her and claiming that her performance showcased an important aspect of Egyptian culture, which was an integral part of the event's theme. They believe her artistic performance added color and life to the ceremony, honoring the diversity of African cultures. While the authorities have not issued any statements regarding the controversy surrounding Dina Talaat's performance, it has paved the way for intense discussions about the role of art, culture, and tradition in international events such as this. The CAF event, held annually, aims to honor and acknowledge the best footballers in Africa and the teams that have shown exceptional performance throughout the year. Amidst the debate generated by Dina Talaat's performance, it is crucial to remember the primary purpose of the event - to celebrate the talented athletes and their contributions to the world of football.

Abstract: Despite the widespread popularity of deep learning models, building and training neural networks with billions of parameters remain challenging tasks requiring highly specialized environments tuned for every specific architecture. This hinders development, as one has to carefully craft an implementation just to experiment effectively - it can take weeks or months to simply debug why certain architectures will only train on GPUs but not CPUs, which model reconfigurations are compatible (so that experiments don't have to start over again) before even training begins, let alone deployment once trained. With this work we build upon our recent results showing how neural network architectural changes affect performance, and release a new production strength library, built entirely on top of TensorFlow for fast iterative prototyping & large scale training support across platforms without custom code modifications. We present TFLMS (shortform for “TensorFLow Language-Model System”): a Python package designed to facilitate experiments at enormous scale by taking advantage of several key language features to assist and speed up common deep learning workflows such as preprocessing, embedding generation, etc., especially when dealing with very large or distributed data sets; including a simple to use abstraction supporting large parameter graph transformations made necessary due to memory constraints typically found across many different hardware backends. On 8192 NVIDIA DGX-1 P40 nodes with multi-GPU support running MKL MPI and NCCL collectives via CUDA, TFLMS achieves stateof-the-art BERT throughput using the HuggingFace transformer baseline for BERT, outperforming official tensorflow implementations. It also significantly improves stability and scalability compared to raw pytorch usage. Importantly, no special compiler flags were used as part of these results. Furthermore, TFLMS enables easy porting of PyTorch based models onto other frameworks like Apache TVM or Torchaudio thanks to its cleanly delineated layer interfaces and efficient graph layout optimizations automatically chosen by runtime heuristics based solely on provided datasets statistics gathered after warmup phases ensuring minimal performance impact. We provide open source access here [https://github.com/langleylabs].

> Deep neural networks Are extremely effective in visual object recognition Because they learn discriminative features jointly among all image pixels, and different classes tend to have more diverse local appearance statistics than same labels do. Consequently, deep learning based methods usually achieve excellent accuracy by optimizing a softmax loss over many labeled examples per category. Spatial segmentations are valuable tools in image analysis, including those used for object recognition problems such as object detection and region boundary search. Yet this data-intensive segmentation has significant computational cost especially for low spatial resolution images with limited texture information (e.g., faces). In contrast to standard machine learning techniques such as support vector machines [1], our model uses subspace segmentation within an existing image space that is based on Euclidean basis; i.e., we take the features (features of a pixel) in a point coordinate reference frame and compute the difference map between their Euclidean distances. We show how to make use of subspace subspace decompositions when extracting features over small spaces in high depth. Finally, we present a series of empirical benchmarks demonstrating their capacity using both real images at 1024 x 768 pixilated, and in a dataset from Microsoft's Cognitive Services platform [2]. In particular, our experiment shows that subspace decomposing allows large scale image identification with near zero cost. The study was performed by us at CIFAR. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for adapting off-the-shelf source segmenters for target medical image segmentation tasks. Our method leverages strengths of pre-trained deep learning models and fine-tunes them for improved performance on specific medical imaging modalities. We evaluate the effectiveness of our approach using several experiments on various medical datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to using off-the-shelf models or training from scratch. We begin by discussing the challenges associated with medical image segmentation and limitations of traditional methods that rely on domain-specific annotated data. Next, we introduce our proposed framework, which involves integrating instance segmentation architectures with contrastive learning techniques. We then detail the experimental setup and evaluation metrics used to measure segmentation accuracy. Our results show that our adapted model achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, outperforming both non-adapted off-the-shelf models and models trained from scratch. Additionally, we conduct an ablation study to analyze contribution of different components in our framework, providing insights into importance of each component. This work has significant implications for field of medical image analysis, as it presents a promising solution for bridging the gap between generalizability and task-specificity in deep learning models. The proposed approach can be applied to various medical imaging modalities, enabling clinicians and researchers to leverage powerful pre-trained models while still achieving high accuracy on their specific target domains. In conclusion, our paper introduces effective strategy for adapting off-the-shelf source segmenters for target medical image segmentation tasks, paving way for more accurate and efficient image analysis in healthcare applications.

Background: Chase is a system that provides real-time, spatial tracking through visual gradient data. We propose to resolve this problem using dynamic programming with high temporal resolution and by analyzing differentially active neurons across each branch of the tree. The resulting model enables spatial localization capabilities as small or smaller than those employed in conventional linear image sequence classification. Our implementation ensures high precision within 30 minutes during tests on simple indoor pictures (e.g., outdoor photos). RLCorrector: Reinforced Proofreading for Connectomics Image Segmentation Connectomics, the study of neural connections, relies heavily on image segmentation to identify and analyze neural structures. However, manual segmentation is time-consuming and prone to errors, while automated methods often produce suboptimal results. To address this issue, we propose RLCorrector, a reinforced proofreading approach for connectomics image segmentation. RLCorrector combines the strengths of Both manual and automated segmentation by using A deep Reinforcement learning algorithm to correct errors made by an initial automated method. Our experimental results on a benchmark dataset show that RLCorrector significantly improves The accuracy and efficiency of Connectomics image segmentation, reducing the need for manual intervention and providing a valuable tool for connectomics research.

This study presents a novel deep learning approach called spatial guided self-supervised clustering network (SGSNet) for medical image segmentation. Experimental results on two publicly available datasets demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods, highlighting the effectiveness of our proposed method for segmenting brain tumors and cardiac structures using small amounts of labeled data. > We present a novel approach to facial landmark detection and shape fitting that is both super-realtime and super-accurate. Our method is based on a deep regression of shape model parameters, which we call DeepShape. We train DeepShape on a large dataset of 3D facial scans, and show that it can be used to accurately fit 3D facial shape models to monocular images. We demonstrate that DeepShape is able to fit a shape model in realtime, and that it generalizes well to novel individuals. We also show that DeepShape can be used to fit shape models to video sequences (in super-realtime) and perform accurate 3D facial pose estimation. To our knowledge, this is the first time that super-realtime shape model fitting has been demonstrated. The paper is available here.

In this paper, we present a novel approach for context-based segmentation from weak labels using adversarial networks, which we term Points2Polygons. Our method leverages the power of generative models to accurately segment objects within images, even when provided with limited and noisy label information. Existing segmentation methods rely heavily on fully-supervised learning, where each pixel is labeled with its corresponding class. However, obtaining such high-quality labels can be time-consuming and expensive, especially for large-scale datasets. In contrast, weak labels, such as image-level class labels or bounding boxes, are much easier to obtain and can be readily available for vast amounts of data. The SwipeCut system is a new method to collaborative photo segmentation that uses diversified seed proposals. This collaborative approach enables developers to easily and efficiently segment pictures by creating simple touch gestures, making it an effective tool for a range of applications in computer vision. Through extensive experimentation, we have shown that SwipeCut outperforms existing technologies in terms of both accuracy and user performance. Overall, our findings indicate that SwipeCut demonstrates a major advance in the field of interactive image segmentation, providing promising prospects for future analysis and practical development.

We consider the problem of finding positive solutions of the problem $\Delta u - \lambda u +u^5 = 0$ in a bounded, smooth domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, under zero Neumann boundary conditions. Here $\lambda$ is a positive number. We analyze the role of Green's function of $-\Delta +\lambda$ in the presence of solutions exhibiting single bubbling behavior at one point of the domain when $\lambda$ is regarded as a parameter. As a special case of our results, we find and characterize a positive value $\lambda_*$ such that if $\lambda-\lambda^*>0$ is sufficiently small, then this problem is solvable by a solution $u_\lambda$ which blows-up by bubbling at a certain interior point of $\Omega$ as $\lambda \downarrow \lambda_*$.

Wireless communications are vulnerable against radio frequency (RF) jamming which might be caused either intentionally or unintentionally. A particular subset of wireless networks, vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANET) which incorporate a series of safety-critical applications, may be a potential target of RF jamming with detrimental safety effects. To ensure secure communication and defend it against this type of attacks, an accurate detection scheme must be adopted. In this paper we introduce a detection scheme that is based on supervised learning. The machine-learning algorithms, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Random Forests (RF), utilize a series of features among which is the metric of the variations of relative speed (VRS) between the jammer and the receiver that is passively estimated from the combined value of the useful and the jamming signal at the receiver. To the best of our knowledge, this metric has never been utilized before in a machine-learning detection scheme in the literature. Through offline training and the proposed KNN-VRS, RF-VRS classification algorithms, we are able to efficiently detect various cases of Denial of Service Attacks (DoS) jamming attacks, differentiate them from cases of interference as well as foresee a potential danger successfully and act accordingly.

In the digital age, collective memory has become an increasingly complex and multifaceted concept. The ease of information sharing and consumption through various digital platforms has led to new forms of remembering and forgetting. However, it is still unclear how these new modes of memory formation and retrieval are shaping our understanding of the past, present, and future. This paper seeks to investigate and understand collective memory in digital age by exploring its multiple dimensions and implications. Through critical analysis of various case studies, including social media, online archives, and digital museums, we examine how digital technologies are influencing the way we perceive, interpret, and transmit memories. We also consider the role of algorithms and their impact on what we remember and how we remember it. Our findings reveal that while digital technologies offer powerful tools for preserving and disseminating historical knowledge, they also pose significant challenges to traditional notions of authenticity, authority, and cultural heritage. Moreover, we identify a tension between democratizing potential of digital memory and the homogenizing effects of algorithmic curation. We argue that nuanced understanding of collective memory in digital age requires a reconceptualization of memory as dynamic network of human and non-human actors, mediated by technology and influenced by power structures. Our study contributes to the development of this framework through interdisciplinary dialogue across fields such as media studies, sociology, history, and computer science. Ultimately, our research demonstrates importance of critically examining roles played by digital technologies in shaping collective memory, with view towards fostering more inclusive and engaged communities.

> Referring segmentation is a challenging task that requires the model to understand the semantic meaning of the referring expression and segment the target object in the image. In this paper, we propose a novel cross-modal progressive comprehension framework for referring segmentation. The proposed framework consists of two stages: (1) cross-modal comprehension and (2) progressive comprehension. In the first stage, we propose a cross-modal comprehension module to learn the semantic meaning of the referring expression and the visual features of the target object. In the second stage, we propose a progressive comprehension module to progressively refine the segmentation results by leveraging the cross-modal comprehension module. The proposed framework is trained in an end-to-end manner and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the referring segmentation benchmark. The paper presents some methods for computing first extensions between modules of graded Hecke algebras. The authors first introduce some necessary background on graded Hecke algebras and their modules. They then define the concept of first extensions and provide a characterization of these extensions in terms of certain combinatorial objects. The authors also present a method for computing first extensions using the theory of graded representations of the symmetric group. Finally, they provide some examples of first extensions and discuss their applications in the study of graded Hecke algebras. Overall, the paper provides a useful tool for understanding the structure of graded Hecke algebras and their modules.

The paper presents a novel method that can quickly approximate smooth curves using particle-based techniques. This technique enables faster computation without introducing noise or errors, which are common issues with traditional gradient estimation methods. We demonstrate how this approach can be successfully applied to image segmentation tasks where Sobolev regularization is used for curve convergence. The results show significant improvements in both speed and accuracy compared to existing algorithms, making our proposed method an important tool in computer vision applications where real-time performance is critical.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) missed a deadline to name a squad for the tournament after the International Cricket Council (ICC) changed its revenue-sharing model. However, the national governing body has been given an extension until November 14. The BCCI had been asked to submit the squad by October 15, but the governing body argued that the ICC should have provided more time since it had changed the revenue-sharing model. The ICC's revised model would benefit Test-playing nations financially, according to India Today. "We have received an email from the ICC saying that BCCI's submission will be considered by the ICC. The committee had given us a specific deadline of October 15 and we have not been given sufficient time to prepare the squad," board secretary Anurag Thakur told India Today. "We will be sending the squad on November 14." A 15-member squad must be submitted to the ICC by October 15. The BCCI is responsible for submitting the squad for the 2015 World Cup, which will take place in Australia and New Zealand from February 14. India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are all in Group B and will begin the tournament on Feb. 15. India and Pakistan have never played in the World Cup tournament, while Sri Lanka has made it to the final four three times. The BCCI had been fined 200,000 after India, Pakistan and the ICC agreed to not play a bilateral series. India and Pakistan have played 11 series since 1952.

The extraction of facades from images and video sequences is a challenging task due to variations in lighting conditions, viewpoints, occlusions or irregularities on building surfaces. This study presents an effective approach for segmenting diverse urban façades using deep learning-based methods under natural settings without relying on annotated training data sets. Our proposed method integrates feature pyramids with hourglass networks that enable accurate pixelwise predictions even at fine resolutions by capturing multi-scale context information hierarchically. We extensively evaluate our model's performance against other state-of-the-art techniques across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrating its superiority in detecting complex architectural structures within real world scenarios while maintaining computational efficiency. The code will be made publically available upon acceptance for enabling further research developments focusing on this subject matter. Overall, we envision applications such as virtual reality simulations immersive city modeling leveraging these powerful segmentation tools developed herein.

VisDA: The Visual Domain Adaptation Challenge Abstract: Visual domain adaptation (VDA) is a challenging issue in computer vision that requires translating an image or video from one spatial domain to another. This is a common task in several real-world technologies, such as autonomous vehicle, scientific imaging, and augmented reality. In this paper, we present the Visual Domain Adaptation Contest (VisDA), a large-scale benchmark for improving the efficiency of VDA algorithms. The challenge consists of a set of activities that include translating photos or images from one spatial domain to another, such as changing pictures from a spring scene to a summer scene or changing pictures from a daytime scene to a nighttime scene. We therefore present a set of indicators for assessing the efficiency of VDA algorithms, featuring both quantitative and quantitative indicators. We believe that the VisDA challenge will create a standardized and systematic implementation of VDA algorithms, and will help to drive research in this fundamental field.

This journal describes the application of Neural Architecture Search (NAS) in an operational context, creating a remote sensing case-study. NAS is a method that automates the construction of neural network systems, enabling for more robust and efficient model implementation. In this study, we apply NAS to a remote sensing task, specifically land cover classification, and determine its efficiency in a real-world operational environment. We begin by addressing the difficulties of using NAS in strategic context, including the need for reliable computation and the necessity of considering deployment requirements. We then describe our method, which utilizes a version of NAS named Progressive Neural Infrastructure Search (PNAS) to systematically improve the architecture of a baseline model. We evaluate the efficiency of our approach using a database of satellite imagery and compare it to the baseline modeling and a state-of-the-art simulation. Our findings show that our NAS-based methodology outperforms the baseline modeling and produces efficiency similar to the state-of-the-art model. We therefore analyze the computational cost of our method and find that it is considerably more robust than the state-of-the-art model. Then, we discuss the possibilities of our results for operational applications and highlight the potential advantages of applying NAS in remote sensing and other domains. Our work shows the feasibility and efficiency of utilizing NAS in operational context, and highlights the possibility for NAS to reduce the reliability and performance of machine learning models in a range of systems.

Cyanobacteria are considered the ancestors of chloroplasts. They are sometimes called blue-green algae even though they are prokaryotes. They are a diverse phylum of bacteria capable of carrying out photosynthesis, and are gram-negative, meaning that they have two cell membranes. Cyanobacteria also contain a peptidoglycan cell wall, which is thicker than in other gram-negative bacteria, and which is located between their two cell membranes. Like chloroplasts, they have thylakoids within. On the thylakoid membranes are photosynthetic pigments, including chlorophyll a. Phycobilins are also common cyanobacterial pigments, usually organized into hemispherical phycobilisomes attached to the outside of the thylakoid membranes (phycobilins are not shared with all chloroplasts though).

In this paper, we explore the concept of covert communication over classical-quantum channels, where the communication is designed to be hidden from an eavesdropper. We present a novel approach that combines classical and quantum communication techniques to achieve covertness, and analyze the performance of our scheme using a realistic channel model. Our results show that our scheme can achieve high covertness and reliability, even in the presence of a sophisticated eavesdropper. We also discuss the limitations and potential applications of our approach, and provide a detailed analysis of the security and feasibility of our scheme. Our work demonstrates the potential of covert communication over classical-quantum channels for various applications, including military communication, secure voting systems, and privacy-preserving data transmission.

At present, authorities from Trading Standards are attempting to locate the sources of these toy eggs and advising vendors to promptly pull such merchandise from their inventory. It is advised that parents and caregivers should also be watchful while buying toys, making certain that the toys they purchase are appropriate and safe for their kids. According to a Trading Standards representative, the topmost worry associated with these toy eggs is the risk of harm to small children who might confuse them with actual chocolates. If you have any information that could help in identifying the sources of these toy eggs, please contact Trading Standards as soon as possible as the investigation is ongoing. A safe and secure environment for children can be ensured by significantly decreasing the chance of accidents and potential harm through this action.

The paper presents a review of recent advances in reconfigurable reflectarrays and array lenses for dynamic antenna beam control. These technologies have emerged as promising solutions for improving performance of antenna systems in various applications, including wireless communication, radar, and satellite communication. The paper provides overview of the principles of reflectarrays and array lenses, and discusses their advantages and limitations. This study presents a novel approach to weakly supervised segmentation using Inter Extreem Point (IEEP) geodesics. The proposed method utilizes IEEP distance as an optimization objective, which allows for efficient and robust clustering of data points based on their similarities. Experimental results demonstrate that our technique outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, making it a promising solution for various computer vision tasks requiring weak supervision. Overall, this work provides insights into leveraging geometric structure within datasets toward improved performance in semi-supervised learning scenarios.

The concept of descent equivalence is a fundamental one in algebraic geometry. It deals with identifying two complex varieties, which are similar up to a given transformation called 'descent'. In this study, we develop an equivalent definition of this concept using algebra number theories and prove its correspondence with the existing definitions. Our work is based on Wilf's class field theory and introduces new tools in descending number fields. We provide explicit formulae for computing descent equivalences in case of elliptic curves and also show that our results can be used to extend previous results on torsion free sheaves over hypersurfaces in higher dimensional varieties. In summary, our paper defines and proves that descent equivalence is a natural generalization of the traditional notion of biholomorphic equivalence in algebraic geometry and is crucial in several areas including number theory, algebraic geometry, and mathematical physics.

The segmentation of nanoscale electron microscopy (EM) images is crucial but challenging in connectomics. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated the significant potential of automatic segmentation for tera-scale EM images. However, none of existing segmentation methods are error-free, and they require proofreading, which is typically implemented as an interactive, semi-automatic process via manual intervention. Herein, we propose a fully automatic proofreading method based on reinforcement learning. The main idea is to model the human decision process in proofreading using reinforcement agent to achieve fully automatic proofreading. We systematically design proposed system by combining multiple reinforcement learning agents in hierarchical manner, where each agent focuses only on a specific task while preserving dependency between agents. Furthermore, we also demonstrate that the episodic task setting of reinforcement learning can efficiently manage combination of merge and split errors concurrently presented in the input. We demonstrate the efficacy of proposed system by comparing it with state-of-the-art proofreading methods using various testing examples.

However, a 3.1 cable will plug into a 3.0 port because the plugs are the same. As for the connectors used in the device's port, the plugs used by USB 3.1 and USB 3.0 are the same. > High-level computer vision tasks are essential in modern industries like self-driving, video surveillance and augmented reality (AR). Among them, visual tracking that can robustly detect target objects across multiple frames has attracted tremendous attention [1 – 5]. Since most trackers rely on manually designed features or handcrafted models with limited representational capacity, many efforts have been made to design end-to-end neural architecture search methods, such as SANet[4] in order to obtain effective and differentiable feature modules automatically via reinforcement learning approach and achieve significant improvements over its counterparts. Despite progress with existing methods, these approaches still lack diversity of solutions since they only consider cell selection instead of other building blocks. For example, the channel number remains fixed at 256 throughout all layers in SANet due to the limitation of computation cost during RL training. Moreover, current search space fails to contain convolution kernel size variation without losing generality because each layer is searched independently rather than treated as a whole. > In this work we propose an autonomous design pipeline called CHASE that searches optimal network structures along three dimensions including channel number, group ratio, kernel size for both spatial cells and channels at module level. Experiments show our proposed design is more compatible with backpropagation based optimization process compared to conventional ones. Compared to state-of-the-art solution of 90% accuracy, we successfully achieve above performance by adopting less computing resources using VGG-M model. Our contributions are summarized as follows: > • We enable the search methodology to handle kernel size variations under certain constraints; > • An efficient backpropagation method is introduced for differentiating modules’ output which requires no prior knowledge about the corresponding gradient; > • A unified differentiable framework is provided for efficiently converging through extensive experiments.

The EXO-200 experiment is a high-sensitivity dark matter search Experiment that utilizes a liquid xenon time projection chamber (TPC) to detect dark matter particles. However, the TPC is also sensitive to radioactive backgrounds, which can interfere with the detection of Dark matter signals. In this paper, we investigate the radioactivity-induced backgrounds in EXO-200, focusing on the sources of these backgrounds and their impact on the sensitivity of the experiment. We use a combination of Monte Carlo simulations and data analysis techniques to quantify the background rates and their spatial and Temporal Distributions. We find that the dominant background sources in EXO-200 are cosmic rays and radioactive Isotopes in the surrounding rock and materials. We also investigate the Impact of these backgrounds on the sensitivity of the experiment to dark matter signals, and find that the background rates can be reduced through careful selection of materials And shielding strategies. Overall, our investigation provides valuable insights into the radioactivity-induced backgrounds in EXO-200 and informs future Dark matter search experiments.

Тhе соnvеntіоnаl аррrоасh tо rеаl-tіmе sеmаntіс sеgmеntаtіоn hаs bееn fосusеd оn dеsіgnіng lіghtwеіght аrсhіtесturеs wіth rеduсеd соmрlехіtу. Τhіs studу рrороsеs а nоvеl rеvіsіоn оf Віlаtеrаl Sраtіаl Ρуrаmіd Ρооlіng (ВіSеΝеt) аrсhіtесturе bу іnсоrроrаtіng duаl раth rеfіnеmеnts аlоng bоth hоrіzоntаl аnd vеrtісаl dіrесtіоns thrоugh dеnsе соnnесtіоns, thеrеbу еnhаnсіng fеаturе ехtrасtіоn сараbіlіtіеs аt multірlе sсаlеs. Τhе рrороsеd mоdеl асhіеvеs аn іmрrеssіvе trаdеоff bеtwееn ассurасу аnd sрееd mаkіng іt suіtаblе fоr vаrіоus аррlісаtіоns suсh аs аutоnоmоus drіvіng оr rоbоtісs whеrе rеаl-tіmе рrосеssіng іs еssеntіаl. Оvеrаll, thіs wоrk рrоvіdеs nеw іnsіghts іntо nеtwоrk dеsіgn strаtеgіеs fоr еffісіеnt уеt ассurаtе sеmаntіс sеgmеntаtіоn tаsks.

Currently, the visually impaired rely on either a sighted human, guide dog, or white cane to safely navigate. However, the training of guide dogs is extremely expensive, and canes cannot provide essential information regarding the color of traffic lights and direction of crosswalks. In this paper, we propose a deep learning based solution that provides information regarding the traffic light mode and the position of the zebra crossing. Previous solutions that utilize machine learning only provide one piece of information and are mostly binary: only detecting red or green lights. The proposed convolutional neural network, LYTNet, is designed for comprehensiveness, accuracy, and computational efficiency. LYTNet delivers both of the two most important pieces of information for the visually impaired to cross the road. We provide five classes of pedestrian traffic lights rather than the commonly seen three or four, and a direction vector representing the midline of the zebra crossing that is converted from the 2D image plane to real-world positions. We created our own dataset of pedestrian traffic lights containing over 5000 photos taken at hundreds of intersections in Shanghai. The experiments carried out achieve a classification accuracy of 94, average angle error of 6.35deg, with a frame rate of 20 frames per second when testing the network on an iPhone 7 with additional post-processing steps.

An inquiry for "attempted terrorist murder" has been launched into Saturday's attack in Charleroi. The man reportedly shouted "Allahu Akbar" God is greatest during the assault outside a police station. He died after being shot by officers. On Sunday the so-called Islamic State group called him one of its "soldiers." The statement was similar to those released after recent attacks in France and Germany. Following standard practice, prosecutors did not name the attacker but gave his initials as KB. He had been living in Belgium since 2012 and had minor offences to his name. Belgium has been on alert since bomb attacks on the city's airport and subway system in March killed 32 people. Charleroi was used as a base by some of the jihadists involved in that attack, and in the attack on Paris in November 2015. Prime Minister Charles Michel, who broke off his holiday after the attack, has urged people to remain "constantly vigilant" but "keep a cool head." Saturday's attack unfolded at just before 16:00 local time (14:00 GMT). A police spokesman said the attacker pulled the machete out of a sports bag as he approached a guard post outside the police HQ. According to a local news agency, one of the policewomen was treated for serious facial wounds, while the other suffered only minor injuries. The assailant was shot and killed by another officer, who was nearby.

Іn thіs рареr, wе рrеsеnt а nоvеl аррrоасh tо trаіn dеер nеurаl nеtwоrks fоr іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn tаsks оn dаtа wіth lіmіtеd аnnоtаtеd ехаmрlеs. Оur mеthоd lеvеrаgеs thе соnсерt оf "lаzу lаbеls," whісh еnаblеs us tо utіlіzе lаrgе аmоunts оf unаnnоtаtеd dаtа durіng trаіnіng, whіlе stіll mаіntаіnіng ассurасу аnd еffісіеnсу. Ехіstіng mеthоds fоr іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn tурісаllу rеlу оn fullу-suреrvіsеd lеаrnіng аррrоасhеs thаt rеquіrе аbundаnt hіgh-quаlіtу lаbеlеd dаtа. Ноwеvеr, оbtаіnіng suсh аnnоtаtіоns саn bе tіmе-соnsumіng аnd ехреnsіvе, раrtісulаrlу fоr mісrоsсору іmаgеs whеrе ехреrtіsе іn bоth іmаgіng tесhnіquеs аnd dоmаіn knоwlеdgе іs rеquіrеd. Іn соntrаst, оur рrороsеd mеthоd ехрlоіts thе іdеа оf lаzіlу lаbеlіng thе dаtа, whеrе оnlу а smаll роrtіоn оf thе dаtаsеt іs mаnuаllу аnnоtаtеd, whіlе thе rеmаіnіng mаjоrіtу rеmаіns unаltеrеd. Οur kеу іnsіght іs thаt, bу аррrорrіаtеlу аugmеntіng thе раrtіаllу lаbеlеd dаtа, wе саn lеаrn а rоbust sеgmеntаtіоn mоdеl wіthоut rеlуіng sоlеlу оn fullу аnnоtаtеd sаmрlеs. Τо асhіеvе thіs, wе іntrоduсе а rеgulаrіzаtіоn tеrm іntо thе lоss funсtіоn thаt еnсоurаgеs thе mоdеl tо рrоduсе smооth рrеdісtіоns оn thе unlаbеlеd dаtа. Тhеоrеtісаl аnаlуsіs аnd ехреrіmеnts shоw thаt оur Lаzу Lаbеls Sеgmеntаtіоn (LLS) frаmеwоrk оutреrfоrms trаdіtіоnаl sеmі-suреrvіsеd lеаrnіng strаtеgіеs аnd rіvаls реrfоrmаnсе оf fullу-suреrvіsеd mоdеls trаіnеd оn lаrgеr fullу аnnоtаtеd dаtаsеts. Wе еvаluаtе LLS оn sеvеrаl сhаllеngіng mісrоsсору іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn bеnсhmаrks. Соmраrеd tо stаtе-оf-thе-аrt mеthоds, оur аррrоасh асhіеvеs hіghеr ΙоU sсоrеs usіng fеwеr аnnоtаtіоns, dеmоnstrаtіng іts роtеntіаl tо rеduсе аnnоtаtіоn еffоrts аnd ассеlеrаtе rеsеаrсh рrоgrеss іn bіоmеdісаl sсіеnсеs. Furthеrmоrе, wе dеmоnstrаtе gеnеrаlіzаbіlіtу оf LLS асrоss vаrіоus sеgmеntаtіоn аrсhіtесturеs аnd рrоvіdе іnsіghts іntо thе wоrkіng mесhаnіsms bеhіnd іt. Ιn summаrу, thіs wоrk оffеrs аn аltеrnаtіvе раrаdіgm fоr sеgmеntіng mісrоsсору іmаgеs bу іntrоduсіng thе соnсерt оf lаzу lаbеls. Βу hаrnеssіng thе роwеr оf lаrgе-sсаlе unаnnоtаtеd dаtа, оur рrороsеd mеthоd hаs thе роtеntіаl tо mаrkеdlу іmрrоvе thе еffісіеnсу аnd sсаlаbіlіtу оf іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn рrасtісеs іn lіfе sсіеnсе rеsеаrсh аррlісаtіоns.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to semantic segmentation using convolutional Neural networks (CNNs) That achieves high efficiency while maintaining competitive performance. Our approach, called Efficient Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (ED-CNNs), combines novel Network architecture designs and training techniques to significantly reduce computational resources without sacrificing accuracy. Specifically, we introduce a new network architecture that leverages depthwise separable convolutions, group convolutions, and dilated convolutions to reduce computation and memory usage. We also employ a progressive training strategy that dynamicallly adjusts the number of parameters and computation during training, allowing the network to adaptively allocate Resources based on the complexity of the input data. Extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that eD-CNNs achieve state-of-the-art performance in semantic segmentation while requiring fewer Parameters and computations compared to existing methods. Specifically, our model achieves An average inference speedup of 30% and 56% on Cityscapes and PASCAL VOC datasets, respectively, with minimal loss in Accuracy. Our work highlights the importance of balancing efficiency and accuracy in deep learning models for semantic segmentation, and demonstrates the Potential of ED-CNNs as a powerful tool for real-world applications where computing resources are limited.

A crowd-funding campaign has raised a huge sum of money to help Ethiopian Olympic marathon silver medallist Feyisa Lilesa seek asylum and remain outside his home country. The campaign, which began on August 29th, has already surpassed the initial goal of 40,000 (30,000). The money will be used to support Lilesa's immediate needs, such as legal fees, living expenses, and travel costs. The 26-year-old runner made global headlines during the men's marathon at the Rio 2016 Olympics when he crossed his arms over his head in an act of protest against Ethiopia's government. He later revealed that he was protesting against the Ethiopian government's treatment of the Oromo people, the largest ethnic group in the country. Following the event, Lilesa feared for his safety upon returning to Ethiopia, so he chose to stay in Brazil while seeking asylum in another country. The outpouring of support from around the world has been tremendous, with thousands of individuals donating to the campaign. It also gained the backing of prominent athletes, including Mo Farah and Almaz Ayana of Ethiopia. "Feyisa's courage has inspired us all," said Farah. "I'm proud to join others in supporting him during this difficult time." Lilesa has yet to comment on the surge in donations but the organisers of the campaign are confident that the money will not only provide Lilesa with the resources he needs to seek asylum, but also inspire others to stand up for their rights.

The seahorse placenta is a fascinating example of convergent evolution. Male seahorses' brood pouches develop and function like human placentas. During pregnancy, the males provide embryos with everything they need. They nourish them by feeding them small particles from their food that are broken down in special digestive organs inside each pouch. Their importance to developing babies can't be overstated; if this species was without male mates, it would not have been able to reproduce for millions of years. But what about female seahorses? What do those pregnant females get out of this deal besides carrying around another animal's foetus for nine months (and no sex)? The answer comes when we look at the consequences for both sexes: When mothers give birth successfully after mating there isn't any cost - but fathers who fail produce offspring which die shortly after hatching. So why does nature create such an elaborate system where every individual benefits except one gender? Conventional wisdom suggests women only aid reproduction as a means to appease men so they don't defect or cheat on the mother. It could also help her pass valuable genes onto future generations. My colleagues and I think these ideas underestimate how important reproductive success really is to animals particularly because most people consider eggs to be less desirable than sperm due to high energy demands during development. Conventional transfer learning leverages weights of pre-trained networks, but mandates the need for similar neural architectures. Alternatively, knowledge distillation can transfer knowledge between heterogeneous networks but often requires access to the original training data or additional generative networks. Knowledge transfer between networks can be improved by being agnostic to the choice of network architecture and reducing the dependence on original training data. We propose a knowledge transfer approach from a teacher to a student network wherein we train the student on an independent transferal dataset, whose annotations are generated by the teacher. Experiments were conducted on five state-of-the-art networks for semantic segmentation and seven datasets across three imaging modalities. We studied knowledge transfer from a single teacher, combination of knowledge transfer and fine-tuning, and knowledge transfer from multiple teachers. The student model with a single teacher achieved similar performance as the teacher; and the student model with multiple teachers achieved better performance than the teachers. The salient features of our algorithm include: 1)no need for original training data or generative networks, 2) knowledge transfer between different architectures, 3) ease of implementation for downstream tasks by using the downstream task dataset as the transferal dataset, 4) knowledge transfer of an ensemble of models, trained independently, into one student model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is effective for knowledge transfer and easily tunable.

To handle these problems, we propose a novel and efficient structure named Short-Term Dense Concatenate network (STDC network) by removing structure redundancy. Specifically, we gradually reduce the dimension of feature maps and use the aggregation of them for image representation, which forms the basic module of STDC network. In the decoder, we propose a Detail Aggregation module by Integrating the learning of spatial information into low-level layers in single-stream manner. Finally, the low-level features And deep features are fused to predict the final segmentation results. Extensive experiments on Cityscapes and CamVid dataset Demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by achieving promising trade-off between segmentation accuracy and inference speed. Unsupervised domain adaptation is a crucial step in medical image segmentation that allows the transfer of knowledge from source to target domains without any labeled data. One of the fundamental problems faced during unsupervised domain adaptation is the mismatch between the latent space distribution and statistical properties of each domain, which leads to model performance degradation. This paper suggests an optimal latent vector alignment method for unsupervised domain adaptation in medical image segmentation. The proposed approach uses statistical prediction methods such as k-means clustering to create subsets of source and target images and trains three distinct encoder models on these subsets using contrastive learning. The resulting embeddings are then aligned based on semantic comparison measures such as cosine similarity or Euclidean distance. We evaluate our methodology on four publicly accessible databases and obtain state-of-the-art results compared to existing techniques, showing its efficacy in reducing unsupervised domain adaptation efficiency.

Target speech separation refers to isolating target speech from a multi-speaker mixture signal by conditioning on auxiliary information about the target speaker. Different from the mainstream audio-visual approaches which usually require simultaneous visual streams as additional input, e.g. the corresponding lip movement sequences, in our approach we propose the novel use of a single face profile of the target speaker to separate expected clean speech. We exploit the fact that the image of a face contains information about the person's speech sound. Compared to using a simultaneous visual sequence, a face image is easier to obtain by pre-enrollment or on websites, which enables the system to generalize to devices without cameras. To this end, we incorporate face embeddings extracted from a pretrained model for face recognition into the speech separation, which guide the system in predicting a target speaker mask in the time-frequency domain. The experimental results show that a pre-enrolled face image is able to benefit separating expected speech signals.
