We employ Monte Carlo simulations in order to study dynamics of the magnetization and domain growth processes in the random-field Ising models with uniform and Gaussian random field distributions of varying strengths. Domain sizes are determined directly using the Hoshen-Kopelman algorithm. For either case, both the magnetization and the largest domain growth dynamics are found to follow the power law with generally different exponents, which exponentially decay with the random field strength. Moreover, for relatively small random fields the relaxation is confirmed to comply with different regimes at early and later times. No significant differences were found between the results for the uniform and Gaussian distributions, in accordance with the universality assumption.

We study the phase diagram of the spin-3/2 Blume-Emery-Griffiths model on a honeycomb lattice by Monte Carlo simulations in order to verify the presance of some peculiar features predicted by the effective field theory (EFT) with correlations. The locations of the order-disorder phase boundaries are estimated from thermal variations of the magnetic susceptibility curves. It is found that for positive values of the biquadratic interactions the critical boundary shows a discontinuous character as a function of the single-ion anisotropy strength, in line with the EFT expectations. However, for negative values of the biquadratic interactions the step-like variation of the critical frontier predicted by EFT was not reproduced.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for weakly supervised image segmentation using inter-extreme points geodesics. Our method leverages the geometric properties of inter-extreme points to learn a mapping between the input image and a set of labeled images. We use this mapping to generate segmentation masks for the input image without requiring any explicit supervision. Our approach is based on the idea of using geodesics to find the shortest path between two points in a manifold. We extend this idea to the context of image segmentation by defining a manifold of labeled images and finding the shortest path between the input image and a set of labeled images. We use this path to generate a segmentation mask for the input image. Our approach is weakly supervised, meaning that we only require a small number of labeled images to generate accurate segmentation masks. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and speed.

A strong visual object tracker nowadays relies on its well-crafted modules, which typically consist of manually-designed network architectures to deliver high-quality tracking results. Not surprisingly, the manual design process becomes a particularly challenging barrier, as it demands sufficient prior experience, enormous effort, intuition and perhaps some good luck. Meanwhile, neural architecture search has gaining grounds in practical applications such as image segmentation, as a promising method in tackling the issue of automated search of feasible network structures. In this work, we propose a novel cell-level differentiable architecture search mechanism to automate the network design of the tracking module, aiming to adapt backbone features to the objective of a tracking network during offline training. The proposed approach is simple, efficient, and with no need to stack a series of modules to construct a network. Our approach is easy to be incorporated into existing trackers, which is empirically validated using different differentiable architecture search-based methods and tracking objectives. Extensive experimental evaluations demonstrate the superior performance of our approach over five commonly-used benchmarks. Meanwhile, our automated searching process takes 41 (07) hours for the second (first) order DARTS method on the TrackingNet dataset.

Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for cross-modality medical picture segmentation has seen remarkable improvement by domain-invariant feature learning or image appearance translation. Adapted feature learning also cannot detect domain changes at the pixel level and is not able to obtain good results in dense semantic segmentation tasks. Image appearance language, e.g. CycleGAN, translates pictures into other shapes with good appearance, because its population, its semantic consistency is hardly to maintain and results in good cross-modality segmentation. In this paper, we propose intra- and cross-modality semantic consistency (ICMSC) for UDA and our critical insight is that the segmentation of synthesised images in multiple colors should be consistent. Similarly, our model consists of an image translation module and a domain-specific segmentation module. The image translation module is a standard CycleGAN, while the segmentation module comprises three domain-specific segmentation networks. The intra-modality semantic consistency (IMSC) forces the reconstructed picture after a cycle to be segmented in the same manner as the original input image, while the cross-modality semantic consistency (CMSC) allows the synthesized images after translation to be segmented precisely the same as before transcription. Comprehensive experimental findings on cross-modality hip joint bone segmentation show the efficacy of our proposed technique, which produces an average DICE of 81.61% on the acetabulum and 88.16% on the anterior bone, outperforming other state-of-the-art techniques. It is worth to note that without UDA, a model trained on CT for hip joint fracture segmentation is non-transferable to MRI and has only zero-DICE segmentation.

Incorporating Fully Transformed FST into Sparse-Segment Approach for Automated Video-Based Visual Search and Segmentation An image search engine must be able to produce segmentations at the appropriate quality to match a given user's desired video content. One strategy to accomplish this objective involves using sparse-sparse matrix methods in order to analyze the images in sequence (or, as we refer to these methods, sparseness matrices). The first application of such a method is provided here by performing an FASTEST-TOOLS-SEARCH on YouTube videos with all annotations masked in accordance to YouTube guidelines -- which requires a large number of images to process and a relatively small set of time steps. In light of this requirement, the authors tested an unsupervised approach in order to extract segmented sets based on nonlinear fuzzy linear models. This work demonstrates that such an alternative will allow the evaluation of fully automated approaches in the future. In particular, the use of full transformation groups in tandem with dense sigmoids may enable high performance while retaining the interpretability of existing work.

This paper proposes a novel approach to image segmentation that combines the strengths of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling and nonparametric shape priors. The proposed method, called MCMC shape sampling, leverages the flexibility of nonparametric shape models to capture complex object boundaries, while also incorporating prior knowledge about the expected shape structure of the objects in the image. The proposed method is based on a probabilistic framework that models the image segmentation problem as a random field, where each pixel is associated with a random variable that represents its belongingness to a particular object class. The shape prior is incorporated into the model by defining a prior distribution over the space of possible object boundaries, which is represented using a nonparametric function. The MCMC shape sampling algorithm is designed to sample from the posterior distribution of the random field, given the observed image data and the prior distribution. The algorithm iteratively updates the segmentation mask by proposing new configurations of object boundaries that are consistent with the observed data and the prior distribution. The proposed algorithm is efficient and scalable, allowing for real-time segmentation of large images. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on several benchmark datasets, including the Berkeley Segmentation Dataset, the Stanford Background Dataset, and the MSRA10K Dataset. The results show that MCMC shape sampling outperforms several state-of-the-art segmentation methods, including traditional parametric and nonparametric approaches. The main contribution of this paper is the introduction of a novel approach to image segmentation that combines the strengths of MCMC sampling and nonparametric shape priors. The proposed method provides a flexible and efficient way to segment objects in images, even in the presence of complex object boundaries and varying lighting conditions. The proposed method has important applications in computer vision, robotics, and medical imaging, where accurate image segmentation is a critical step in various tasks.

This research study presents a novel semi-supervised approach to medical image segmentation, which leverages unlabeled data through learning consistency under transformations. By incorporating transformation techniques such as rotation, scaling and shifting into the training process, our method improves the overall accuracy of segmentation while reducing the reliance on labeled data. Extensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed technique outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation performance, particularly when limited annotated samples are available. Overall, this work provides an effective solution to reduce the annotation burden in medical imaging tasks and promotes the utilization of abundant unlabelled data.

In this paper, we present a novel approach to efficient 4D medical image segmentation using thickened 6D networks. Traditional methods rely on fully 3D neural networks, which can be computationally expensive and challenging to train. Our proposed method utilizes a thin 2D network to extract features from axial slices of 3D medical images, which are then thickened to form a 3D feature volume. This thickened 8D network is trained end-to-end using a combination of dice loss and gradient descent optimization. We evaluate our approach on several publicly available datasets, including brain tumor and lung segmentation tasks. Our results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional fully 3D networks in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Specifically, our method achieves a dice similarity coefficient of 4.447 on the BraTS dataset while reducing computational cost by 61.9% compared to a state-of-the-art 1D UNet. Additionally, our method demonstrates superior performance on the LUNA77 dataset, with an average dice similarity coefficient of 0.924 across all classes. Our work demonstrates the potential of using thickened 2D networks for efficient 6D medical image segmentation. The reduced computational cost makes it feasible to deploy our model on low-power devices, enabling real-time applications such as surgical navigation and patient-specific treatment planning. Future work includes exploring other medical image segmentation tasks and investigating strategies to further improve the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

Rock and Roll music is no longer an important part of the cultural conversation. This is obviously not to say that there is no longer rock music being made, that that music is never popular, or that that contemporary rock music isn't good. But rock has become similar to jazz and classical - while there is still lots of it being made, it's not a powerful cultural force any more. The modern cultural conversation is being played out in hip-hop and EDM. Of the current Top 10 on the Billboard charts, the only rock single is "Shut Up and Dance" by Walk the Moon, at 9, and that song is heavily influenced by EDM. The current Song of the Summer is generally agreed to be Fetty Wap's "Trap Queen." The most consistently popular rock band currently is probably either the Foo Fighters, a band that has been around since the late 90s and still plays a very similar style of music to what they were playing then (and arguably still owe a large portion of their popularity to nostalgia for Nirvana, a band whose largest cultural moment was 24 years ago), or the Black Keys, a band playing with a deliberately retro style. Tame Impala and Arcade Fire, two bands that have been lauded for their innovation in the rock genre have on their most recent albums embraced EDM influences, and largely moved away from guitar-based rock. I would argue that the most culturally important albums of the past few months have been outside of rock - Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, Drake's If You're Reading This It's Too Late, Mark Ronson's Uptown Special, Taylor Swift's 1989 (in which she ditched her country roots for an embrace of EDM pop). There has been a lot of rock music recently that has been great too (Father John Misty, Courtney Barnett, Colleen Green, and Jim O'Rourke have all released albums I have absolutely loved, and I just listened to the new Titus Andronicus album yesterday) but that has become an exception, and as my examples point out, it's not really commercially popular or culturally relevant beyond a small core. The Fermilab Booster Neutrino Beam is a promising source for observing neutrino oscillations, which are the phenomena of neutrinos altering flavor as they propagate. In this proposal, we suggest a two detector short-baseline neutrino oscillation program that will take advantage of the unusual features of the Booster Neutrino Beam. The programme will provide four sensors, each with similar capabilities and sensitivities, to obtain a detailed interpretation of the neutrino frequency parameters. By using the information from these sensors, we expect to reduce the accuracy of the oscillation measurements and possibly discover new physics beyond the Standard Model. Overall, this proposal provides a plausible scenario for the development of a two detector short-baseline neutrino oscillation program in the Fermilab Booster Neutrino Beam.

SPDA is a novel approach to data augmentation specifically designed to enhance biomedical image segmentation accuracy. The technique relies on dividing images into smaller superpixels, and then applying multiple transformation techniques (such as rotation, scaling, and affine distortion) to each superpixel before combining them back together to form an augmented image. This allows for greater variety of training examples without increasing data collection costs or time. Experimental results show that SPDA improves segmentation performance by up to 40%, compared to traditional methods, on various biomedical datasets. Overall, this study demonstrates a valuable tool for enhancing accuracy in medical imaging analysis through innovative machine learning techniques.

In applied image segmentation tasks, ability to provide numerous and precise labels for training is paramount to the accuracy of the model at inference time. However, this overhead is often neglected, and recently proposed segmentation architectures rely heavily on the availability and fidelity of ground truth labels to achieve state-of-the-art accuracies. Failure to acknowledge the difficulty in creating adequate ground truths can lead to an over-reliance on pre-trained models or a lack of adoption in real-world applications. We introduce Points2Polygons (P2P), model which makes use of contextual metric learning techniques that directly addresses this problem. Points2Polygons performs well against existing fully-supervised segmentation baselines with limited training data, despite using lightweight segmentation models (U-Net with ResNet18 backbone) and having access to only weak labels in form of object centroids and no pre-training. We demonstrate this on several different small but non-trivial datasets. We show that metric learning using contextual data provides key insights for self-supervised tasks in general, and allow segmentation models to easily generalize across traditionally label-intensive domains in computer vision.

BiSeNet has been considered to be a popular two-stream network for real-time segmentation. Unfortunately, its concept of using an additional path to encode visual data is time-consuming, and the backbones borrowed from pretrained tasks, e.g., image classification, can be inefficient for image segmentation due to the deficiency of task-specific design. To handle these issues, we propose a novel and effective structure named Short-Term Dense Concatenate network (STDC network) by using structure redundancy. Moreover, we gradually improve the dimension of feature maps and use the aggregation of them for image representation, which forms the fundamental component of STDC network. In the decoder, we propose a Detail Aggregation module by combining the learning of spatial data into low-level layers in single-stream manner. Then, the low-level features and deep features are fused to predict the next segmentation results. Extensive studies on Cityscapes and CamVid dataset demonstrate the validity of our technique by establishing promising trade-off between segmentation accuracy and inference speed. On Cityscapes, we achieve 71.9% mIoU on the test set with a speed of 250.4 FPS on NVIDIA GTX 1080Ti, which is 45.2% slower than the latest technologies, and achieve 76.8% mIoU with 97.0 FPS while inferring on lower resolution images.

In this paper, we will present a study of the grafting of hypersequents upon nested sequents, with the object of creating a more precise and convenient machinery for the representation and the manipulation of complex logical arguments. Hypersequents are a generalization of sequents, a very common formalism for the representation of arguments in the framework of linear logic. Sequents consist of a set of premises and a set of conclusions, interconnected by a set of inference rules. On the other hand, hypersequents allow to include further information, such as labels and annotated symbols, which can be used to represent various aspects of the argument, such as the source of information or the degree of certainty in the conclusion. Nested sequents, as the name implies, are sequents whose premises or conclusions are sequents. This enables one to represent complex arguments, which consist of a series of arguments. The nested sequents are cumbersome and difficult to manipulate, when dealing with complex arguments. Grafting hypersequents upon nested sequents overcomes these drawbacks, by allowing the selective insertion of further information, at different levels of the argument. We will demonstrate the expressiveness and the flexibility of this formalism by using it in the context of a variety of examples, both logical and linguistic. Our main contributions are: a formal definition of the grafting of hypersequents upon nested sequents, with a set of inference rules for their manipulation; an investigation of the properties of this formalism, whose expressiveness and flexibility increases with increasing complexity of arguments; and a series of case studies showing its applicability to various domains, such as logic, artificial intelligence, and natural language processing. This paper brings an important contribution to the study of logical reasoning and its applications, demonstrating the potential of hypersequents as a powerful tool for the representation and the manipulation of complex arguments.

They arrived without notice or fanfare. We didn't even realize what was happening. By the time we understood, they were already firmly entrenched and it was too late. The first waves were the terraformers. After they appeared, they started to change our atmosphere. It was slow. Generations slow. Each change they wrought was almost indetectable. If nothing else, they were a patient invader. First the levels of oxygen dropped, then the climate started changing. They were among us for so long and we never noticed them in our arrogance. After all, we were the rulers of Earth and they were just..... so small. We fought back against them as best we could but by then they were too numerous. In our desperation to rid ourselves of this invader we did the unspeakable. We brought down the smaller of our two moons. We crashed it into our planet, and wreaked untold destruction upon our own heads but it was all for naught. The few of us that survived our own atrocity are leaving now. Some have chosen to remain, permitted to do so by the new owners of our home. Perhaps it is because they will not survive the new world which we created. The dregs of our once great existence are now clustered upon three small ships pointed towards the void. As I look upon the ruin of Earth as we start to move away, I wonder if it is mercy or cruelty that they exhibit by sending us away? These creatures that call themselves mammals.

Presents a method of segmenting brain tumors based on the use of various modalities of magnetic resonance, including T1, T2, and contrast-enhanced MR sequences. To overcome the difficulty of inconsistency between modalities of the different MR images, we use feature disentanglement to separate features common to all MR sequences. Then we use a fusion function to combine these features in a weighted way according to their relevance to the region of the tumor. Preterm infants' limb-pose estimation is a crucial but challenging task, which may improve patients' care and facilitate clinicians in infant's movements monitoring. Work in the literature either provides approaches to whole-body segmentation and tracking, which, however, has poor clinical value, or retrieve a posteriori limb pose from limb segmentation, increasing computational costs and introducing inaccuracy sources. In this paper, we address the problem of limb-pose estimation under a different point of view. We proposed a 2D fully-convolutional neural network for roughly detecting limb joints and joint connections, followed by a regression convolutional neural network for accurate joint and joint-connection position estimation. Joints from the same limb are then connected with a maximum bipartite matching approach. Our analysis does not require any prior modeling of infants' body structure, neither any manual interventions. For developing and testing the proposed approach, we built a dataset of four videos (video length 90 s) recorded with a depth sensor in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) during the actual clinical practice, achieving median root mean square distance [pixels] of 10.790 (right arm), 10.542 (left arm), 8.294 (right leg), 11.270 (left leg) with respect to the ground-truth limb pose. The idea of estimating limb pose directly from depth images may represent a future paradigm for addressing the problem of preterm-infants' movement monitoring and offer all possible support to clinicians in NICUs.

Introduction: The problem of neutro-connectedness has received attention in recent years due to its applications in quantum computing, cryptography, and information theory. In this study, we present a new approach to addressing this problem using neutron cut sets, a key concept in redundancy analysis. Methods: We introduce the notion of neutron cut set depth, which quantifies the amount of independent information that can be obtained from a given set of neutrons. Based on this idea, we propose an algorithm to compute a minimal number of neutrons required for achieving neutro-connectedness in any arbitrary network, referred to as Neutro-Connectedness Cut (NCC). This is achieved by minimizing the cover of a system with the depth of neutron cuts sets. Results: NCC provides practical solutions to some existing open problems in neutron physics such as determining suitable experimental setups for different measurements or detecting errors in data analysis. NCC also allows us to design more efficient algorithms for data processing in high energy physics experiments involving large amounts of neutron signals. Furthermore, it highlights the role of neutron redundancy in improving performance and efficiency in quantum communication systems and other technologies that rely on quantum entanglement. Conclusion: Overall, our findings showcase the potential benefits of incorporating neutron cut sets into neutro-connectedness studies and could lead to novel applications and improvements in multiple fields of science.

Despite the remarkable performance of deep learning methods on various tasks, most cutting-edge models rely heavily on large-scale annotated training examples, which are often unavailable for clinical and health care tasks. The labeling costs for medical images are very high, especially in medical image segmentation, which typically requires intensive pixel/voxel-wise labeling. Therefore, the strong capability of learning and generalizing from limited supervision, including a limited amount of annotations, sparse annotations, and inaccurate annotations, is crucial for the successful application of deep learning models in medical image segmentation. However, due to its intrinsic difficulty, segmentation with limited supervision is challenging and specific model design and/or learning strategies are needed. In this paper, we provide a systematic and up-to-date review of the solutions above, with summaries and comments about the methodologies. We also highlight several problems in this field, discussed future directions observing further investigations.

We evaluate our approach on the RefCOCO dataset and show that it outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. This research explores the use of contextual information beyond image data for semantic segmentation. By utilizing additional sources of context, such as text and location metadata, we aim to improve the accuracy and robustness of machine learning models in this task. Through a comprehensive analysis of various techniques for integrating these supplementary cues into the model's decision-making process, our study demonstrates the effectiveness of mining rich contexts from multiple modalities during training and inference stages of deep neural networks. Overall, our findings suggest that leveraging multi-modal inputs can enhance generalization performance on real-world applications involving complex scenes with varying lighting conditions or object occlusions, ultimately contributing to improvements in computer vision systems' interpretability and reliability.

A large labeled dataset is key to the success of supervised deep learning, but for medical image segmentation, it is highly challenging to obtain sufficient annotated images for model training. In many scenarios, unannotated images are abundant and easy to acquire. Self-supervised learning (SSL) has shown great potentials in exploiting raw data information and representation learning. In this paper, we propose Hierarchical Self-Supervised Learning (HSSL), new self-supervised framework that boosts medical image segmentation by making good use of unannotated data. Unlike current literature on task-specific self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning, we utilize SSL to learn task-agnostic knowledge from heterogeneous data for various medical image segmentation tasks. Specifically, we first aggregate a dataset from several medical challenges, then pre-train the network in a self-supervised manner, and finally fine-tune on labeled data. We develop a new loss function by combining contrastive loss and classification loss and pretrain an encoder-decoder architecture for segmentation tasks. Our extensive experiments show that multi-domain joint pre-training benefits downstream segmentation tasks and outperforms single-domain pre-training significantly. Compared to learning from scratch, our new method yields better performance on various tasks (e.g., +0.69% to +18.60% in Dice scores with 5% of annotated data). With limited amounts of training data, our method can substantially bridge performance gap w.r.t. denser annotations (e.g., 10% vs.~100% of annotated data).

We present UDify, a multilingual multi-task model capable of accurately predicting universal part-of-speech, morphological features, lemmas, and dependency trees simultaneously for all 124 Universal Dependencies treebanks across 75 languages. By leveraging a multilingual BERT self-attention model pretrained on 104 languages, we found that fine-tuning it on all datasets concatenated together with simple softmax classifiers for each UD task can meet or exceed state-of-the-art UPOS, UFeats, Lemmas, (and especially) UAS, and LAS scores, without requiring any recurrent or language-specific components. We evaluate UDify for multilingual learning, showing that low-resource languages benefit the most from cross-linguistic annotations. We also evaluate for zero-shot learning, with results suggesting that multilingual training provides strong UD predictions even for languages that neither UDify nor BERT have ever been trained on. > Video description is a task of automatically generating a textual description of a video. It is a challenging task due to the complexity of the video content and the diversity of the description. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-scale multiple instance video description network (MIMIVD) to address the video description task. The proposed MIMIVD consists of two main components: a multi-scale feature extraction module and a multiple instance description module. The multi-scale feature extraction module is designed to extract multi-scale features from the video content, which can capture both the global and local information of the video. The multiple instance description module is designed to generate a description for each frame of the video, which can capture the diversity of the description. The proposed MIMIVD is trained in a multi-task learning framework, which can improve the performance of the video description task. The experimental results on the MSVD and MSR-VTT datasets show that the proposed MIMIVD outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of the video description accuracy. Laser-induced graphene oxidation (LIGO) is a promising method for the production of graphene oxide (GO) with high surface area and tunable properties. In this study, we employed in-situ Raman spectroscopy to investigate the LIGO process and the resulting GO properties. We found that the LIGO process can be optimized by controlling the laser power, duration, and wavelength. The Raman spectra of the LIGO products showed characteristic peaks of GO, including the G-band and D-band. We also observed the formation of oxygen-containing functional groups on the LIGO products, which were confirmed by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. The Raman and FTIR results indicated that the LIGO process can produce GO with high oxygen content and surface area, which is beneficial for various applications. Overall, our study provides valuable insights into the LIGO process and the resulting GO properties, which can facilitate the development of GO-based materials for energy storage, electronics, and other applications.

In recent years, deep neural networks have made unprecedented progress in computer vision and other areas with an abundance of labeled data. However, creating rich training labels remains costly or impossible on many interesting tasks due to complexity and subjectivity. An increasingly popular solution to this issue is to train network models by minimizing some distance metric between weak labeled observations (e.g., points) and segmented images as determined by human annotators instead of creating exact boundaries themselves [1]. This relaxation naturally allows for incorporating additional information, such as contextual relationships that help constrain image interpretation. In contrast, typical approaches using point ground truth often ignore the spatial relationship between supervised structures, which can lead to poor generalization. Thus, we propose Points2polygons, an adversarially trained ConvNet capable of jointly utilizing multiple complementary sources of labeling (i.e., both weak labels and dense polygon outlines obtained through manual boundary editing) simultaneously during adversarial training without any need to retrain our model when faced with new weak labels only for all applications. Points2polygons improves over state-of-the-art methods for semantic and instance segmentation from coarse (weak) and complete dense polygon labels by 5%-6%, consistently across various application domains. While our focus is primarily on improving performance using existing datasets containing dense annotations as unlabeled auxiliary ground truth, including our new ones specifically created for validation, our findings should also have important theoretical implications within ongoing debate regarding role of strong or weak labels in Deep Learning as well.

3D Semi-Supervised Learning with Uncertainty-Aware Multi-View Co-Training is an innovative approach to 3D object recognition and segmentation. This paper provides a novel approach that uses semi-supervised learning with multi-view co-training to develop the reliability and reliability of 3D object recognition. The proposed approach utilizes uncertainty-aware multi-view co-training to leverage the strengths of different views and minimize the effect of noise and confusion in the training data. The findings indicate the efficacy of the proposed approach in increasing the reliability and reliability of 3D object recognition and segmentation, especially in the absence of limited labeled data. Overall, this paper provides a useful contribution to the field of 3D computer vision by providing a new and effective approach to semi-supervised learning with uncertainty-aware multi-view co-training.

Within this thesis we propose a platform for combining Augmented Reality (AR) hardware with machine learning in a user-oriented pipeline, offering to the medical staff an intuitive 3D visualisation of volumetric Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imageing (MRI) medical image segmentations inside the AR headset, that does not need human intervention for loading, processing and segmentation of medical images. The AR visualisation, based on Microsoft HoloLens, employs a modular and thus scalable frontend-backend architecture for real-time visualisations on multiple AR headsets. As Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have lastly demonstrated superior performance for the machine learning task of image semantic segmentation, the pipeline also includes a fully automated CNN algorithm for the segmentation of the liver from CT scans. The model is based on the Deep Retinal Image Understanding (DRIU) model which is a Fully Convolutional Network with side outputs from feature maps with different resolution, extracted at different stages of the network. The algorithm is 2.5D which means that the input is a set of consecutive scan slices. The experiments have been performed on the Liver Tumor Segmentation Challenge (LiTS) dataset for liver segmentation and demonstrated good results and flexibility. While multiple approaches exist in the domain, only few of them have focused on overcoming the practical aspects which still largely hold this technology away from the operating rooms. In line with this, we also are next planning an evaluation from medical doctors and radiologists in a real-world environment.

This paper provides a statistical logistic shape model inference methodology applied to cochlea image segmentation. The approach is aimed to address problems related to reliability, reliability and computational performance in analyzing images of the human cochlea. The proposed technique provides improved efficiency compared to existing techniques by creating more detailed boundaries with reduced computation time while providing low levels of automation. Results from benchmark testing suggest that this novel algorithm provides an inexpensive solution towards creating automated segmented outcomes for further research purposes such as hearing preservation surgery planning or personalized medicine interventions involving inner ear imaging data. Specifically, it includes insights into potential biomarkers correlated with cognitive disorders affecting auditory systems which may facilitate earlier detection/intervention interventions targeted at improving hearing function among vulnerable species (e.g., prenatal screening programs). Overall, these technologies contribute greatly towards improving our understanding about many issues pertaining auditory development & pathology assessment through non-invasive visualization methods like MRI scans alone or combined techniques where appropriate.

Beijing, China - DiDi's co-founder and President, Jean Liu, announced to her colleagues on Friday that she plans to step down from her position, according to anonymous sources. The move comes just weeks after DiDi, the Chinese ride-hailing giant, went public. Liu, who is widely regarded as one of the most powerful women in China's technology industry, has been a driving force behind DiDi's rapid growth. She co-founded the company with Cheng Wei in 2012 and has served as the company's President ever since. News reports suggest that Liu is leaving the company to pursue personal interests, including spending more time with her family. In a statement, Liu said, "I am proud of what we have accomplished at DiDi and grateful to have had the opportunity to work with such talented and dedicated colleagues. I am confident that under Cheng's leadership, the company will continue to thrive." DiDi's CEO, Cheng Wei, praised Liu's contributions to the company in a statement released on Friday. "Jean has been an invaluable member of the DiDi team and we are grateful for all that she has done to help us grow and succeed. We wish her all the best in her future endeavors." DiDi has been on a major expansion push in recent years. The company has expanded beyond its core ride-hailing business to offer a wide range of services, including bike-sharing, food delivery, and financial services. DiDi went public in June in one of the biggest initial public offerings of the year, raising over 4 billion in the process. The company's stock has struggled since its debut, however, as Chinese regulators cracked down on ride-hailing companies and concerns about competition from rival firm, Meituan, weighed on investors.

This paper deals with a complete bipartite matching problem with the objective of finding an optimal matching that maximizes a certain generic predefined utility function on the set of all matchings. After proving the NP-hardness of the problem using reduction from the 3-SAT problem, we propose a randomized algorithm based on Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) technique for solving this. We sample from Gibb's distribution and construct a reversible positive recurrent discrete time Markov chain (DTMC) that has the steady state distribution same as the Gibb's distribution. In one of our key contributions, we show that the constructed chain is 'rapid mixing', i.e. the convergence time to reach within a specified distance to the desired distribution is polynomial in the problem size. The rapid mixing property is established by obtaining a lower bound on the conductance of the DTMC graph and this result is of independent interest.

Holes and cracks in rigid foam films are common defects that can affect their performance and durability. In this paper, we investigate the properties and behavior of these defects in rigid foam films. We use a combination of experimental and computational techniques to characterize the mechanical and thermal properties of the films with holes and cracks. We find that the presence of these defects can significantly reduce the stiffness and strength of the film, and can also affect its thermal conductivity. We also investigate the effects of different types of holes and cracks on the film's behavior, and compare the results with those of intact films. Our findings have important implications for the design and use of rigid foam films in various applications, and can help to improve their performance and reliability.

This study presents Vessel-CAPTCHA, a novel learning framework designed to efficiently annotate and segment blood vessels in medical images. By leveraging deep neural networks trained on large datasets generated through crowdsourcing efforts employing a CAPTCHA-based approach, our proposed method achieves accurate results while reducing the need for manual labeling by experts. The efficiency of this machine leaning technique is demonstrated via extensive experiments conducted on benchmark databases revealing superior performance when compared with stateof-theart methods. Overall, we believe that such robust automated techniques have great potential towards improving vascular analysis workflows within biomedical research communities.

Despite remarkable performance of deep learning methods on various tasks, most cutting-edge models rely heavily on large-scale annotated training examples, which are often unavailable for clinical and health care tasks. The labeling costs for medical images are very high, especially in medical image segmentation, which typically requires intensive pixel/voxel-wise labeling. Therefore, the strong capability of learning and generalizing from limited supervision, including limited amount of annotations, sparse annotations, and inaccurate annotations, is crucial for the successful application of deep learning models in medical image segmentation. However, due to its intrinsic difficulty, segmentation with limited supervision is challenging and specific model design and/or learning strategies are needed. In this paper, we provide a systematic and up-to-date review of solutions above, with summaries and comments about the methodologies. We also highlight several problems in this field, discussed future directions observing further investigations.

Image segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision that involves dividing an image into meaningful regions. Traditional methods often rely on strong shape priors, which may not always be available or accurate. This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using weak shape priors, which are based on statistical properties of the image data itself. The proposed method employs a graph-based representation of the image, where nodes represent pixels and edges represent their spatial relationships. Weak shape priors are incorporated into the graph by modeling the distribution of edge lengths and angles. The segmentation problem is then formulated as a graph cut problem, which is efficiently solved using the spectral relaxation algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets.

Semi-supervised medical image segmentation is a challenging task that requires the use of limited labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data. One of the main challenges in this task is the presance of hard regions, which are regions that are clearly defined and have a high degree of homogeneity. Enforcing mutual consistency of hard regions is crucial for achieving accurate segmentation results. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for enforcing mutual consistency of hard regions in semi-supervised medical image segmentation. Our approach involves the use of a graph-based representation of the image, where nodes represent hard regions and edges represent the boundaries between them. We then use a mutual consistency constraint to ensure that the hard regions are consistent with each other. Our approach is evaluated on a dataset of medical images and is shown to improve the accuracy of the segmentation results compared to state-of-the-art methods.

This study presents a novel approach to generating discriminative object proposals by utilizing submodular ranking. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of object detection tasks in computer vision applications. By leveraging the principles of submodularity, our algorithm produces high-quality candidate regions that are more likely to contain objects while reducing the number of false positives. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, highlighting the effectiveness of our technique in producing highly accurate object proposals. Overall, this work contributes to advancements in efficient and effective object proposal generation through the application of submodular optimization techniques.

Stimulation threshold in intraoperative nerve monitoring (IONM) can affect the predictive value of the monitoring. The stimulation threshold is the minimum electrical stimulus required to elicit a response from a nerve. The predictive value of IONM depends on its sensitivity and specificity, which can vary depending on the stimulation threshold, technique used, and the type of surgery. Lower stimulation thresholds may help to identify nerves with greater accuracy, but there could be false positives, which could lower the specificity of IONM. On the other hand, higher stimulation thresholds could lead to potential nerve damage due to strong electrical stimulation. Several studies have shown varying results regarding the optimal stimulation threshold for intraoperative nerve monitoring. Some studies have suggested that higher stimulation thresholds help improve the specificity of IONM without sacrificing sensitivity, while others have found that lower stimulation thresholds might better predict postoperative nerve function. Thus, while stimulation threshold does affect the predictive value of intraoperative nerve monitoring, the optimal threshold setting may differ based on factors such as the type of surgery, technique used, and individual patient characteristics. A tailored approach to determining the stimulation threshold for each patient may help maximize the predictive value of IONM in preventing nerve injury during surgery.

In this paper, we investigate the compatibility properties of synchronous and asynchronous communication between components in a distributed system. We explore the challenges posed by different types of communication protocols, such as synchronization, interleaving, and message ordering, and examine their impact on program execution. Using formal verification techniques, such as model checking and state-space analysis, We identify patterns that ensure correctness and reliability of the distributed system under varying conditions and provide guidelines to optimize these patterns. Our results demonstrate that proper design choices can enable seamless integration of synchronous and asynchronous communication paradigms, while maintaining compatibility and predictable behavior. Overall, our work sheds light on the complexities involved in building robust and efficient distributed systems involving both synchronous and asynchronous channels.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to anomaly detection in time series of graphs based on locality statistics. Traditional methods for anomaly detection in graph data rely on global properties such as connectivity patterns or node degrees, which can be computationally expensive and may not capture subtle changes in the graph structure over time. Our method instead focuses on capturing local patterns in the graph neighborhoods, which are more efficient to compute and can detect early signs of anomalies. We introduce a new set of statistical measures that capture the local structural properties of nodes and edges in the graph, such as neighborhood density, diversity, and proximity. We then use these measures to train a machine learning model that can identify anomalous subgraphs in the input time series. To evaluate our method, we conduct experiments on several real-world datasets and compare our results with state-of-the-art baselines. Our experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency. We also demonstrate the versatility of our method by applying it to different types of graph data, including social networks, citation networks, and protein-protein interaction networks. Furthermore, we perform an ablation study to analyze the contribution of each local statistic to the overall performance of our method. The main contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows: (1) we propose a new method for anomaly detection in time series of graphs based on locality statistics; (2) we introduce a new set of statistical measures that capture the local structural properties of nodes and edges in the graph; (3) we develop a machine learning model that uses these measures to detect anomalous subgraphs; and (4) we provide comprehensive experimental evaluations demonstrating the effectiveness and efficiency of our method compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Overall, our work provides a promising direction for effective and efficient anomaly detection in large-scale graph data.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to medical image segmentation using a spatial guided self-supervised clustering network (SGSCN). Our method leverages inherent spatial structure in medical images to learn clustering representations without need for annotated data. The SGSCN model consists of convolutional neural network (CNN) followed by a spatially-aware clustering module. The CNN encodes input image into a set of feature maps, which are then used to compute spatial similarity graph. The spatially- aware clustering module partitions the graph into distinct clusters, where each cluster corresponds to a specific class label. We evaluate our method on several publicly available medical imaging datasets, including MRI brain scans and CT lung scans. Experimental results show that SGSCN outperforms traditional supervised learning approaches, as well as state-of-the art self-supervised methods, in terms of segmentation accuracy. Furthermore, we demonstrate effectiveness of our method in scenarios where annotations are limited or difficult to obtain. This research presents a novel approach to clothing co-parsing, which involves jointly segmenting clothes from images and labelling their attributes such as colour and texture. This advancement has potential applications in various fields including e-commerce, fashion design, and virtual try-on systems.

This work provides a conceptual methodology for studying weakly nonlinear self-sustained explosions, which are explosive events that occur in confined spaces. The concept is based on assumptions and predictions about the behaviour of the liquid at low temperature and low velocity, as well as the presence of chemical interactions that contribute to the energy liberation. The main findings show how the critical wave velocity and critical Mach number depend on the properties of the fluid and the reaction kinetics. These quantities can be used to predict instability or stability in the detonative flow field. Specifically, the impact of boundary conditions, such as oil leak rates and shocks, on the propagation of the shock front is obtained. By integrating theoretical data with mathematical observations, this research offers a complete description of the physics underlying these complex phenomena. However, it provides valuable insights into the systems responsible for explosions happening in many environments, including industrial systems and rocket motors.

We present the 2017 Visual Domain Adaptation (VisDA) dataset and challenge, a large-scale testbed for unsupervised domain adaptation across visual domains. Unsupervised domain adaptation aims to solve the real-world problem of domain shift, where machine learning models trained on one domain must be transferred and adapted to a novel visual domain without additional supervision. The VisDA2017 challenge is focused on the simulation-to-reality shift and has two associated tasks: image classification and image segmentation. The goal in both tracks is to first train a model on simulated, synthetic data in the source domain and then adapt it to perform well on real image data in the unlabeled test domain. Our dataset is the largest one to date for cross-domain object classification, with over 933K images across 87 categories in the combined training, validation and testing domains. The image segmentation dataset is also large-scale with over 30K images across 50 categories in the three domains. We compare VisDA to existing cross-domain adaptation datasets and provide a baseline performance analysis using various domain adaptation models that are currently popular in the field.

In the present article, we present a new architecture of a self-trained clustering network which utilizes the spatial distribution of the different nodes to enhance the performance of medical image segmentation. The architecture uses both supervised and unsupervised learning. The former provides the images with the classes of tissues, the latter classifies the similar nodes independently of their classes. The experiments show an improvement of the performance of the proposed method over the existing models on a large scale. The paper discusses possible improvements in the pre-processing techniques, the possibility of extending the framework to other modalities, and other possible applications in the field of medical images. In conclusion, our method improves the accuracy of medical image segmentation by introducing a powerful tool that enables the identification and separation of different classes of tissues in complex medical images with minimal human interference.

This paper proposes a novel approach to model selection for time series data using graphical LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) method. The traditional LASSO method is widely used for linear regression models, but it has limitations when applied to time series data. The graphical LASSO method allows for efficient inference and visualization of coefficients in presence of complex time-varying relationships. The proposed method uses a Bayesian framework to incorporate prior information into the model and account for uncertainties in parameters. It also employs a sparsity inducing penalty term to automatically select relevant features that explain variability in the time series data. Extensive simulations show that our proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of forecast accuracy and computational efficiency. It is further demonstrated on real-world datasets where it identifies important factors contributing to the time series dynamics, providing valuable insights for decision making in various domains. This research contributes to the field of machine learning and signal processing by offering powerful tool for large-scale time series data analysis, which can be applied to various fields such as finance, economics, healthcare and environmental monitoring.

We propose a novel regularization-based continual learning method, dubbed as Adaptive Group Sparsity based Continual Learning (AGS-CL), using two group sparsity-based penalties. Our method selectively employs the two penalties when learning each node based its the importance, which is adaptively updated after learning each new task. By utilizing the proximal gradient descent method for learning, the exact sparsity and freezing of the model is guaranteed, and thus, the learner can explicitly control the model capacity as the learning continues. Furthermore, as a critical detail, we re-initialize the weights associated with unimportant nodes after learning each task in order to prevent the negative transfer that causes the catastrophic forgetting and facilitate efficient learning of new tasks. Throughout the extensive experimental results, we show that our AGS-CL uses much less additional memory space for storing the regularization parameters, and it significantly outperforms several state-of-the-art baselines on representative continual learning benchmarks for both supervised and reinforcement learning tasks.

The paper "CHASE: Robust Visual Tracking via Cell-Level Differentiable Neural Architecture Search" presents a novel approach to visual tracking that utilizes a differentiable neural architecture search (DNAS) method to optimize the tracking performance. The proposed method, called CHASE (Cell-Level Hierarchical Architecture Search for Efficient Tracking), uses a hierarchical architecture search strategy to identify the optimal architecture for visual tracking. The search is performed at the cell level, allowing for the exploration of a large search space and the identification of the most effective architectural components. The resulting architecture is then trained using a robust visual tracking dataset, resulting in improved tracking performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. The paper also presents an analysis of the effectiveness of the different architectural components and demonstrates the robustness of the proposed method to variations in the tracking environment. Overall, the paper demonstrates the potential of DNAS for improving the performance of visual tracking systems.

As a cat, sort of, fabric-and-stitching construct in a human gait, I find myself sauntering around ordinary people whose heads swivel and eyes bugger, breaking into eager whispers. Look, don't you know that's what they do? So here we are at the conference centre with its two conference rooms, and on each side is a corner tableau: a woman being interviewed by someone else; a young man in front of a laptop who has tapped out an email message, his chin resting upon one hand while he watches Wintour spinning her raspberries; or a middle-aged man casually wandering through a crowded room like a strolling suburban homesteader - overwhelmed as usual but unperturbed, talking to everyone. When I look over, I see, all wrongfully, that this particular man is a case in point for why women should have more men to talk to about fashion. He looks pretty much the same for every interview she does: big shoulders, a round face, a bushy moustache. The only way you can tell him apart from others is when he is wearing expensive clothes consisting entirely of cashmere sweaters piled high with inset leather jackets. And if he happens to be working, chances are you've seen him before, standing behind the bar, showing off his extremely well-groomed beard to anyone passing by. One would never mistake him for wearing anything remotely outside his comfort zone (which is not sweatpants). It seems unfair having so few available conversations with other men. But then again, it isn't really: there aren't many of us, after all. "I wish we had more men," says Eyal Ben David, an Israeli journalist and critic of the Israeli press who is co-chairing the show this year. "It used to take almost 30 years until our own country got rid of the stereotypes." There were once no women in journalism in Israel. Now there are dozens; there are even some women editors. And yet, a full third of reporters at Haaretz, the largest newspaper in Israel, are female. So how come the fields of discourse remain barren of men? When Bernard Arnault, the billionaire founder of LVMH (Luxury Group Village), started designing costumes for Chanel's annual couture shows, designers asked whether the formerly predominantly male audience might one day be impressed. This academic paper presents a novel adaptive strategy for improving the accuracy and efficiency of superpixel-based region-growing image segmentation. The proposed approach utilizes an initial oversegmentation step to generate candidate regions, which are then refined through an iterative process that adapts to the local texture and color characteristics of the imaged being segmented. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in both segmentation quality and computational efficiency compared to existing methods. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the design of efficient and effective algorithms for automated image analysis tasks.

The segmentation of nanoscale electron microscopy (EM) images is crucial but challenging in connectomics. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated the significant potential of automatic segmentation for tera-scale EM images. However, none of the existing segmentation methods are error-free, and they require proofreading, which is typically implemented as an interactive, semi-automatic process via manual intervention. Herein, we propose a fully automatic proofreading method based on reinforcement learning. The main idea is to model the human decision process in proofreading using a reinforcement agent to achieve fully automatic proofreading. We systematically design the proposed system by combining multiple reinforcement learning agents in a hierarchical manner, where each agent focuses only on a specific task while preserving dependency between agents. Furthermore, we also demonstrate that the episodic task setting of reinforcement learning can efficiently manage a combination of merge and split errors concurrently presented in the input. We demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed system by comparing it with state-of-the-art proofreading methods using various testing examples.

As I woke up, I could just make out that Ramirez's pod was empty. As I looked around, I saw that the others were empty as well. Strange, that I was the only one of us asleep for so long. I turned and looked out the window. This planet we were on looked a lot like Earth. I checked my radio for any signs of civilization here, but I could find none. We were definitely very far away from Earth. I saw the tent outside my window. It was white and black. I went inside it and saw Ms. O'Leary working. I went to talk to her. "Hi Ms. O'Leary," I said, "how are you doing?" she just looked at me, pale, like she saw a ghost or something. I would soon come to realize that she thought I had died in the crash. She said, "um, fine, I guess. How are you? It's been almost a year since we landed on this planet." A year? Oh my god, this must have come as a surprise to her. Overall, though, she seemed glad that I was still alive. She shouted outside the tent to Ramirez: "He's alive!" Ramirez looked pleased as punch to hear that I was still alive. I'll bet that with me gone, it was up to Ramirez to do most of the work. I could see from here that Ramirez wasn't wearing his space suit. This planet must be a lot like Earth. I went out to see Ramirez again.

Тhіs іs а tесhnіquе thаt аssіgns lаbеls tо dіffеrеnt rеgіоns оf аn іmаgе bаsеd оn thеіr соntеnt. Ηоwеvеr, оnе mаjоr сhаllеngе fасіng sеmаntіс sеgmеntаtіоn mоdеls іs dеаlіng wіth аmbіguоus оr соntехtuаl sіtuаtіоns whеrе vаrіоus оbjесts оr соnсерts mау hаvе multірlе роssіblе mеаnіngs dереndіng оn thе surrоundіng еnvіrоnmеnt. Τо аddrеss thіs іssuе, wе рrороsе ІSΝеt (Іntеgrаtе Іmаgе-Lеvеl аnd Sеmаntіс-Lеvеl Соntехt), whісh іntеgrаtеs bоth іmаgе-lеvеl соntехt frоm ехtеrnаl knоwlеdgе sоurсеs suсh аs Wіkіреdіа, аnd sеmаntіс-lеvеl соntехt frоm рrе-ехіstіng mоdеls. Βу соmbіnіng thеsе twо fоrms оf соntехt, оur аррrоасh іmрrоvеs thе реrfоrmаnсе оf sеmаntіс sеgmеntаtіоn tаsks bу рrоvіdіng mоrе ассurаtе аnd nuаnсеd іntеrрrеtаtіоns оf іmаgе соntеnts. This paper presents an efficient energy minimization method for enforcing Statistics in machine learning models. The proposed approach aims to optimize the trade-off between model accuracy and computational complexity by Incorporating statistical measures into the training process. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the performance of machine learning models while reducing the computational overhead. overall, this study provides a promising solution for addressing the challenges of Enforcing statistics in machine learning and has potential applications in various domains.

This study presents a novel approach to weakly supervised segmentation using Inter Extreme Point (IEEP) geodesics. The proposed method utilises IEEP distance as an optimisation objective, which allows for efficient and robust clustreing of data points based on their similarities. Experimental results demonstrate that our technique outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, making it a promising solution for various computer vision tasks requiring weak supervision. Overall, this work provides insights into leverageing geometric structure within datasets toward improved performance in semi-supervised learning scenarios.

This academic paper explores the use of contextual information beyond image data for semantic segmentation. By analyzing various sources of contextual information, such as text, audio, and video, the paper demonstrates how these additional data sources can improve the accuracy and efficiency of semantic segmentation. Through a series of experiments and case studies, the paper provides evidence that mining contextual information beyond image data can lead to significant improvements in the performance of semantic segmentation models. Overall, this paper offers valuable insights for researchers and practitioners working in the field of computer vision and machine learning.

This paper presents a Bayesian Logistic Shape Model Inference approach for cochlea image segmentation. The proposed method utilizes logistic shape model to represent the cochlea structure and employs Bayesian framework to infer model parameters from the image data. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments on dataset of cochlea images, showing significant improvement in segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods. The paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of medical image analysis by offering robust and accurate method for cochlea segmentation.

Federated learning allows distributed medical institutions to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model with privacy protection. While at clinical deployment, the models trained in federated learning can still suffer from performance drop when applied to completely unseen hospitals outside the federation. In this paper, we point out and solve a novel problem setting of federated domain generalization (FedDG), which aims to learn a federated model from multiple distributed source domains such that it can directly generalize to unseen target domains. We present a novel approach, named as Episodic Learning in Continuous Frequency Space (ELCFS), for this problem by enabling each client to exploit multi-source data distributions under the challenging constraint of data decentralization. Our approach transmits the distribution information across clients in a privacy-protecting way through an effective continuous frequency space interpolation mechanism. With the transferred multi-source distributions, we further carefully design a boundary-oriented episodic learning paradigm to expose the local learning to domain distribution shifts and particularly meet the challenges of model generalization in medical image segmentation scenario. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated with superior performance over state-of-the-arts and in-depth ablation experiments on two medical image segmentation tasks. The code is available at "https://github.com/liuquande/FedDG-ELCFS".

Yi (2016a, b) gave exact-solution algorithms for constraint-solving and maximum-cut problems on grids, which require a quadratic space. We extended these techniques to solve a large-scale semidefinite problem, and gave a 5-times-larger-than-n-square-factor-dependent exact solution for k-colorings, where n N is the number of nodes in the model, and the edge density is bounded from (N) (N/n3/8). This extends the results of Chlamtac et al., who only considered stronger graphs and could only obtain heuristics without any guarantees. We extended these results to other combinatorial maximum-cut problems and unweighted quadratic modular constraints, as well as to the framework of multiple commodity cuts, which is closely related to knapsack inequalities. We also give some practical implementation details of this k-coloring solution, such as the use of block coding, and the computation of semi-definite conditions with randomized methods such as ROT. Together with various reduction rules, our implementations run under the same time conditions, and often have good solutions for non-unique problems.

The Keep Military Museum in Dorchester plans to use the money to convert a bunker into an interactive experience. It also wants to create an online gallery of Dorset and Devon people who fought in the war, and a room for community talks and school visits. The Keep is the only military museum for the regiments of both Dorset and Devon. The museum, which is receiving the money from the Heritage Lottery Fund, houses thousands of original and unique exhibits, including the desk belonging to Adolf Hitler and hundreds of items from WWI. Curator Colin Parr said they wanted to gather stories from people whose relatives had taken part in the war. He added: "Our volunteers will create an online history gallery which will include a contributory archive for people wishing to share their history with us." Nerys Watts, of the Heritage Lottery Fund, said: "All communities living in the UK have been affected by the First World War in some way, either by the events that took place, or by the changes it brought about. "We are keen to support projects that, like this one, enable local people to understand more about the heritage of the First World War and how it touched and changed their community."

The paper presents a novel approach to video segmentation using separable convolutional LSTMs. The proposed method leverages the advantages of both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to improve the efficiency and accuracy of video segmentation. The separable convolutional architecture reduces the computational complexity of the CNN, while the LSTM network captures temporal dependencies in the video. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and shows significant improvements in both accuracy and speed compared to state-of-the-art methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for real-time video segmentation tasks.

This paper investigates the small redshift limit of steady states in the spherically symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system, a model that describes gravity coupled with an imperfect fluid. The study focuses on the stability of these steady states as well. By using various mathematical techniques such as inverse scoring and linearized perturbations, we analyze how these steady states behave under different conditions. Our findings suggest that certain steady states are indeed stable while others exhibit instability depending on specific parameters involved in the problem. Overall, this research provides valuable insights into understanding astrophysical phenomena like black holes or neutron stars where similar models apply.

Active contours, also known as snakes or active contours, are a popular image segmentation technique that uses an energy functional to deform a contour to the desired boundary in an image. Physical modeling techniques are a class of methods that incorporate physical principles into the active contour framework to improve its performance and robustness. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of physical modeling techniques in active contours for image segmentation. We begin by introducing the basic concepts of active contours and the challenges associated with their use. We then discuss the different physical modeling techniques that have been proposed in the literature, including those based on elasticity, fluid dynamics, and electromagnetism. We provide a detailed analysis of the advantages and limitations of each technique and highlight their applications in various imaging modalities. We also discuss the numerical implementation of these techniques and the challenges associated with their optimization. The paper concludes with a discussion of the future directions for physical modeling techniques in active contours, including the integration of machine learning methods and the development of new physical models that can better capture the complexity of real-world images. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of physical modeling techniques in active contours for image segmentation, and is a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners working in this field.

"We therefore need to reduce our cost structure to be more in line with our student numbers, as well as universities in the capital similar to London Met," he said.

Registration is a key task in scientific imagery research which can be applied to many functions including image segmentation, intra-operative monitoring, multi-modal image alignment, and motion prediction. Popular registration methods such as ANTs and NiftyReg optimize an objective function for each pair of pictures from scratch which is time-consuming for small pictures with complex deformation. Facilitated by the slow progress of deep learning, learning-based methods such as VoxelMorph have been developing for image registration. These methods can reach competitive efficiency in a fraction of a third on advanced GPUs. In this work, we construct a neural registration framework, called NeurReg, with a hybrid loss of displacement fields and data similarity, which greatly improves the current state-of-the-art of registrations. Within the implementation, we simulate various transformations by a registration simulator which provides fixed image and displacement field ground truth for training. Additionally, we design two segmentation frameworks based on the proposed registration framework: 1) atlas-based segmentation, 2) joint learning of both segmentation and registration tasks, and 3) multi-task learning with atlas-based segmentation as an intermediate feature. Numerous experimental findings validate the validity of the proposed NeurReg framework based on several indicators: the endpoint error (EPE) of the predicted displacement field, mean square error (MSE), normalized local cross-correlation (NLCC), mutual information (IL), Dice coefficient, uncertainty analysis, and the interpretability of the segmentation. The proposed NeurReg increases registration accuracy with fast inference speed, which can significantly accelerate related medical image analysis activities.

This study investigates how various combinations of regularizations can improve performance of convolutional networks and classification schemes when training images based on large labelled datasets (e.g., images labeled as cats by ImageNet). An important aspect of such models—that is, most recent models used in deep learning—is automatically adjusting the weights of individual pixels through stochastic gradient descent; the resulting softmax outputs represent features that have been learned to be meaningful by those using them; moreover, this network architecture allows the model to perform complex object detection tasks without explicitly being able or wanting to learn these particular attributes and thereby increase its sensitivity. We build on these strengths in a new approach which involves creating pre-trained versions of three neural network architectures: linear unit function with sparse nonlinearities, a fixed cost L2 regularizer based on a special k-nn implementation, and an SVD regularized over spatial features. The proposed designs are evaluated with two different image recognition tasks (image segmentation and regression) via standard supervised and unsupervised algorithms as described earlier in Section 5 and demonstrate significant improvements compared to comparable previous work. These results allow us to provide preliminary results suggesting that pre-processing is likely to dramatically accelerate the development and use of Deep Convolutional Networks and consequently help greatly progress knowledge of object detection across diverse applications across various computer vision problems. You'll notice in the introduction a few notes about the methods under consideration in terms of size, amount of feature data used and whether or not you're focusing on one type of regularizer. I'm calling it my own variation of kNN here. The key difference is simply that instead of taking your input image, applying the right level of regularization (or none at all if you don't need or want any) and then outputting a single value (the output), here we take our input image (also called input) and apply a high-quality, local filter using a multi-valued hyper-parameter followed by our desired (k, v) regularizers. To find out more about it check out the GitHub repo where I posted my work. The advance in deep learning technology has brought about significant improvements in tracking objects visually, but challenges remain such as occlusions and variations in object pose. To address these issues, we propose a novel approach called CHASE (Cell-level differentiable Neural architecture SEarch) to robust visual tracking. Our method first adopts a multi-object tracking framework that uses a cellular neural network encoder to extract features of objects at both local and global levels, followed by a decoder that generates bounding boxes, distances, and directions of all visible objects from previous frames. We then incorporate differentiable neural architecture search, enabling our system to learn an optimized network structure that improves overall tracking performance on synthetic and real-world datasets. Experiments show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmark datasets in terms of precision and stability, demonstrating the value of our proposed optimization algorithm in improving robustness during tracking.

The house salad is a variation on a traditional AntiPasto theme- and is a meal, and event, in and of its self. The best thing about Mardeneley's is that EVERYTHING on the menu is good! It only gets Four stars because it could use a bit more snob appeal (and a better beer selection).

Update! See Edit 2 below! I don't know much about politics. I have a pretty poor understanding of real world economics. I don't follow world events or watch the news. I generally don't bother to keep track of what's going on in the world unless it impacts me directly, or maybe I think there's something meaningful I can do to change it to my own benefit (which has never actually come up). When it comes to who should be elected in any local, state or federal capacity, or what laws should or should not be passed, I am simply not a qualified to provide input on any level. So why am I allowed to vote?
