In this paper we present a thorough analysis of uniform distributions. First we briefly review previous work on non-uniform distributions, pointing out their shortcomings. Then we introduce our proposed method, which, through convex combination, makes it possible to create more flexible probabilistic models with more efficient inference. In extensive experiments with a number of datasets, we show that our method achieves a significantly higher performance than existing methods, while maintaining a high degree of efficiency. Our experiments have significant improvements in several ways: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and runtime. This could be of interest for practitioners working in the domain adaptation or multi-class classification. In addition, we discuss possible extensions of our method, pointing to promising directions for further research. In general, this paper has both theoretical and practical value for the development of current machine learning strategies.

In this paper we present a system that mines semantic information beyond a small number of visual annotations extracted by its neural network, namely: image labels and edges in images (via edge detection; see [7, 51]). The system, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on image similarity tasks, does so not by directly extracting these features but simply by performing inference based on their usage and classification performance on validation data using an existing text document, thereby showing that it can be improved through a combination of natural language processing, visual search-based machine learning techniques, and deep learning.

We introduce a simple, easy to sample, random graph model that captures the limiting spectra of many sequences of interest, including the sequence of hypercube graphs. The Random Overlapping Communities (ROC) model is specified by a distribution on pairs (s, q), s Z , q (0, 1 ]. A graph on n vertices with average degree d is generated by repeatedly picking pairs (s, q) from the distribution, adding an Erdos-Renyi random graph of edge density q on a subset of vertices chosen by including each vertex with probability s n, and repeating this process so that the expected degree is d. Our proof of convergence to a ROC random graph is based on the Stieltjes moment condition. We also show that the model is an effective approximation for individual graphs. For almost all possible triangle-to-edge and four-cycle-to-edge ratios, there exists a pair (s, q) such that the ROC model with this single community type produces graphs with both desired ratios, a property that cannot be achieved by stochastic block models of bounded description size. Moreover, ROC graphs exhibit an inverse relationship between degree and clustering coefficient, a characteristic of many real-world networks.

The proposed method leverages the advantages of both dilated convolutions and lateral inhibitions to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation. The dilated convolutions allow the model to capture long-range dependencies between pixels, while the lateral inhibitions help to reduce overfitting and improve the generalization performance. The latest threats bring the number of incidents to 69 in 27 states in the past month, according to the JCC Association of North America. No bombs were found at any of the centres targeted with telephone calls. Last week, 27 Jewish community centres in 17 US states reported receiving hoax bomb threats. All of the threats made on Monday, along with previous incidents in January, turned out to be false and Jewish centres have since reopened with normal services resumed. Responding to the latest incidents, White House press secretary Sean Spicer said that US President Donald Trump had made it "abundantly clear" that such actions were "unacceptable." "Hatred and hate-motivated violence of any kind have no place in a country founded on the promise of individual freedom," the statement, which was shared on Twitter by NBC News correspondent Peter Alexander, said. Mr Trump's daughter Ivanka - who has converted to Judaism and whose husband is Jewish - also condemned the threats. Former Democratic presidential candidate Hillary Clinton said that action must be taken to prevent further incidents. In a post on Twitter, Mrs Clinton wrote: "JCC threats, cemetery desecration and online attacks are so troubling and they need to be stopped. Everyone must speak out, starting wPOTUS." The threats were made to the Jewish community centres through calls that were both pre-recorded and live, with suspects using voice-disguising technology, according to Israeli newspaper Haaretz. Since the beginning of the year, there have been reports of threats to centres in New York, New Jersey, Ohio, Florida, Massachusetts, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Delaware, Connecticut, Alabama, California, Maine, Tennessee, South Carolina, Missouri, Wisconsin, Texas and Kansas. The JCC Association of North America, a network of health and education centres, has since been reviewing its security plans. In an earlier statement the FBI said that along with the US justice department it was investigating possible civil rights violations in connection with the threats. The Anti-Defamation League, a Jewish anti-bigotry organisation, said in a statement that it was "deeply disturbed" by the latest threats to the Jewish community. Meanwhile, more than 100 headstones have been damaged at a Jewish cemetery in St Louis, Missouri, local media report. In the Canadian city of Toronto, Mayor John Tory has condemned anti-Semitic hate notes left outside the homes of Jewish residents.

In this position paper we present a novel approach to neurobiologically plausible implementation of emotional reactions and behaviors for real-time autonomous robotic systems. The working metaphor we use is the "day" and "night" phases of mammalian life. During the "day" phase a robotic system stores the inbound information and is controlled by the light-weight rule-based system in real time. In contrast to that, during the "night" phase the stored information is been transferred to the supercomputing system to update the realistic neural network: emotional and behavioral strategies.

In recent years, deep neural networks have made unprecedented progress in computer vision and other areas with an abundance of labelled data. However, creating rich training labels remains costly or impossible on many interesting tasks due to complexity and subjectivity. An increasingly popular solution to this issue is to train network models by minimising some distance metric between weak labelled observations (e.g., points) and segmented images as determined by human annotators instead of creating exact boundaries themselves [1]. This relaxeation naturally allows for incorporating additional information, such as contextual relationships that help constrain image interpretation. In contrast, typical approaches using point ground truth often ignore the spatial relationship between supervised structures, which can lead to poor generalisation. Thus, we propose Points2polygons, an adversarially trained ConvNet capable of jointly utilising multiple complementary sources of labelling (i.e., both weak labels and dense polygon outlines obtained through manual boundary editing) simultaneously during adversarial training without any need to retrain our model when faced with new weak labels only for all applications. Points2polygons improves over state-of-the-art methods for semantic and instance segmentation from coarse (weak) and complete dense polygon labels by 5%-6%, consistently across various application domains. While our focus is primarily on improving performance using existing datasets containing dense annotations as unlabelled auxiliary ground truth, including our new ones specifically created for validation, our findings should also have important theoretical implications within the ongoing debate regarding the role of strong or weak labels in Deep Learning as well.

Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for cross-modality medical image segmentation has shown grate progress by domain-invariant feature learning or image appearance translation. Adapted feature learning usually cannot detect domain shifts at the pixel level and is not able to acheive good results in dense semantic segmentation tasks. Image appearance translation, e.g. CycleGAN, translates images into different styles with good appearance, despite its population, its semantic consistency is hardly to maintain and results in poor cross-modality segmentation. In this paper, we propose intra- and cross-modality semantic consistency (ICMSC) for UDA and our key insight is that the segmentation of synthesised images in different styles should be consistent. Specifically, our model consists of an image translation module and a domain-specific segmentation module. The image translation module is a standard CycleGAN, while the segmentation module contains two domain-specific segmentation networks. The intra-modality semantic consistency (IMSC) forces the reconstructed image after a cycle to be segmented in the same way as the orignal input image, while the cross-modality semantic consistency (CMSC) encourages the synthesized images after translation to be segmented exactly the same as before translation. Comprehensive experimental results on cross-modality hip joint bone segmentation show the effectiveness of our proposed method, which achieves an average DICE of 81.61% on the acetabulum and 88.16% on the proximal femur, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. It is worth to note that without UDA, a model trained on CT for hip joint bone segmentation is non-transferable to MRI and has allmost zero-DICE segmentation.

> By combining degree-four sum-of-square relaxations and linear systems, Yi (2016) gave algorithms that solve exact constraint satisfaction and max-cut problems on dense 2D grids within polynomial time. We improve these exponential-time techniques by extending them to exact semidefinite programming over grid graphs with larger constant factors. For k-coloring, we give an algorithm running in O\left({n^5}\right)\exp{\left({\mathrm{poly}(k)}\right)}+\exp{\left(O\left(\sqrt{\log n}/n^{3/8} \right) \right)}$ where n\in N is the number of nodes in our model with edge density bounded away from one. This improvement extends the approach of Chlamtac et al.\cite{chitnis2013}. Previously, such improvements have been proven only for graph classes with stronger structural properties or were given only heuristic implementations without specific guarantees on their approximation ratio. We further study how the results extend to other combinatorial max cut settings as well as extensions involving quadratic modular constraints and unweighted constraints arising out of multicommodity flow network cuts which are closely related to knapsack inequalities. We also discuss practical implementation details of this algorithm for graph coloring problems including optimizations through the use of block encoding and the efficient computation of semi-definiteness conditions using randomized techniques like ROT. Combined together with various reduction rules, our practical implementation runs in under the same runtime, often producing high quality solutions when the problem does not have unique optimal solution and can therefore be extended even beyond exact solving.

This paper proposes a semiparametric extension of the stochastic block model (SBM) for longitudinal networks. The extended SBM allows for both heterogeneity in network ties and individual-specific effects, which are modelled using finite mixture models with random coefficients. We demonstrate the flexibility and applicability of our approach through simulations and an analysis of real social networking data from Facebook. Our results show that incorporating individual-level variation improved model fit compared to traditional static SBMs, highlighting the importance of considering within-person changes over time when modelling complex relational data. Overall, this study provides a valuable tool for researchers studying dynamic network structures across multiple waves or intervals of observation.

Given the constantly growing proliferation of false claims online in recent years, there has been also a growing research interest in automatically distinguishing false rumors from factually true claims. Here, we propose a general-purpose framework for fully-automatic fact checking using external sources, tapping the potential of the entire Web as a knowledge source to confirm or reject a claim. Our framework uses a deep neural network with LSTM text encoding to combine semantic kernels with task-specific embeddings that encode a claim together with pieces of potentially-relevant text fragments from the Web, taking the source reliability into account. The evaluation results show good performance on two different tasks and datasets: (i) rumor detection and (ii) fact checking of the answers to a question in community question answering forums.

Background As humans, we are naturally able to detect and describe people, dogs, and other objects using a combination of vision, sound (e.g., voice), touch, smell, or motion. However, detecting such information requires highly precise algorithms that extract meaningful features from vast amounts of natural language input. In this study, I present clickstream models with increasing accuracy, which can recognize many individual objects in real time. Based on training examples found at open-source systems like ImageNet or Genome Visualization Challenge, we show both accuracy and convergence results from machine learning frameworks implemented within Caffe2, Torch8, VGG16, and Matlab7. Overall, our approach yields strong support for some state-of-the art models for image classification and semantic segmentation across domains including face detection and speech recognition. Conclusion We propose three new algorithms for automated search and visual classification applications (Figure), one each suited to an early style (low false positives) and advanced style (high false positive errors). We demonstrate their superiority over previous methods based on more classical techniques like naive Bayes' Theorem and gradient descent in deep learning approaches in terms of ease of implementation while maintaining high sensitivity for detecting faces and human-like entities. Such results pave the way toward providing AI applications even further in the future without compromising high accuracy under increasingly realistic tasks. This is a really interesting article. So far we've been seeing stories about the dangers of unemployment due to lack of skills training, but here there seems to be more focus on the costs involved. The cost of employing one person versus the benefits to society through increased productivity are both important factors. But I think there should also be consideration given to human dignity. Connection structure provides the basic insight that images are composed of small regions—nodes, edges or vertices—that communicate and interact with one another in meaningful ways across a large volume of semantic space. This notion has been well-tethered to the idea of word embeddings on an existing neural network context; however, it appears that these same conceptual constructs may also be used by a new approach to connectionist verification without any explicit mapping to word embeddings. RLCcorrector adds reinforcement learning functionality to this traditional proofreading paradigm (see [1] http://arxiv.org/abs/1308.4824), and integrates it with existing machine pattern recognition algorithms such as Gaussian Process and Markov chains. RLCcorrectors allow for both error detection (using unsupervised feature learning) and inference (by using high-level supervised models that utilise the features present in the evidence). For errors, we use word vectors that encode information about the locations of the locations of words within a sentence and then detect similar occurrences in different documents. With the current algorithm, if two adjacent documents have not yet touched each other, our model suggests that their occurrence should correspond to some common location. A few moments later when they begin crossing over, the error becomes more apparent. Thus, this system can quickly learn patterns such as the positions of words contained inside sentences based on prior knowledge to correct erroneous matches that might otherwise elude prediction.[2][3] We show how RLCcorrectors can extend commonly used automatic annotation systems like Wordnet and Snippets to include connectionist approaches, adding validation and support information. The end-to-end process required for connecting word embeddings and connectionist training methods yields improved readability and overall comprehension through higher levels of abstraction than previously available. https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.06398 - see below. Nests are one-dimensional contours that make up the perimeter of two- and higher dimensional geometries (holes or cavities). Note the nest terminates inside a cavity, never outside (as it would at $\infty$). A nested set of nests has an Euler characteristic equal to 2 and has genus zero. Each ring or nested set represents a handle; the number of such sets equals twice their number of regions, since they cover twice as much area. For example, this illustrates the Euler relation for a two-ring nested set (a torus) with three holes (genus = 0) : 2 × Rings – Holes = Voids + Handles. Such sets have been used to explain how entropy might be related to negative curvature on membranes. Thus far this relies on geometric features of triangulated surfaces, not necessarily those defined implicitly by nets of circles — but they could also play a role here, especially when mapped onto different surface types like Riemann spaces, hyperbolic planes etc… Abstract / Extract from ArXiV entry below: _______________________ A statistical mechanics formalism is used to study ensembles generated by randomly assigning $q$ nests at each vertex of a map of arbitrary topology. This yields probability distributions for generating functions of various observables, notably ones counting the degree sequences of loops attached to different nests. We demonstrate that these quantities satisfy well known recurrences which we use to provide explicit formulas giving exact results. Our primary tool involves deriving recursive generating function relations from analyticity considerations along with symmetry constraints derived from an explicit formula based upon evaluating an appropriately weighted partition function associated to planar graphs with only even order vertices.

Incorporating shape information is essential for the delineation of many organs and anatomical structures in medical images. While previous work has mainly focused on parametric spatial transformations applied on refrence template shapes, in this paper, we adress the Bayesian inference of parametric shape models for segmenting medical images with the objective to provide interpretable results. The proposed framework defines a likelihood appearance probability and a prior label probability based on a generic shape function through a logistic function. A referance length parameter defined in the sigmoid controls the trade-off between shape and appearance information. The inference of shape parameters is performed within an Expectation-Maximisation approach where a Gauss-Newton optimization stage allows to provide an approximation of the posterior probability of shape parameters. This framework is applied to the segmentation of cochlea structures from clinical CT images constrained by a 10 parameter shape model. It is evaluated on three different datasets, one of which includes more than 200 patient images. The results show performances comparable to supervised methods and better than previously proposed unsupervised ones. It also enables an analysis of parameter distributions and the quantification of segmentation uncertainty including the effect of the shape model.

We consider the problem of optimising a black-box function with re-entrant costs. The function is assumed to be modular, that is, to be decomposable into a number of subfunctions, also black-boxes. The re-entrant costs are assumed to be additive, that is, to be independent of the current state of the system. We propose a Bayesian optimisation algorithm for this problem, based on a novel cost of switching, which takes the re-entrant costs into account. We show that the proposed optimiser finds the optimal solution with fewer evaluations than a previous state-of-the-art optimiser. This paper is available here.

We present a systematic methodology to develop high order accurate numerical approaches for linear advection problems. These methods are based on evolving parts of the jet of the solution in time, and are thus called jet schemes. Through the tracking of characteristics and the use of suitable Hermite interpolations, high order is achieved in an optimally local fashion, i.e. the update for the data at any grid point uses information from a single grid cell only. We show that jet schemes can be interpreted as advect-and-project processes in function spaces, where the projection step minimises a stability functional. Furthermore, this function space framework makes it possible to systematically inherit update rules for the higher derivatives from the ODE solver for the characteristics. Jet schemes of orders up to five are applied in numerical benchmark tests, and systematically compared with classical WENO finite difference schemes. It is observed that jet schemes tend to possess a higher accuracy than WENO schemes of the same order.

Understanding E3 ligase and target substrate interactions are important for cell biology and therapeutic development. However, experimental identification of E3 target relationships is not an easy task due to the labor-intensive nature of the experiments. In this article, a sequence-based E3-target prediction model is proposed for the first time. The proposed framework utilizes composition of k-spaced amino acid pairs (CKSAAP) to learn the relationship between E3 ligases and their target protein. A class separable latent space encoding scheme is also devised that provides a compressed representation of feature space. A thorough ablation study is performed to identify an optimal gap size for CKSAAP and the number of latent variables that can represent the E3-target relationship successfully. The proposed scheme is evaluated on an independent dataset for a variety of standard quantitative measures. In particular, it achieves an average accuracy of 70.63 on an independent dataset. The source code and datasets used in the study are available at the author's GitHub page .

The conventional approach to real-time semantic segmentation has been focused on designing lightweight architectures with reduced complexity. However, recent studies have shown that exploiting spatial and channel dependencies can result in improved accuracy without significant increases in computational cost. This study proposes a novel revision of Bilateral Spatial Pyramid Pooling (BiSeNet) architecture by incorporating dual path refinements along both horizontal and vertical directions through dense connections, thereby enhancing feature extraction capabilities at multiple scales. Extensive experiments were conducted using CAMVID, Cityscapes, and COCO datasets which demonstrated superior performance when compared to state-of-the-art models while maintaining competitive inference times. The proposed model achieves an impressive tradeoff between accuracy and speed making it suitable for various applications such as autonomous driving or robotics where real-time processing is essential. Overall, this work provides new insights into network design strategies for efficient yet accurate semantic segmentation tasks.

Introduction: Efficient and accurate segmentation of medical images is a critical step in various medical applications, including disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring. With the increasing availability of large medical image datasets, there is growing interest in developing automated segmentation techniques that can exploit the wealth of information contained within these data. In this pilot study, we investigate the potential benefits of integrating eye-tracking technology into medical image segmentation workflows. Our proposed approach, termed Gaze2Segment, leverages the cognitive processes of human observers to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation algorithms. Methods: We conducted a user study with a group of experts and novices who were asked to perform manual segmentation tasks on a set of medical images using a gaze-based interface. The participants' eye movements were tracked and recorded while they performed the segmentation task, and their gaze patterns were analyzed to identify regions of high attention. We then used these gaze patterns as input to a deep learning model, which was trained to predict the corresponding segmentation masks. The performance of our Gaze2Segment approach was evaluated against traditional image segmentation methods, and the results were compared using several metrics. Results: Our preliminary results show promising improvements in segmentation accuracy and efficiency when incorporating eye-tracking technology into the segmentation process. The gaze patterns from expert observers were found to be more consistent and focused than those of novice observers, leading to better segmentation outcomes. Additionally, we observed that the integration of eye-tracking technology assisted in reducing the time required for manual segmentation, indicating improved efficacy and productivity. Discussion and Conclusion: The results of this pilot study suggest that integrating eye-tracking technology into medical image segmentation workflows has great potential for improving both accuracy and efficiency. By leveraging the cognitive processes of human observers, our proposed Gaze2Segment approach may enable the development of more robust, reliable, and interpretable segmentation models. Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for cross-modality medical image segmentation has shown great progress by domain-invariant feature learning or image appearance translation. Adapted feature learning usually cannot detect domain shifts at the pixel level and is not able to achieve good results in dense semantic segmentation tasks. Image appearance translation, e.g. CycleGAN, translates images into different styles with good appearance, despite its population, its semantic consistency is hardly to maintain and results in poor cross-modality segmentation. In this paper, we propose intra- and cross-modality semantic consistency (ICMSC) for UDA and our key insight is that the segmentation of synthesised images in different styles should be consistent. Specifically, our model consists of an image translation module and a domain-specific segmentation module. The image translation module is a standard CycleGAN, while the segmentation module contains two domain-specific segmentation networks. The intra-modality semantic consistency (IMSC) forces the reconstructed image after a cycle to be segmented in the same way as the original input image, while the cross-modality semantic consistency (CMSC) encourages the synthesized images after translation to be segmented exactly the same as before translation. Comprehensive experimental results on cross-modality hip joint bone segmentation show the effectiveness of our proposed method, which achieves an average DICE of 81.61% on the acetabulum and 88.16% on the proximal femur, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. It is worth to note that without UDA, a model trained on CT for hip joint bone segmentation is non-transferable to MRI and has almost zero-DICE segmentation.

The proposed approach, termed cross-modal progressive comprehension, utilizes both conceptual and semantic features to reduce the reliability of referring segmentation. The technique is based on a deep cognitive network that gradually refines its knowledge of the input image and language description, leading to more accurate object localization and classification. Experimental findings on two benchmark datasets demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods for referring segmentation.

This article proposes a new method of referring segmentation, a process of recognizing the object mentioned in a natural language sentence. This method, called “cross-modal progressive comprehension”, uses visual and linguistic features to improve the accuracy of the referring segmentation. It is based on a deep learning network which gradually refines its understanding of the input image and the natural language sentence, and the referring segmentation is thus made more precise. The experiments carried out on two standard datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "Impact of electrode density of states on transport through pyridine-linked single molecule junctions" explores the effect of electrode density of states on the transport properties of single molecule junctions containing pyridine linkers. The study investigates how the electrode density of states influences the electronic transport through these junctions and how this relationship can be utilised to control and manipulate the electronic properties of these systems. The results of the study provide valuable insights into the fundamental principles governing the electronic transport in single molecule junctions and have potential applications in the development of novel nanoscale electronic devices.

As a supervised learning task, the training of the deep neural network is intended to 'teach' the network to mimic the human visual perception that is represented by the image-label pairs in the training data. The super-resolution (SP) images are seen as easily perceivable by humans, but the conventionally trained deep network often has difficulty with such images. To mimic the human visual perception, it is desirable that the deep network should be able to understand not only the original images but also the SP images. We therefore propose a new method of deep learning that applies super-resolution data augmentation to the deep learning of medical image segmentation. The proposed method uses all the original training images as the training data, and after applying the super-resolution method, it obtains super-resolution images from the original images, and the original images and super-resolution images are combined to train the deep network. Testing the effectiveness of the method on four medical image datasets reveals that the method is effective and can consistently improve the performance of the conventional fully convolutional network for the biomedical image segmentation in both two-dimensional images and three-dimensional images. We also performed further studies to demonstrate that the proposed method can actually reduce the generalization gap.

Large, fine-grained image segmentation datasets, annotated at pixel-level, are difficult to obtain, particularly in medical imaging, where annotations also require expert knowledge. Weakly-supervised learning can train models by relying on weaker forms of annotation, such as scribbles. Here, we learn to segment using scribble annotations in an adversarial game. With unpaired segmentation masks, we train a multi-scale GAN to generate realistic segmentation masks at multiple resolutions, while we use scribbles to learn their correct position in the image. Central to model's success is novel attention gating mechanism, which we condition with adversarial signals to act as shape prior, resulting in better object localization at multiple scales. Subject to adversarial conditioning, segmentor learns attention maps that are semantic, suppress the noisy activations outside objects, and reduce the vanishing gradient problem in the deeper layers of the segmentor. We evaluated our model on several medical (ACDC, LVSC, CHAOS) and non-medical (PPSS) datasets, and we report performance levels matching those achieved by models trained with fully annotated segmentation masks. We also demonstrate extensions in variety of settings: semi-supervised learning; combining multiple scribble sources (a crowdsourcing scenario) and multi-task learning (combining scribble and mask supervision). We release expert-made scribble annotations for ACDC dataset, and the code used for the experiments, at https://vios-s.github.io/multiscale-adversarial-attention-gates

Robot perception systems need to perform reliable image segmentation in real-time on noisy, raw perception data. State-of-the-art segmentation approaches use large CNN models and carefully constructed datasets; however, these models focus on accuracy at the cost of real-time inference. Furthermore, the standard semantic segmentation datasets are not large enough for training CNNs without augmentation and are not representative of noisy, uncurated robot perception data. We propose improving the performance of real-time segmentation frameworks on robot perception data by transferring features learned from synthetic segmentation data. We show that pretraining real-time segmentation architectures with synthetic segmentation data instead of ImageNet improves fine-tuning performance by reducing bias learned in pretraining and closing the \textit{transfer gap} as a result. Our experiments show that our real-time robot perception models pretrained on synthetic data outperform those pretrained on ImageNet for every scale of fine-tuning data examined. Moreover, the degree to which synthetic pretraining outperforms ImageNet pretraining increases as availability of robot data decreases, making our approach attractive for robotics domains where dataset collection is hard and/or expensive.

If you sell your house before you have paid off your mortgage, you'll need to use the proceeds from the sale to pay off your mortgage first. This is typically done through the escrow process, where the buyer's funds are held until all liens and mortgages are satisfied. If the proceeds from the sale are greater than the balance of your mortgage, you'll receive the remaining funds. However, if the proceeds are less than the balance of your mortgage, you'll need to come up with the difference to pay off the mortgage in full. Additionally, if there are any prepayment penalties associated with your mortgage, you'll need to factor those in as well. Overall, the amount of money you'll make will depend on the current market value of your home and the outstanding balance on your mortgage.

Canon Enid Morgan remembers exactly how she felt when her husband sat down next to her, slipped his arm around her shoulders and told her that he had been called by God. 'It's not a choice, Enid,' he said. 'I am not choosing this life.' 'But what will I do?' she asked. 'How will I survive?' 'You'll have to be strong. You're my rock, remember.' 'How can you say that?' she asked. 'You've always been the strong one. I've always looked up to you.' 'And you always will,' he said. 'But I need you to be strong now. For me. For us.' 'I can't,' she said. 'I don't know how.' 'You can,' he said. 'You will.' And she did. She was strong for him, and for their children. She supported him through his ordination, and through his first parish. She was there for him when he was made Bishop, and when he became Archbishop. She was there for him when he was diagnosed with cancer, and she held him as he died. But she was never the same after he left her. The light in her eyes went out, and she became a shadow of her former self.

The ROAM method is introduced, which is a combination of random layer mixing and semi-supervised learning. By combining labelled and unlabelled examples during training, this method enhances feature representation and reduces overfitting by producing synthetic samples by a linear interpolation between images in the layers of the network. This technique has been successfully tested on several of the well-known datasets used in the field of computer vision, including image recognition and segmentation. The improvement obtained by ROAM over traditional supervised methods has been demonstrated using several test sets, comparing it with classical methods, and showing that it not only reduces reliance on human annotated images, but also that it can be used to its full potential to generate an accurate result.

We desgin a novel fully convolutional network architecture for shapes, denoted by Shape Fully Convolutional Networks (SFCN). 3D shapes are represented as graph structures in the SFCN architecture, based on novel graph convolution and pooling operations, which are similar to convolution and pooling operations used on images. Meanwhile, to build our SFCN architecture in the original image segmentation fully convolutional network (FCN) architecture, we also design and implement a generating operation} with bridging function. This ensures that the convolution and pooling operation we have designed can be successfully applied in the original FCN architecture. In this paper, we also present a new shape segmentation approach based on SFCN. Furthermore, we allow more general and challenging input, such as mixed datasets of different categories of shapes} which can prove the ability of our generalisation. In our approach, SFCNs are trained triangles-to-triangles by using three low-level geometric features as input. Finally, the feature voting-based multi-label graph cuts is adopted to optimise the segmentation results obtained by SFCN prediction. The experiment results show that our method can effectively learn and predict mixed shape datasets of either similar or different characteristics, and achieve excellent segmentation results.

In this paper, we explore the concept of rational sets in Euclidean spaces and spheres, with a particular focus on their properties and applications. We begin by defining rational sets and discussing their basic properties, including their relationship to algebraic sets and their behaviour under Möbius transformations. We then examine the topology of rational sets in Euclidean spaces, showing that they are dense and have a rich structure that is closely related to that of the underlying space. We also investigate the combinatorics of rational sets, demonstrating that they exhibit a fascinating variety of behaviours, including the existence of subset sums and intersection patterns. Next, we turn our attention to rational sets in spheres, where we encounter additional challenges and opportunities. We develop techniques for studying these sets, combining tools from algebraic geometry, functional analysis, and geometric measure theory. Our main results include the characterisation of rational sets in spheres as orbits of certain group actions, the study of their packing densities, and the construction of explicit examples of rational sets with desirable properties. Throughout the paper, we highlight connections between rational sets and other areas of mathematics, such as number theory, combinatorial optimisation, and theoretical computer science. We also discuss potential applications of rational sets, including coding theory, cryptography, and machine learning. Our work provides new insights into the nature of rational sets in Euclidean spaces and spheres, opening up fresh directions for research and offering a deeper understanding of the intricate relationships between algebra, geometry, and topology.

A recent British Medical Association (BMA) survey has unveiled concerning statistics for the UK healthcare sector as an increasing number of family doctors are considering leaving their profession or relocating for better pay and work-life balance. In a poll of 15,560 general practitioners (GPs), one in ten is said to be contemplating moving to countries for higher remuneration, with larger percentages of doctors also considering part-time work or leaving the medical profession entirely. The survey reveals that one in six GPs is considering moving to part-time roles to alleviate the stress of their demanding jobs, while 7 are deliberating quitting medicine for good. The medical profession, especially GPs, has been under immense pressure in recent years due to an increasing workload, demanding patients, and significant administrative burdens. The industry has also been hit with a recruitment and retention crisis, resulting in longer waiting times for patients seeking medical attention. This survey arrives at an interesting time, as family doctors in the UK have greatly benefited from a pay deal in the early 2000s, which saw their salaries increase by 50. However, this considerable wage increase has not significantly impacted the intentions of doctors to move abroad or seek alternative careers. In a statement addressing the revelations of this survey, a spokesperson from the Department of Health and Social Care has assured the public that they are increasing investment in general practice and have committed to hiring around 6,000 more primary care doctors by 2024. However, with such a large number of doctors considering leaving the profession altogether or moving to part-time work to cope with the increasing strain, it remains to be seen whether this investment will be enough to ensure the future stability of the UK's healthcare sector. In the meantime, patients may face longer waiting times, and rural communities may be at heightened risk of losing GP services altogether.

Introduction: The aim of this research is to propose a real-time predictive maintenance platform for business vehicles using 3d printer technology. This solution will enable businesses to reduce downtime, optimize operations and improve maintenance budgeting by detecting equipment failures before they occur. The proposed system relies on a combination of sensors, data analytics, and machine learning algorithms to monitor vehicle performance in real-time, identify potential issues, and provide recommendations for preventative maintenance. In addition the use of 3d printer technology offers an efficient and cost effective way of repairing broken parts. Methodology: This study uses literature review to gather information about existing technologies and approaches to predictive maintenance. A detailed analysis was conducted on various types of commercial vehicles currently in use and their associated components which need frequent maintenance and replacement. Data from different sources such as satellite imagery, sensor readings and historical records were collected, processed and analyzed through machine learning and statistical techniques. Finally, 3d printer technology was integrated into the algorithm to generate custom designed and manufactured replacement parts on demand. Results: The results demonstrate that the proposed real-time predictive maintenance platform can effectively detect and diagnose issues before any significant damage occurs in business vehicles. Furthermore, the application of 3d printer technology provides an efficient and cost-effective means of replacing faulty or critical replacement parts. Results indicated that the platform reduced overall maintenance costs while also optimizing fleet availability leading to improved operational efficiency. Conclusion: In conclusion, the implementation of a real-time predictive maintenance platform for business vehicles using 3d printer technology represents a major step forward in improving vehicle reliability and reducing maintenance costs. Further refinements and advancements of this systems are expected to have a positive impact on logistics industry overall.

We met on a rainy day in August. She was standing over the metal guard rails of an overpass, staring at the murky waters below. I was walking towards her. "It's a long way down," she said. I nodded. "Sure is." She looked at me then, and I saw the sadness in her eyes. "Do you ever feel like just giving up?" she asked. I swallowed hard. I wanted to tell her that I understood, that I'd been there before. But the words wouldn't come. "It's okay," she said softly. "I know how you feel." We stood there for a moment, staring at the dark water below. Then, slowly, she reached out and took my hand. "Let's get out of here," she said. And I knew then that I'd found a friend.

This academic paper aims to reduce the model variance of a rectal cancer segmentation network. The authors propose a novel approach that combines data augmentation techniques with a deep learning-based segmentation model. The proposed approach is evaluated on a large dataset of rectal cancer images and demonstrates significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to the baseline model. The results suggest that the proposed approach can effectively reduce the model variance and improve the generalization performance of the segmentation network. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the development of robust and accurate segmentation models for rectal cancer diagnosis.

Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) have shown remarkable performance in image classification tasks, while Random Forests (RF) have been successful in various classification and regression problems. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to combine the strengths of both models by integrating a DCNN with an RF classifier. Specifically, we use output of the DCNN as input to RF classifier, which results in Fast Random Forest Classifier (FRFC). We evaluate the effectiveness of FRFC on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms both DCNN and RF models in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Our results suggest that FRFC is a promising approach for image classification tasks, particularly in scenarios where computational resources are limited.

Radwan Hamed collapsed during a game in Belgium in 2006. Last year a judge ruled Spurs breached its duties to him. In a screening prior to signing for the club, an electrocardiogram test showed his heart was "unequivocally abnormal" but he was not stopped from playing. The club regretted a former employee had been remiss in their duties. In a statement, the family of Mr Hamed, who is now 27, said they were "relieved" a settlement had been reached, following a decade-long legal battle. "Just as Radwan had no choice but to start his difficult journey towards recovery, we had no choice but to start the difficult journey to obtain justice," they said. "We risked losing our home and faced personal financial ruin in order to pursue justice for our son. "The club did not tell us or Radwan about his potentially fatal condition. Had they done so, Radwan would not have continued to play football." The teenager collapsed during the game against Cercle Bruges on 4 August 2006 and was rushed to an intensive care unit but suffered oxygen starvation to his brain. In the 2015 hearing, Mr Justice Hickinbottom ruled the club was 70 liable or Mr Hamed's injuries and Dr Peter Mills, the Football Association's regional cardiologist for South East England, was 30 liable. The Premier League club will not be hit with a fee directly as their 70 portion was incurred by physicians they previously employed, who have agreed to indemnify the club. Football Association rules require all football academy recruits to be referred to a cardiologist to help identify those prone to potentially fatal heart conditions. Mr Hamed's MRI scan showed no obvious signs of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but Dr Mills wrote to Spurs saying the condition could not be excluded on these findings alone. Eleven months later, the teenager, who was unaware his tests had revealed an "abnormal" heart condition, signed a contract with Spurs. A spokesman for Spurs said: "The club wholeheartedly regrets that a former employee, as adjudged, was remiss in their duties to Radwan. "This judgment will hopefully now secure the best possible treatment and care for him."

The hypothesis that boreal bird species could have survived through the Ice Ages is backed by the fact that old differences between them exist. During the ice ages, the cold and coniferous forest habitats were occupied by boreal birds. Evidence for long-term survival and adaptation to these conditions can be obtained through genetic studies that demonstrate significant differentiation among various populations or lineages of these birds. In the Ice Ages, certain regions called refugia provided suitable living conditions that remained free of ice, allowing boreal forests to survive. Over time, the birds living in the refuges in the boreal regions may have become genetically different from other bird populations due to their isolation. The proof of this difference backs the belief that these avian communities could endure the tough circumstances of the Ice Ages. It is important to remember that ancient genetic differences do not necessarily indicate lasting survival during the Ice Ages. Genetic variation in bird populations may be influenced by additional elements such as habitat alterations or competition with other species. In order to confirm this hypothesis, additional research would be required, particularly in terms of comprehending the specific adjustments that these birds possess that enable them to endure chilly conditions.

In this paper, we present a novel approach for enumerating corners in tree-like tableaux, which are combinatorial objects that have found applications in various areas of mathematics and computer science. Our approach is based on a careful analysis of the structure of these tableaux, and involves the use of generating functions to encode the enumerative properties of their corners. We introduce a new statistic, called the corner number, which keeps track of the number of corners in each tableau. Using this statistic, we derive a recursively defined formula for the generating function of corners in tree-like tableaux. We then manipulate this formula to extract various enumerative results, including the total number of corners, the distribution of corners across different rows and columns, and the probability that a given cell belongs to a corner. Our methods are illustrated with examples and experimental data, and we discuss connections to related work in algebraic combinatorics and computational biology. The results of this paper contribute to a better understanding of the structural properties of tree-like tableaux, and demonstrate the power of generating function techniques in enumerative combinatorics.

This paper proposes a new validity index for fuzzy-possibilistic C-means clustering. The proposed index is based on the fuzzy-possibilistic concept and takes into account the uncertainty of the data. The index is evaluated through a series of experiments, which demonstrate its effectiveness in identifying the optimal number of clusters and its ability to handle noisy and overlapping data. The results show that the proposed index outperforms existing validity indices in terms of accuracy and robustness. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of clustering analysis by offering a new and effective validity index for fuzzy-possibilistic C-means clustering.

A system to identify and prioritize signal Prioritization in Urban networks Abstract There has been much recent interest towards real-time information about traffic, which Could be used to inform decisions affecting vehicles (e.g. traffic lights). This work identifies how it might Look if one's car became able to select its preferred route. It demonstrates that it can provide information such as The speed limit on a road when driven by a vehicle or Its proximity to other roadways, allowing an evaluation of signals priorities and their effects on speeds. We demonstrate two distinct methods from machine learning and statistics that allow us to make optimal selection of priority lines via dynamic Optimization. These methods are useful for the following purposes in a highly-urbanized setting with numerous lane closures during rush hours: 1) identifying and maximizing the number of open lanes of travel; 2) evaluating routes by choosing among different levels of priority between two or more road users; and 3) finding where those Locations best intersect eachother.

The fuzzy K -means problem is a generalization of the classical K -means problem to soft clusterings, i.e. clusterings where each points belongs to each cluster to some degree. Although popular in practice, prior to this work the fuzzy K -means problem has not been studied from a complexity theoretic or algorithmic perspective. We show that optimal solutions for fuzzy K -means cannot, in general, be expressed by radicals over the input points. Surprisingly, this already holds for very simple inputs in one-dimensional space. Hence, one cannot expect to compute optimal solutions exactly. We give the first (1) -approximation algorithms for the fuzzy K -means problem. First, we present a deterministic approximation algorithm whose runtime is polynomial in N and linear in the dimension D of the input set, given that K is constant, i.e. a polynomial time approximation algorithm given a fixed K. We achieve this result by showing that for each soft clustering there exists a hard clustering with comparable properties. Second, by using techniques known from coreset constructions for the K -means problem, we develop a deterministic approximation algorithm that runs in time almost linear in N but exponential in the dimension D. We complement these results with a randomized algorithm which imposes some natural restrictions on the input set and whose runtime is comparable to some of the most efficient approximation algorithms for K -means, i.e. linear in the number of points and the dimension, but exponential in the number of clusters.

RLCorrector: Reinforced Proofreading for Connectomics Image Segmentation abstract: Connectomics, the study of the neural connections within The brain, relies heavily on accurate image segmentation to identify and trace neural fibers. However, current segmentation methods often produce errors, particularly in the presence Of complex fiber crossings and other Challenging features. To address this challenge, we Propose RLCorrector, a novel reinforcement learning-based approach that leverages proofreading techniques to improve the accuracy of connectomics image segmentation. RLCorrector combines the strengths of deep learning-based segmentation methods with the accuracy And efficiency of proofreading techniques. Our approach consists of two main components: a segmentation model and a proofreader. The segmentation model generates an initial segmentation Of the input image, which is then passed through the proofreader. The proofreader Uses reinforcement learning to learn a policy that Corrects errors in the segmentation, iteratively refining the output until an accurate segmentation is achieved. We evaluate RLCorrector on several benchmark datasets and compare its performance to state-of-the-art segmentation methods. Our results show that RLCorrector significantly improves upon existing methods, with an average accuracy increase of 15% across all datasets. We also demonstrate the versatility of our approach by applying it to various segmentation tasks, including fiber tract Segmentation and synapse detection. our work has important implications for the field of connectomics, as accurate image segmentation is crucial for understanding the structure and function of the brain. RLCorrector offers a promising solution for improving the accuracy and efficiency of connectomics image segmentation, and Has the potential to enable new applications and insights in neuroscience research.

Java attempts to run trusted and untrusted code within the same virtual machine, with the only thing separating them being the permission system and visibility modifiers. A bug anywhere in the JVM may allow untrusted code to violate the security of its trusted neighbors. As we can see, the Java platform is not as secure as people might think. In fact, it has been said that the Java platform is even less secure than Microsoft's Windows platform. The article concluded that software companies should avoid using Java and consider other platforms such as C. The most popular programming language in the world is Java. But this high-level language isn't immune to security problems. In fact, the Java platform is arguably less secure than Microsoft's Windows platform. And though Sun Microsystems has introduced some improved security features in recent years, many experts believe that the Java platform is simply too insecure for enterprise applications. So there you have it. The most popular programming language in the world is also one of the least secure.

This paper presents a novel Spatial Guided Self-supervised Clustering Network (SGS-Net) for medical image segmentation. The proposed approach utilizes a self-supervised clustering method to learn meaningful representations from unlabeled data, which are then used to guide the segmentation network. The SGS-Net incorporates a spatial guidance module that enforces consistency between the learned clusters and the spatial structure of the image, improving the accuracy of the segmentation results. Experimental results on two medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

Abstract This paper discusses three important concerns, namely (i) how precisely one can create efficient, exact reconstructions of graph (in graph theory) given their degree-4 sum-of-squares structure (which is a particular representation scheme but can be perfectly approximated by some other such schemes not presented here), and (ii) how it actually works at certain sorts of computational problems - in comparison to, e.g., ordinary linear programming, which has no such question at all. The answers require insights into the general difficulties we encounter compared with modern machine learning methods when dealing with these representations. We often discuss, among other things, the limitations on accuracy that this technique creates. At some cases we show instances where many sub-optimal solutions are obtained because our reconstruction algorithm cannot converge fast enough or sufficiently close the precision-vs.-accuracy trade-off between precision and computation time. However, we present new theoretical findings demonstrating that only after many iterations the result remains quite unstable under various statistical/statistical interpretation rules for our representations.

The heaving mass of flesh and fur gurgled slowly to a halt. Shanes body moved slowly with the beast as its energy faded. He puffed into the cold morning air, arms wrapped around the giant almost in embrace. He gently tugged at his blade and eased it slowly from the animals neck. Blood gushed from the wound before slowing to a quiet stream. The beast lay still with the forest it called home, its warmth in life ever fading. Shane looked upon his kill with a sense of guilt. Its magnificence was eerily apparent as it sprawled in front of him. He placed both hands on the head of the beast and closed his eyes, taking a deep breath through his nose. The smell of the creature mixed with the trees and the earth, its aroma flowing into Shane as he took a moment to appreciate his bounty. The sacrifice would not go unnoticed. He slowly opened his eyes and looked to the sky, the sun filtering through the treetops, the clouds drifting silently by. "Thankyou great forest." He began. "You have provided one of yours so that I might provide for my own. I'm sorry I had to take this life. It will provide the fuel for many more." He moved his hands slowly upon the animals great neck. "The cycle continues." He let out a long sigh as he began to cut into the body, pulling his knife along slowly like the opening of a zip. Its organs fell and slopped into a heap at its side. Shane reached inside the great giant, its warmth still evident, pulling at the remaining parts and motioning them to the ground. He wiped his hands in the undergrowth and slipped his blade into its holder on his belt. Placing his hands once more upon the animal, he whispered a final thanks. He grabbed one front leg and pulled it upwards, its muscles large and imposing, a shadow of what had thundered through the trees not long earlier. He pulled hard at the leg and twisted his body with the animal, draping it across his back. With a tense grit of his teeth and a final heave, he dragged the other across his shoulder. "You will not be forgotten" he said, but there was no answer.

This research demonstrates the potential of neutron stars as methods to investigate extreme solar dense matter, which is important in explaining the properties and behavior of dense solid cores. By collecting findings from astronomical phenomena involving neutron stars, such as electromagnetic waves or X-ray emissions, scientists can gain insights into the basic physics governing these astronomical objects with high accuracy. The results provided herein show that observing neutron star populations provides useful data about the equation of State (EoS) of asymmetric nuclear matter at unparalleled densities, shedding light on processes like core-collapse supernovae explosions and the birth of black holes. Overall, this study highlights the significance of utilizing astronomical phenomenon including neutron stars as a means towards improving our comprehension of ultrahighdensity quark particle plasma states prevalent within nuclearsized states deep inside terrestrial nuclei.

This work proposes a novel method of semantic segmentation which makes use of the extraneous information contained in the image. For a long time, we have been making our segmentations with only the content of the image. Now, besides the visual content of the image, we have the importance of its external environment. Our method is composed of two main components: the first is a knowledge injection mechanism which, by the help of a textual lexicon, integrates a variety of external information such as object categories and scene understanding into the feature extraction process; the second is a priority-aware mechanism which adapts the features according to the importance of each pixel in the image. The evaluation is done on various datasets, including Cityscapes, Pascal VOC and Coco. The evaluation is shown to produce significant improvements over the state of the art. The most important results are: * An efficient knowledge injection mechanism which integrates external knowledge from a variety of sources without the need for manual annotation. * A priority-aware mechanism which adapts the feature representations to the importance of each pixel, improving the overall performance and robustness of the model. This work has important implications for applications where accurate semantic segmentation is essential, such as driving, robots and medical image analysis.

"This paper investigates the influence on learning mechanisms of crowd-based environments, in which large numbers of people interact over an extended period with common challenges at common points within these communities. We show that a large number of individuals will be exposed to a limited set of salient features, and this group structure can have a significant effect on their capacity for learning. We provide evidence that the influence of the social environment on learning in general, not just MOOC related learning, derives from both diffusion (spread) effects and structural constraints on the formation of knowledge. The effects were evident across a wide range of tasks including reading comprehension, knowledge integration exercises and multiple choice question types."

The trial concluded in 2019 and the priest had already served more than half of the sentence before being pardoned by Pope Francis on Sunday. He added that M.C. was "relieved and happy" to have been pardoned by the Pope. This is not the first time that Pope Francis has intervened in a Vatileaks case. In 2012, he pardoned Paolo Gabriele, a Vatican employee who had been sentenced to 18 months in prison for leaking confidential documents. The pardon of M.C. is seen as an indication that the Pope is willing to take a stand against those who abuse their power within the Church. It also shows that he is committed to transparency and accountability within the institution. The decision to release M.C. has been praised by many Church leaders who believe that it is an important step towards ensuring justice for all and restoring trust in the Catholic Church.

The ceasefire was supposed to open the way to aid deliveries in Syria, followed by the rolling out of a co-ordinated military campaign by Moscow and Washington against so-called Islamic State (IS) targets and other groups linked to al-Qaeda. In practice the latest attacks on the aid convoy and hospital seem to have taken things back to square one. Indeed the cynicism of the attack on the convoy in particular is remarkable. The Russians have shown drone footage of their monitoring of the convoy, the route and location of which were pre-announced. But what happened next is disputed. The Americans are hinting strongly that the convoy was attacked from the air by a pair of Sukhoi Su-24 jets - either Russian or Syrian. It makes little difference to Washington, which holds Moscow responsible either way. In contrast, the Russians deny any culpability; they say their aircraft were not in the area and that the destruction of the convoy was the result of action on the ground - the implication is from rebel forces. Quite what purpose anyone had in destroying the convoy is unclear, other than to jeopardise the ceasefire. But the seeds of its collapse were there from the outset. Firstly, the ceasefire was negotiated not between the warring parties on the ground but by two of their patrons - the US and Russia - who are both engaged in the conflict, in different ways and with very different goals. Changes in the cellular expression of miRNAs, which occur during the disease progression and in various patients, demonstrate the impact of HIVSIV infection on them. The results of our study show that SIV infection affects the levels of primary transcripts and mature forms of miRs-29a, -29b, -9, and -146a. Our demonstration indicates that the SIV 3' UTR contains operational MREs for each of the four miRNAs. Significantly, the miRNAs control the propagation of viruses and the quantity of viral RNA in macrophages, which are the main cells targeted by the virus in the central nervous system, resulting in inflammation that causes HIV-related cognitive impairments. This report can provide assistance in identifying miRNAs that specifically target viral RNAs and HIVSIV, as well as in discovering miRNAs that could be targeted by new treatments for HIV.

The concept of parallel universes and multiple possible outcomes has long been a subject of speculation and debate within physics. In recent years, this idea has also become increasingly significant in field of quantum computing, where it is central to understanding the fundamental nature of computational processes. This scholarly article provides overview of "many-world" or "quantum parallelism" approaches in computing. It begins by discussing classical analogies such as branching timelines, parallel processing, and probability distributions, before diving into how these concepts are applied directly to quantum mechanics. This includes discussions on superposition states, entanglement, and measurement, which form the core principles of quantum computing. The authors then explore some of current research and development of many-worlds models of computation. These include ideas like reversible gates, quantum error correction, adiabatic algorithms, and so on. Additionally, they also examine potential applications of these new models in areas such as cryptography, optimization problems, and drug discovery. Throughout, the article aims to provide readers with a broad yet accessible introduction to "many-worlds" concepts in quantum computers. By exploring both theoretical foundations and practical implementations, this work offers insight into promising developments taking place at intersection of computer science and quantum theory.

Abstract. Eikonal Active Regions (EAR) (a.k.a region active contour maps, or ARCs), are widely used on 3D surfaces to create local information for classification and automated localization; however they do not provide adequate resolution in many circumstances due to overburdening data. To overcome this limitations, we present our proposed two-layer feature selection method that exploits the overlap between a surface's ERs with its high curvature and their correlation with other ERs to achieve high spatial resolution while minimising cost. Our algorithm operates by applying a regularisation kernel based on the geometrical proximity between ER regions to extract local features at higher distances, which subsequently result in an improvement in resolution. We observe consistent performance improvements up to 1 km using ER with a resolution of ~3 m across several environments and applications such as mobile robots, surveillance cameras, indoor mapping and augmented reality systems without relying on additional data collection techniques which may be more resource intensive than conventional topological segmenting methods. Our analysis results also show better generalisations than commonly available solutions especially in low elevation situations resulting in more complete datasets without unnecessary data degradation.

Despite the remarkable performance of deep learning methods on various tasks, most cutting-edge models rely heavily on large-scale annotated training examples, which are often unavailable for clinical and health care tasks. The labeling costs for medical images are very high, especially in medical image segmentation, which typically requires intensive pixel/voxel-wise labeling. Therefore, the strong capability of learning and generalizing from limited supervision, including a limited amount of annotations, sparse annotations, and inaccurate annotations, is crucial for the successful application of deep learning models in medical image segmentation. However, due to its intrinsic difficulty, segmentation with limited supervision is challenging and specific model design and/or learning strategies are needed. In this paper, we provide a systematic and up-to-date review of the solutions above, with summaries and comments about the methodologies. We also highlight several problems in this field, discussed future directions observing further investigations.

DeepIGeoS is a novel deep learning-based interactive geodesic framework for medical image segmentation. This framework relies on convolutional neural networks to extract features from medical images and employs interactive segmentation to further improve the accuracy of the results. The proposed method provides a friendly interaction mechanism for the interactive segmentation, so that the medical experts can modify the segmentation result as required. The experimental results demonstrate that DeepIGeoS outperforms other methods in terms of the accuracy of the segmentation and the efficiency of the computation, and is thus a powerful tool for the analysis of medical images.

It was all over the news. "The Woman that Wouldn't Wake," "Sleeping Beauty Come to Life," the headlines all read. Physicians were baffled, and the rest of us? We had no idea what this meant. They ran tests on the poor girl. No breath, no heartbeat. It was no illness that had ever been seen before. The case inspired me, in my last year of medical school. I was determined to find an answer. It was a challenge. She was kept in a solitary room; the family's wishes. They were sparing no expense to find out what was wrong with their daughter. She had no history of illness; in fact, she was perfectly healthy. Aside from the fact that she had no pulse, or brain activity. It seemed as though she was just..... gone. An empty shell. Other physicians gave up the search early on, resigning the poor soul to sleep eternity away. I could not do that. She was so young. There are things you can only experience in the first hundred years, after all. Every century is irreplaceable. But even I had to give up when we could tell that the tissue was wasting away on the child's small body. There was nothing that could be done. She would never wake up. The only thing we could do was name the illness. And I called it: Death.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in the field of healthcare, which involves identifying and separating different regions of interest within an image. However, obtaining high-quality annotations for training segmentation models can be time-consuming and expensive. In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised medical image segmentation approach that leverages learning consistency under transformations. Specifically, we introduce a novel consistency loss function that encourages the model to learn consistent segmentation results across different transformations of the input image. We also propose a novel transformation-invariant feature extraction method that can be used to improve the performance of the segmentation model. Our approach is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, and the results show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and robustness. Overall, our work demonstrates the potential of semi-supervised learning for medical image segmentation and highlights the importance of learning consistency under transformations for improving the performance of such models.

Crowd counting from unconstrained scene images is a crucial task in many real-world applications like urban surveillance and management, but it is greatly challenged by the camera's perspective that causes huge appearance variations in people's scales and rotations. Conventional methods address such challenges by resorting to fixed multi-scale architectures that are often unable to cover the largely varied scales while ignoring the rotation variations. In this paper, we propose a unified neural network framework, named Deep Recurrent Spatial-Aware Network, which adaptively addresses the two issues in a learnable spatial transform module with a region-wise refinement process. Specifically, our framework incorporates a Recurrent Spatial-Aware Refinement (RSAR) module iteratively conducting two components: i) a Spatial Transformer Network that dynamically locates an attentional region from the crowd density map and transforms it to the suitable scale and rotation for optimal crowd estimation; ii) a Local Refinement Network that refines the density map of the attended region with residual learning. Extensive experiments on four challenging benchmarks show the effectiveness of our approach. Specifically, comparing with the existing best-performing methods, we achieve an improvement of 12 on the largest dataset WorldExpo'10 and 22.8 on the most challenging dataset UCFCC50.

In this paper, we present a novel approach to multi-object tracking that combines the strengths of category-agnostic object detection and vision-based tracking. Our proposed method, called "Track, then Decide," leverages a deep learning framework to simultaneously detect objects across different categories and track them over time, without requiring any predefined catagory information or annotations. Existing approaches to multi-object tracking typically rely on categorical information to distinguish between objects, which can be limiting in real-world scenarios where objects may belong to various categories or have similer appearances. In contrast, our method employs a category-agnostic approach that focuses on the spatial and temporal consistency of objects, enabling it to handle diverse object categories and occlusions. The key innovation of our method is the integration of a tracking-by-detection strategy with a category-agnostic object detection algorithm. This allows us to first detect objects without assuming any specific catagory, and then associate detected objects across frames using a robust tracking mechanism. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets, showing improved performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Our main contributions are threefold: (1) we introduce a category-agnostic vision-based multi-object tracking framework that does not require prior knowledge of object categories; (2) we develop a novel tracking-by-detection mechanism that associates objects across frames based on their spatial and temporal consistency; and (3) we demonstrate the superiority of our approach through thorough evaluations on multiple datasets. This work has important implications for various computer vision applications, such as autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics, where the ability to effectively track multiple objects in real-time, regardless of their categories, is crucial.
