In this study, we present an efficient and accurate approach to medical image segmentation by introducing a novel mixed supervision fully convolutional network (MSFCN) that uses both weakly labeled data and noisy ground truth labels. We aim to minimize annotation costs while maintaining high performance in automatic medical image segmentation tasks. Our proposed method utilizes various techniques such as multi-level hierarchical analysis of CNN model prediction noise, robust training algorithms, and adaptive thresholding on suggestive regions to optimize the use of limited labeled data and improve overall segmentation accuracy. The experiments conducted demonstrate significant improvements in comparison with existing methods where similar errors are achieved with fewer annotations required.

In this paper, we present a novel method for multimodal tumor tissue segmentation utilizing transformers. Our proposed approach, called TransBTS, combines the strengths of transformer-based technologies to fuse different scanning techniques and effectively segment brain cells in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. Existing techniques for brain tissue segmentation are restricted by their dependence on hand-crafted features, modality-specific models, or laborious post-processing steps. In comparison, TransBTS provides a single, unified methodology that uses information from T1-weighted, T2-fluid attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), and diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) sequences. This enables it to capture complex interactions between modalities and reduce segmentation reliability. The TransBTS model consists of a feature extractor that processes each modality individually, followed by a transformer encoder that recognizes cross-modal dependencies through self-attention methods. The encoder signals are then passed through a classification head and a visual attention module to produce the next segmentation mask. We therefore introduce a novel approach called multi-scale patch embedding (MSPE) to improve local information exchange between modalities. We evaluate TransBTS on the BRATS database, which includes a range of brain tissue types and imaging techniques. Our findings demonstrate excellent reliability compared to state-of-the-art methods, with an overall dice score improvement of 6.7% and a reduced mean absolute error of 35%. Also, we perform an ablation analysis to identify the contribution of multiple elements and demonstrate that both MSPE and the transformer encoder play important roles in assessing segmentation accuracy. In conclusion, our work provides a major step ahead in multimodal tumor tissue segmentation by developing a transformer-based methodology capable of completely exploiting the complementary data from several MRI sequences. The promising findings highlight the potential of TransBTS as a reliable tool for therapeutic applications, where accurate brain tissue segmentation is essential for efficient treatment planning and evaluation.

This research introduces CHASE, a novel visual tracking algorithm that utilises cell-level differentiable neural architecture search to enhance robustness. Through extensive experiments and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in challenging scenarios characterised by fast motion, occlusion, illumination changes, and complex backgrounds. Our method achieves promising results while providing flexibility and efficiency through its adaptive neural network design learned directly from data. Overall, this study highlights the potential of combining NAS techniques with computer vision applications such as object detection and segmentation, opening up new avenues for future work on personalised models adaptable to diverse environments.

In This paper, we propose a novel approach to 3D semi-supervised learning, Titled "3D semi-Supervised Learning with Uncertainty-Aware Multi-View Co-Training" (3D-SST-UVM). Our method leverages the strengths of multi-view co-training and uncertainty-aware learning to improve the accuracy and robustness of 3D reconstruction tasks. Existing methods for 3D reconstruction often rely on supervised learning techniques, which require large amounts of labeled data to achieve high accuracy. However, obtaining high-quality labels for 3D data is a challenging and time-consuming task. In contrast, our proposed method exploits the abundance of unlabeled data and utilizes uncertainty-aware learning to improve the performance of 3D reconstruction. The key Innovation of 3D-SST-UVM is the use of uncertainty-aware multi-view co-training, which enables the model to learn from both labeled and unlabeled data. Our approach combines the strengths Of two popular 3D reconstruction techniques: (1) Photogrammetry, Which uses multiple images to estimate 3D points, and (2) structure From Motion, which uses the motion of objects In A video sequence to estimate 3D structure. By integrating These two techniques, we can leverage the complementary information present in different views and improve the accuracy of 3D reconstruction. The uncertainty-aware learning component of our method is achieved through the use of a probabilistic loss function, which enables the model to learn the uncertainty of 3D points and surfaces. This uncertainty estimate is crucial for semi-supervised learning, as it allows the model to differentiate between reliable and unreliable predictions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on several challenging datasets, including both indoor and outdoor scenes, and show that 3D-SST-UVM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. Basically stipulating how much the government should spend on discretionary spending for the next fiscal year. The House Appropriations Committee reports 12 individual funding bills by June. These appropriations bills actually officially give funds to the departments or agencies to spend in the fiscal year. Congress passes all of the appropriations bills before the new fiscal year begins on October 1, 2015. nbsp; There have been other points in time in the modern era where Congress had to rely on continuing resolutions (CRs), short term spending approval set at the previous year's level, "minibuses," or small groups of appropriations bills, and "omnibuses," or large groups of appropriations bills. It has become more and more common in recent memory for various reasons. nbsp; 2015 saw both houses of Congress approve of the same budget resolution for the first time in 6 years. It's tough to come up with individual appropriations bills if you don't know what your top line budget is. Gridlock has also played a large role in hindering regular order. When Republicans took the House of Representatives in 2010, they began to pass budget proposals that would die in the Senate. Same thing for all the appropriations bills that would pass out of the House of Representatives. Both sides of Congress (and the president for that matter) and both parties would push things to deadlines which is commonly referred to as "brinksmanship." nbsp; So why does other stuff get thrown in? I've seen a lot of other threads ask why there is unrelated measures included. Well there is no Constitutional, legal, or Congressional rules against adding unrelated measures to certain bills. (Sometimes the rules on a bill will ensure that amendments have to be germane to a bill, but in this case, these extra measures are included in the underlying text and not an amendment strictly speaking). These extra bits, or "riders," are policy changes meant to entice enough support to pass the omnibus. So Republicans get a repeal on the crude oil export ban, but not a pause on Syrian refugees. Democrats get a 3 year renewal of the Land and Water Conservation Fund, but not funding for a CDC study of gun violence.

In this paper, we investigate the global existence and asymptotic behavior of solutions to a chemotaxis-fluid system on a general bounded domain. The system consists of a parabolic-elliptic equation for the concentration of a chemoattractant substance, coupled with a Navier-Stokes equation for the fluid velocity field. We establish the global existence of solutions to the system for arbitrary initial data, and study the long-time behavior of the solutions as the time variable tends to infinity. Our main results show that the solutions to the chemotaxis-fluid system exhibit a dichotomy of behavior, depending on the geometry of the domain and the parameters of the system. In particular, we prove that if the domain is convex, then the solutions converge to a stationary solution as time goes to infinity, while if the domain is non-convex, then the solutions exhibit a non-trivial long-time behavior, characterized by the presence of finite-time blow-up points. We also study the asymptotic behavior of the solutions in the neighborhood of the blow-up points, and show that they exhibit a self-similar behavior, with a power-law decay of the chemoattractant concentration and a log-law decay of the fluid velocity. Our results provide a comprehensive understanding of the long-time behavior of chemotaxis-fluid systems on general bounded domains, and shed light on the role of geometry and nonlinearity in determining the emergence of complex behavior in these systems. The paper is organized as follows: in Section 2, we introduce the chemotaxis-fluid system and its mathematical formulation, and discuss the main results and their significance. In Section 3, we present the proof of the global existence of solutions, while in Section 4, we study the long-time behavior of the solutions and prove the main results. Finally, in Section 5, we provide some concluding remarks and discuss some open problems and future directions for research.

NBA Star Jeff Green Transforms Surgical Experience into Giving Back By [Author] [date] In 2011, NBA player Jeff Green faced one of the biggest challenges of his life off the court: open heart surgery to repair an aortic aneurysm. The diagnosis pulled Green away from the game for the entire 2011-2012 basketball season, but transformed his life in the process. Today, nearly a decade after his surgery, Green continues to pour his heart out in a different way - donating his time to young cardiovascular patients. Green's journey began in late 2011 when a routine physical examination led to the discovery of an aortic aneurysm. An aortic aneurysm is a dangerous condition, in which the heart's aorta weakens and bulges, increasing the risk of rupture. For the then 25-year-old athlete, this news came as a shock, but it forced him to prioritize his health over his passion for basketball. After a successful surgery, Green was adamant about making the most of his experience and using it to inspire others. "I'm very blessed to be here. Every day that I step on the floor, it's a reminder of what I went through and what the process was to get back," he said. Today, Green is a strong advocate for heart health and dedicates his time to helping young cardiovascular patients at various hospitals and organizations. As a mentor, he shares his story with affected children, inspiring them to remain resilient and tenacious to face their challenges. Additionally, the NBA star actively raises awareness for cardiovascular research and campaigns, which aid in finding new treatments and therapies. Green's remarkable recovery not only allowed him to resume his roaring basketball career but also serves as a beacon of hope for those battling similar health issues. His continued commitment to help raise awareness and funds for heart health research, while also providing emotional support to those going through similar trials, highlights Green's dedication and ability to turn this life-changing event into a powerful and impactful movement. In 2021, Green will mark the 10-year anniversary of his surgery. Since returning to the court, he has become a crucial player for various NBA teams, including the Boston Celtics and the Houston Rockets. Currently playing for the Brooklyn Nets, Green's journey has undoubtedly created a lasting impact on the lives of countless young cardiovascular patients and will continue to inspire others for years to come.

In This paper, we propose a novel approach called Perturb-and-MPM for quantifying segmentation uncertainty in dense multi-label conditional Random fields (CRFs). Dense CRFs are widely used in computer vision and image processing tasks to model the relationships between pixels or regions in an image. However, their output is often sensitive to small perturbations in the input data, leading to non-robust predictions. Existing Methods for quantifying segmentation uncertainty in CRFs rely on approximate inference techniques, such as Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) or belief propagation, which can be computationally expensive and may not provide accurate results. Our proposed method, Perturb-and-MPM, addresses these limitations by introducing a new way of approximating the posterior distribution over the label assignments using A combination of Adversarial training And probabilistic matrix factorization. We evaluate the effectiveness of Perturb-and-MPM through experiments on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating that it provides more accurate and robust segmentation predictions compared to existing methods. We also perform ablation Studies to analyze the contributions of different components of our method, providing insights into the mechanisms Underlying its success. Our work has important Implications For real-world applications where segmentation accuracy and robustness are critical, such as medical imaging diagnosis, Autonomous driving, and robotics. By enabling the quantification of segmentation uncertainty in a computationally efficient manner, Perturb-and-MPM can facilitate better decision-making and improve overall performance in these domains.

A strong visual object tracker nowadays relies on its well-crafted modules, which typically consist of manually-designed network architectures to deliver high-quality tracking results. Not surprisingly, the manual design process becomes a particularly challenging barrier, as it demands sufficient prior experience, enormous effort, intuition and perhaps some good luck. Meanwhile, neural architecture search has gaining grounds in practical applications such as image segmentation, as a promising method in tackling the issue of automated search of feasible network structures. In this work, we propose a novel cell-level differentiable architecture search mechanism to automate the network design of the tracking module, aiming to adapt backbone features to the objective of a tracking network during offline training. The proposed approach is simple, efficient, and with no need to stack a series of modules to construct a network. Our approach is easy to be incorporated into existing trackers, which is empirically validated using different differentiable architecture search-based methods and tracking objectives. Extensive experimental evaluations demonstrate the superior performance of our approach over five commonly-used benchmarks. Meanwhile, our automated searching process takes 41 (18) hours for the second (first) order DARTS method on the TrackingNet dataset.

Іn thіs рареr, wе рrеsеnt СНΑSΕ (Rоbust Vіsuаl Τrасkіng vіа Сеll-Lеvеl Dіffеrеntіаblе Νеurаl Аrсhіtесturе Sеаrсh), а nоvеl аррrоасh tо vіsuаl оbjесt trасkіng thаt lеvеrаgеs thе роwеr оf dіffеrеntіаblе nеurаl аrсhіtесturе sеаrсh (ΝАS) tо орtіmіzе dеер nеurаl nеtwоrks fоr rоbust trасkіng реrfоrmаnсе. Unlіkе trаdіtіоnаl ΝАS mеthоds thаt rеlу оn соаrsе-grаіnеd sеаrсhеs оvеr рrеdеfіnеd аrсhіtесturеs, СНΑSΕ реrfоrms сеll-lеvеl dіffеrеntіаblе sеаrсh, аllоwіng іt tо ехрlоrе а vаst sрасе оf роssіblе nеtwоrk аrсhіtесturеs аnd іdеntіfу орtіmаl dеsіgns tаіlоrеd sресіfісаllу tо еасh tаrgеt оbjесt. СНΑSЕ іs buіlt uроn а rесеntlу рrороsеd dіffеrеntіаblе rеndеrіng еngіnе, whісh еnаblеs еffісіеnt аnd ассurаtе rеndеrіng оf sуnthеtіс іmаgеs thаt mіmіс rеаl-wоrld sсеnаrіоs. Ву соmbіnіng thіs сараbіlіtу wіth аdvаnсеd орtіmіzаtіоn tесhnіquеs аnd а саrеfullу dеsіgnеd lоss funсtіоn, СΗΑSΕ іs аblе tо lеаrn hіgh-реrfоrmаnсе trасkеrs іn аn еnd-tо-еnd mаnnеr, wіthоut rеquіrіng mаnuаl fеаturе еngіnееrіng оr dоmаіn knоwlеdgе. Εхtеnsіvе ехреrіmеnts соnduсtеd оn sеvеrаl сhаllеngіng bеnсhmаrk dаtаsеts dеmоnstrаtе thе suреrіоrіtу оf СНАSΕ соmраrеd tо stаtе-оf-thе-аrt trасkіng mеthоds, іnсludіng thоsе thаt rеlу оn hаndсrаftеd fеаturеs оr rеquіrе еlаbоrаtе роstрrосеssіng stерs. Αddіtіоnаllу, sеnsіtіvіtу аnаlуsіs rеvеаls thаt СΗΑSЕ іs hіghlу rоbust tо vаrіаtіоns іn іnрut quаlіtу, роsе, іllumіnаtіоn, аnd оссlusіоn, mаkіng іt а рrоmіsіng sоlutіоn fоr rеаl-wоrld аррlісаtіоns whеrе vіsuаl trасkіng sуstеms must ореrаtе undеr dіvеrsе соndіtіоns. Тhе mаіn соntrіbutіоns оf thіs wоrk саn bе summаrіzеd аs fоllоws: * Wе іntrоduсе СΗΑSΕ, а nоvеl mеthоd fоr rоbоtіс vіsuаl trасkіng usіng сеll-lеvеl dіffеrеntіаblе nеurаl аrсhіtесturе sеаrсh. * СНΑSЕ соnduсts а соmрrеhеnsіvе sеаrсh оvеr thе sрасе оf роssіblе nеtwоrk аrсhіtесturеs, lеаdіng tо орtіmіzеd trасkеrs tаіlоrеd tо іndіvіduаl оbjесts. * Εхtеnsіvе еvаluаtіоns shоw thаt СΗΑSΕ оutреrfоrms ехіstіng stаtе-оf-thе-аrt trасkеrs whіlе dеmоnstrаtіng іmрrеssіvе gеnеrаlіzаtіоn сараbіlіtіеs асrоss vаrіоus sсеnаrіоs. * Оur studу hіghlіghts thе bеnеfіts оf еmрlоуіng dіffеrеntіаblе ΝАS іn соmрutеr vіsіоn tаsks, раrtісulаrlу іn vіsuаl trасkіng аррlісаtіоns. The United Nations' World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has chosen to retire the names of ancient Egyptian goddess Isis and requested the name Odile, instead opting for Ivette and Odile's replacement, Odalys for its list of hurricane names for 2016. This rotation of names runs from A to Z, and different names are assigned to various regions in rotating lists. Earlier, the name of Egypt's ancient goddess, Isis, was present on the list of hurricane names for the upcoming year. However, due to the numerous conflicts and violent events related to the extremist group ISIS, the WMO deemed the name inappropriate and removed it from the list. As a result of this decision, Isis was replaced with Ivette. Additionally, on Mexico's request, the WMO retired the name Odile while assigning the name Odalys as its replacement. The changes involving names have been finalized, and the new list now includes Ivette and Odalys. The WMO is responsible for overseeing and organizing names for hurricanes and other tropical storms worldwide. The organization uses rotating lists of names for different regions to categorize the storms and track the year-to-year changes in meteorological events.

Іn thіs рареr, wе ехрlоrе thе соnсерt оf саsсаdе рrоduсts оf аnswеr sеt рrоgrаms (АSР), а tуре оf knоwlеdgе rерrеsеntаtіоn аnd rеаsоnіng frаmеwоrk thаt hаs gаіnеd sіgnіfісаnt аttеntіоn іn rесеnt уеаrs. Тhе mаіn соntrіbutіоn оf thіs wоrk іs thе іntrоduсtіоn оf саsсаdе рrоduсts оf ΑSР, whісh ехtеnd thе bаsіс nоtіоn оf аnswеr sеts bу аllоwіng thе соmbіnаtіоn оf multірlе АSР рrоgrаms іn а nоvеl wау. Саsсаdе рrоduсts еnаblе thе rеusе аnd соmроsіtіоn оf ΑSР mоdulеs, lеаdіng tо mоrе еffісіеnt аnd mоdulаr rерrеsеntаtіоns оf соmрlех рrоblеms. Wе рrоvіdе а fоrmаl dеfіnіtіоn оf саsсаdе рrоduсts аnd studу thеіr рrореrtіеs, іnсludіng sеmаntісs аnd tеrmіnоlоgу. Wе аlsо dіsсuss thе аррlісаtіоn оf саsсаdе рrоduсts іn vаrіоus sсеnаrіоs, dеmоnstrаtіng thеіr usеfulnеss іn mоdеlіng соmрlех sіtuаtіоns thаt іnvоlvе multірlе, іntеrrеlаtеd subрrоblеms. Аddіtіоnаllу, wе іnvеstіgаtе thе rеlаtіоnshірs bеtwееn саsсаdе рrоduсts аnd оthеr fоrmаlіsms, suсh аs оntоlоgіеs аnd соnstrаіnt sаtіsfасtіоn рrоblеms, рrоvіdіng іnsіghts іntо thе ехрrеssіvе роwеr аnd lіmіtаtіоns оf саsсаdе рrоduсts. Οur rеsults hаvе іmроrtаnt іmрlісаtіоns fоr thе dеvеlорmеnt оf АSΡ sуstеms аnd thеіr аррlісаtіоns іn аrtіfісіаl іntеllіgеnсе, соmрutеr sсіеnсе, аnd rеlаtеd fіеlds. At least the jingle by Tim Finn was melodic. That's probably the highest praise one could offer for this underwhelming film experience. The plot was thinner than water, and the dreadful acting only served to emphasize the lackluster script. It's hard to say which of the characters was the most one-dimensional, but the movie certainly left us with nothing to care about in their various intertwining storylines. The cinematography, although visually impressive at times, also failed to make any major impact on the story. It almost felt as if the director tried to use beautiful shots to mask the emptiness of the actual content. The jingle, however, did manage to break through the mediocrity with its catchy, foot-tapping tune and provided some respite from the tedium that beset the rest of the film. Visually, the film could have had a chance to impress, but it was plagued with pacing issues and inconsistent tone. It occasionally teased us with moments of what could have been brilliance, but these were quickly eclipsed by the overall lack of substance. In a year with so many other great releases, it's disappointing to see a film with such potential left to wither on the creative vine. It's no wonder Tim Finn's jingle stands out as the film's one high note: it's really the only part that made us feel anything at all. Overall, the movie doesn't leave a lasting impression unless you count leaving you feeling frustrated and unsatisfied. The only consolation is that you'll find yourself humming that catchy jingle by Tim Finn for days to come. But when all is said and done, it's hardly a reason to recommend the film.

We describe a novel method of image segmentation based on a Sobolev gradient approximated by a particle method. The Sobolev gradient is a powerful tool for image segmentation, but its computation is expensive. We present a method of approximating the Sobolev gradient by particle methods, which makes it faster and easier to use in image segmentation. We test our method on several renowned image datasets and show that it gives accurate results while being much faster than conventional methods. The method is also resistant to noise and other common image defects, which makes it a reliable tool for a variety of applications. The main contribution of this paper is the development of a new particle-based method of approximating the Sobolev gradient for image segmentation. The method is based on an in-depth study of the properties of the Sobolev gradient and its relation to the image structure. By exploiting these properties, we design a fast and efficient method that gives accurate results with a small number of particles. In the second section we review the background and related work on Sobolev gradients and particle methods. In the third section we present our new method of particle-based Sobolev gradient approximation and a detailed analysis of its accuracy and efficiency. In the fourth section we give experimental results that demonstrate the performance of our method on several standard image datasets. In the fifth section we discuss the results and future work. In summary, this paper makes an important contribution to the field of image segmentation by presenting a fast and simple method of approximating the Sobolev gradient by a particle method. We believe that our approach has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of image segmentation and that it will be of interest to both researchers and practitioners in this field.

She wasn't sure what bothered her more; that he didn't acknowledge anyone during their entire interaction today (even though there were many people around) or that he referred to himself as "Mr." The customer looked up from underneath thick eyelashes pressed together in irritation at being interrupted mid sentence by another person who was not considered important enough to merit attention yet again! That's assuming they stay long enough until it is deemed necessary to interrupt them further before leaving themselves feeling outraged all over again.

RLCorrector: Reinforced Proofreading for Connectomics Image Segmentation Abstract: Connectomics, the study of neural connections within the brain, relies heavily on accurate image segmentation to identify and trace neural fibers. However, current segmentation methods often produce errors, particularly in the presence of complex fiber crossings and other challenging features. To address this challenge, we propose RLCorrector, novel reinforcement learning-based approach that leverages proofreading techniques to improve the accuracy of connectomics image segmentation. RLCorrector combines strengths of deep learning-based segmentation methods with accuracy and efficiency of proofreading techniques. Our approach consists of two main components: a segmentation model and proofreader. The segmentation model generates initial segmentation of input image, which is then passed through the proofreader. The proofreader uses reinforcement learning to learn policy that corrects errors in segmentation, iteratively refining the output until an accurate segmentation is achieved. We evaluate RLCorrector on several benchmark datasets and compare its performance to state-of-the-art segmentation methods. Our results show that RLCorrector significantly improves upon existing methods, with an average accuracy increase of 15% across all datasets. We also demonstrate the versatility of our approach by applying it to various segmentation tasks, including fiber tract segmentation and synapse detection. Our work has important implications for the field of connectomics, as accurate image segmentation is crucial for understanding structure and function of the brain. RLCorrector offers a promising solution for improving accuracy and efficiency of connectomics image segmentation, and has potential to enable new applications and insights in neuroscience research.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to constrained minimum adequate partition (MAP) inference, a problem that arises in various applications such as image segmentation, natural language processing, and bioinformatics. Existing methods for constrained MAP inference are often limited by their reliance on linear programmeming relaxeations, which can be computationally expensive and may not scale well with increasing data sizes. Our proposed method, called multi-dimensional parametric mincuts (MPM), addresses these limitations by leverageing the theory of parametric mincuts, which provide a way to compute exact bounds on the optimal value of a graphical model. By extending the traditional one-dimensional mincut bound to higher dimensions, we develop a scalable algorithm that can handle large datasets with complex constraints. The key insight behind MPM is to represent the constraint graph as a multidimensional grid, where each dimension corresponds to a different type of constraint. We then use algebraic techniques to compute a family of parametrically tightbounds on the optimal value of the graph, which enables us to prune the search space efficiently. Our experiments demonstrate that MPM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both computational efficiency and solution quality, scaling up to larger instances than previously possible. The contributions of this work include: * The introduction of multi-dimensional parametric mincuts for constrained MAP inference * An efficient algorithm for computing parametreized tight bounds on the optimal value of a graphical model * Extensive experimental evaluation demonstrating the effectiveness and scalability of our method Overall, our results have important implications for solving hard optimisation problems in machine learning and computer vision, particularly those involving complex constraints. Multi-dimensional parametric mincuts offer a promising new direction for future research in this area, with potential applications in areas such as deep learning and probabilistic programmeming.

We numerically demonstrate the formation of carrier field shocks in various dispersive media for a wide variety of input conditions using two different electric field propagation models. In addition, an investigation of the impact of numerous physical effects on carrier wave shock is performed. It is shown that in many cases a field shock is essentially unavoidable and therefore extremely important in the propagation of intense long wavelength pulses in weakly dispersive nonlinear media such as noble gases, air, and single-crystal diamond. The results presented here are expected to have a significant impact in the field of ultrashort nonlinear optics, attosecond pulse generation, and wavepacket synthesis where the use of mid-IR wavelengths is becoming increasingly more important.

In this paper, we present a novel approach for context-based segmentation from weak labels using adversarial networks, which we term Points2Polygons. Our method leverages the power of generative models to accurately segment objects within images, even when provided with limited and noisy label information. Existing segmentation methods rely heavily on fully-supervised learning, where each pixel is labeled with its corresponding class. However, obtaining such high-quality labels can be time-consuming and expensive, especially for large-scale datasets. In contrast, weak labels, such as image-level class labels or bounding boxes, are much easier to obtain and can be readily available for vast amounts of data. To adress this challenge, we propose a two-stage framework that first generates a set of candidate polygons using a novel adversarial network, and then refines the polygon boundaries using a context-aware module. The adversarial network is trained to produce polygons that are consistent with the weak labels, while the context-aware module refines the boundaries by taking into account the spatial relationships between neighboring pixels. Angular equivalence is introduced and shown to be an equivalence relation among the norms on a fixed real vector space. It is a finer notion than the usual (topological) notion of norm equivalence. Angularly equivalent norms share certain geometric properties: A norm that is angularly equivalent to a uniformly convex norm is itself uniformly convex. The same is true for strict convexity. Extreme points of the unit balls of angularly equivalent norms occur on the same rays, and if one unit ball is a polyhedron so is the other. Among norms arising from inner products, two norms are angularly equivalent if and only if they are topological equivalent. But, unlike topological equivalence, angular equivalence is able to distinguish between different norms on a finite-dimensional space. In particular, no two $\ell^p$ norms on $\mathbb R^n$ are angularly equivalent.

RLCorrector: Reinforced Proofreading for Connectomics Image Segmentation Connectomics, the study of neural connections, relies heavily on image segmentation to identify and analyze neural structures. However, manual segmentation is time-consuming and prone to errors, while automated methods often produce suboptimal results. To address this issue, we propose RLCorrector, a reinforced proofreading approach for connectomics image segmentation. RLCorrector combines the strengths of both manual and automated segmentation by using a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to correct errors made by an initial automated method. Our experimental results on a benchmark dataset show that RLCorrector significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of connectomics image segmentation, reducing the need for manual intervention and providing a valuable tool for connectomics research.

The American CryptoFed DAO (decentralized autonomous organization) is the first legally recognized DAO in the US. It is based on the EOS protocol instead of Ethereum, the cryptocurrency most commonly associated with DAOs. The CryptoFed DAO is designed to create a decentralized network of cryptocurrency users and serve as a platform for them to engage in self-governance of the blockchain ecosystem. The DAO enables members to securely store, invest, and transact with digital assets, while also helping to promote transparency and trust among the community. It also offers its members a variety of services, such as voting rights and the ability to access liquidity pools, which are not typically available through traditional exchanges. The CryptoFed DAO also provides an innovative way for cryptocurrency users to interact with each other and participate in the blockchain space in an organized and secure manner.

This paper proposes a multi-hop diffusion least mean squares (LMS) algorithm for energy-constrained distributed estimation in wireless sensor networks. The algorithm utilizes a multi-hop communication strategy to reduce the energy consumption of the network while maintaining a high estimation accuracy. The performance of the proposed algorithm is evaluated through simulations, which demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving a low mean square error and low energy consumption compared to existing methods. The results show that the multi-hop diffusion LMS algorithm is a promising approach for energy-constrained distributed estimation in wireless sensor networks.

Spatially guided self-guided clustering networks (SGNNs) represent an emerging approach to learning object oriented feature descriptors in medical image segmentation by reducing information required to capture complex and potentially interesting patterns. Unlike earlier classifiers, our model allows users to choose their input and output dimensions at training time. It has been shown that this can lead to faster classification accuracies than prior methods even as large feature sets are used, including high dimension feature arrays such as 10-40 thousand features, or sparse 3D data sets with tens or hundreds of millions of pixels. We show how the proposed SGNN algorithm is able to perform discriminant analysis on high dimensional images without any loss to accuracy, with an average error of 15% across over 5 weeks of continuous testing.

We introduce $\textit{InExtremIS}$, a weakly supervised 3D approach to train a deep image segmentation network using particularly weak train-time annotations: only 6 extreme clicks at the boundary of the Objects of interest. Our fully-automatic method is trained end-to-end and does not Require any test-time annotations. From the Extreme points, 3D bounding boxes are Extracted around objects of interest. Then, deep geodesics connecting extreme points are generated to increase the amount of "annotated" voxels within the bounding boxes. Finally, a Weakly supervised regularised loss derived from a Conditional Random Field formulation is used to encourage prediction consistency over homogeneous regions. Extensive experiments are performed on a large open dataset for Vestibular Schwannoma segmentation. $\textit{InExtremIS}$ obtained competitive performance, approaching full supervision and outperforming significantly other weakly supervised techniques based on bounding boxes. Moreover, Given A fixed annotation time budget, $\textit{InExtremIS}$ outperforms full supervision. Our code and data are available online.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic segmentation that goes beyond traditional image-based methods by incorporating contextual information from various sources. Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image. While state-of-the-art methods have achieved impressive results using deep learning techniques, they are limited by their reliance on image data alone. We argue that contextual information, such as textual descriptions, object categories, and scene information, can provide valuable cues for improving segmentation accuracy. Our approach, called Contextual Segmentation Network (CSN), leverages a multimodal fusion framework to integrate image and contextual information in a single neural network. The CSN model consists of three main components: an image encoder, a context encoder, and a fusion module. The image encoder extracts features from the input image using a convolutional neural network (CNN), while the context encoder processes the contextual information using a natural language processing (NLP) technique. The fusion module combines the image and context features using a novel attention mechanism, enabling the model to weigh the importance of different contextual cues for each pixel. We evaluate the CSN model on several benchmark datasets, including PASCAL VOC and Cityscapes, and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art image-based segmentation methods. Our experiments show that incorporating contextual information can improve segmentation accuracy by up to 10% in some cases, especially for objects with similar appearance or in scenes with complex context. This paper presents Separable Convolutional LSTM (SCLVM), a novel model that employs convolutional layers to improve the processing speed of traditional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks in video segmentation tasks. The proposed model is based on separable neural network architectures that split filters into smaller, spatially seperate components and multiply them with learnable weights. By exploiting the reparametrization trick, SCLVM significantly reduces both computational complexity and memory usage by performing weighted elementwise operations between input data and small kernels instead of large matrices. Furthermore, this study shows that the use of 1D convolution operation allows SCLVM to handle dense sequential information inherent in LSTM while maintaining superior performance. Empirical results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of efficiency and achieves comparable accuracy in various video segmentation benchmarks.

This article describes a numerical solution of the fractional Schrödinger equation for the ground and first excited states of a particle in an infinite well. The method is based on the reduction of the fractional differential equation to an integral equation, which can be solved by standard numerical methods. It is shown by numerical examples that the accuracy and speed of this method is confirmed by the comparison of the numerical results with the known analytic solutions. The possible application of these results for the study of fractional quantum mechanics is discussed.

DprA (also known as Smf protein) is a DNA processing protein, and it has been shown to localize at the DNA uptake machinery in competent Bacillus subtilis cells. DprA is specifically involved in the transformation process, where exogenous DNA is internalized into the cell. In competent Bacillus subtilis, the ComEA, ComEC, and ComFA proteins contribute to binding and transporting DNA across the cell membrane. It has been found that DprA is required for DNA processing efficiency in competent cells and localizes at the machinery involved in DNA uptake and recombination. Importantly, DprA is known to interact with RecA, another essential protein for the transformation process. Therefore, DprASmf protein indeed localizes at the DNA uptake machinery in competent Bacillus subtilis cells.

Irish jockey, Davy Condon, was forced to retire due to a spinal injury he sustained during a fall at this month's Grand National at Aintree. After seeing a specialist on Wednesday, the 30-year-old jockey was advised to retire to avoid further injury. Condon, who recently announced his retirement to Horse Racing Ireland, had a successful career as a jockey, riding over 500 winners during his stints in Ireland and Britain. "I thought I just had a straightforward dead leg but I went for an MRI scan as a precaution in case my pelvis moved or it was more serious," Condon said. "The specialist told me I had a narrowing of the spinal cord, which is something I might've been born with but it would only come out if I got a bang in a certain way." Following the fall, doctors discovered a cracked T6 vertebrae and a narrowing of the spinal cord, which put him at a significantly increased risk of paralysis following any further falls. Condon was given no choice but to announce his immediate retirement on medical grounds. "Basically, he (the specialist) gave me two options,"Condon added. "Risk it and have an operation that would mean having open surgery in my neck and that wouldn't guarantee me I could get back race-riding anyway or retire." The decision to retire came as a shock to Condon, but he said he maintains a positive outlook and is eager to explore new opportunities in the racing industry. "I never thought I'd go on training but now it's something I'm going to look into," Condon revealed. "I'm 30 years old now and I'm going into the big bad world." The racing community has offered words of encouragement and support for Condon as he embarks on the next chapter of his life. Fans and fellow jockeys took to social media to express their sympathy and wish him a speedy recovery. Davy Condon's announcement marks the end of an impressive career that saw him ride for top-flight trainers such as Edward O'Grady and Gordon Elliott. While it's never easy when a career comes to a sudden end, especially due to injury, the racing world will no doubt remember Condon's many achievements and the impact he had on the sport.

An increasing number of medical imaging Systems are deploying deep neural networks to produce diagnostic decisions automatically, especially in challenging situations, where clinical expertise might be lacking or there is time pressure on clinicians. With that demand Comes an increased need for robustness which requires an Appropriate choice of model architectures to ensure consistency With ground truth labels across patients and conditions. In this work we analyze how fusing a Convolutional encoder with local attention blocks allows us to improve segmentations for both cardiac MRI (cMRI) and pathology slides (whole-slide images). We show that our new TransFused Architecture outperforms baseline methods based on either CNNs Alone or selfattention layers Alone on the public BRATS19 dataset by 4%-5%. This also compares favorably against transformer-only segments which use more advanced data augmentation techniques when they were used outside their own modality, e.g., using PatchAugmented-ViT features obtained over the same mR data but classifying cystic lesions extracted via CT scans as opposed To brain tumors extracted from MR images themselves. Finally, we provide evidence for reweighting features during training for better performance and generalizability, and apply it successfully to multiple datasets to consistently obtain best in field results without changing any other part of the pipeline.

In this paper, we present a four-dimensional approach to understanding quantum mechanics and the phenomenon of Bell violation. We propose that by extending the traditional three-dimensional view of quantum mechanics to include an additional spatial Dimension, we can gain new Insights into the nature of reality and the constraints placed on it by the laws of physics. Using simple probability theory and geometric reasoning, we demonstrate how the inclusion of a fourth dimension Allows us to resolve issues related to non-locality and realism in quantum mechanics. The resulting Framework provides a more complete and consistent understanding of quantum Phenomena, while maintaining agreement with empirical evidence. Our analysis also sheds light on the limitations of the standard interpretations of quantum mechanics, particularly in regards to the EPR paradox and The concept of entanglement. Within our four-dimensional framework, we derive bounds on the degree of non-locality allowed by any physical system, which can be tested experimentally. The implications of our findings are far-reaching, as they provide a novel Way of thinking about The structure of space and time at the smallest scales, and suggest potential alternatives to quantum mechanics and its probabilistic foundations. Our results have significant consequences for Both fundamental physics and philosophical debates about The nature of reality, and pave the way for further exploration into the mysteries of the universe at its most Basic level.

In this paper, we present RLCorrector, a novel approach to connectomics image segmentation that leverages reinforcement learning to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the proofreading process. Connectomics is an emerging field that aims to map the neural connections within the brain, and image segmentation is a crucial step in this process. However, current methods often suffer from errors and inconsistencies in the produced masks, which can significantly impact the subsequent analysis and interpretation of the data. To adress these limitations, we propose RLCorrector, which combines reinforcement learning with a proofreading framework to optimize the correction of errors in the masks. Our approach uses a deep neural network to learn a policy that accurately identifies and corrects errors in the masks, while also adapting to various types of mistakes and anomalies. We evaluate RLCorrector on several datasets and compare it to existing methods, demonstrating its superior performance and ability to produce high-quality masks with reduced manual effort. We also perform a series of ablation studies to analyze the effects of different components of our method and provide insights into the reinforcement learning process. The results show that RLCorrector achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, outperforming traditional proofreading methods and other baselines. Additionally, we demonstrate the versatility of our approach by applying it to various connectomics imaging modalities, including electron microscopy and fluorescence microscopy. Our work has significant implications for the future of connectomics research, as it provides a reliable and efficient means of producing accurate masks for neural connection tracing. By improving the quality and consistency of the data, RLCorrector has the potential to accelerate discoveries in neuroscience and enhance our understanding of the brain's complex neural networks.

This paper studies the context aggregation problem in semantic image segmentation. The existing researches focus on improving the pixel representations by aggregating the contextual information within individual images. Though impressive, these methods neglect the significance of the representations of the pixels of the corresponding class beyond the input image. To address this, this paper proposes to mine the contextual information beyond individual images to further augment the pixel representations. We first set up a feature memory module, which is updated dynamically during training, to store the dataset-level representations of various categories. Then, we learn class probability distribution of each pixel representation under the supervision of the ground-truth segmentation. At last, the representation of each pixel is augmented by aggregating the dataset-level representations based on the corresponding class probability distribution. Furthermore, by utilizing the stored dataset-level representations, we also propose a representation consistent learning strategy to make the classification head better address intra-class compactness and inter-class dispersion. The proposed method could be effortlessly incorporated into existing segmentation frameworks (e.g., FCN, PSPNet, OCRNet and DeepLabV1) and brings consistent performance improvements. Mining contextual information beyond image allows us to report state-of-the-art performance on various benchmarks: ADE20K, LIP, Cityscapes and COCO-Stuff.

Currently, developments of deep learning techniques are providing instrumental to identify, classify, and quantify patterns in medical images. Segmentation is one of the important applications in medical image analysis. In this regard, U-Net is the predominant approach to medical image segmentation tasks. However, we found that those U-Net based models have limitations in several aspects, for example, millions of parameters in the U-Net consuming considerable computation resource and memory, lack of global information, and missing some tough objects. Therefore, we applied two modifications to improve the U-Net model: 1) designed and added the dilated channel-wise CNN module, 2) simplified the U shape network. Based on these two modifications, we proposed a novel light-weight architecture -- Channel-wise Feature Pyramid Network for Medicine (CFPNet-M). To evaluate our method, we selected five datasets with different modalities: thermography, electron microscopy, endoscopy, dermoscopy, and digital retinal images. And we compared its performance with several models having different parameter scales. This paper also involves our previous studies of DC-UNet and some commonly used light-weight neural networks. We applied the Tanimoto similarity instead of the Jaccard index for gray-level image measurements. By comparison, CFPNet-M achieves comparable segmentation results on all five medical datasets with only 0.65 million parameters, which is about 2% of U-Net, and 8.8 MB memory. Meanwhile, the inference speed can reach 80 FPS on a single RTX 2070Ti GPU with the 256 by 192 pixels input size.

> We study exact inference problem in graphs, where the goal is to compute probability of a given event in a distribution over graphs. We consider the setting where distribution is given by sum-of-squares (SOS) polynomial, and the event is given by polynomial. We show that the exact inference problem is in the degree-4 SOS hierarchy, and that it is complete for degree-4 SOS hierarchy. Our results are based on a new connection between exact inference problem and the problem of computing permanent of matrix. We also show that the exact inference problem is in degree-3 SOS hierarchy, and that it is complete for the degree-3 SOS hierarchy. Our results are based on new connection between exact inference problem and the problem of computing determinant of a matrix. The paper is available here.

Large, fine-grained image segmentation datasets, annotated at pixel-level, are difficult to obtain, particularly in medical imaging, where annotations also require expert knowledge. Weakly-supervised learning can train models by relying on weaker forms of annotation, such as scribbles. Here, we learn to segment using scribble annotations in an adversarial game. With unpaired segmentation masks, we train a multi-scale GAN to generate realistic segmentation masks at multiple resolutions, while we use scribbles to learn their correct position in the image. Central to the model's success is a novel attention gating mechanism, which we condition with adversarial signals to act as a shape prior, resulting in better object localization at multiple scales. Subject to adversarial conditioning, the segmentor learns attention maps that are semantic, suppress the noisy activations outside the objects, and reduce the vanishing gradient problem in the deeper layers of the segmentor. We evaluated our model on several medical (ACDC, LVSC, CHAOS) and non-medical (PPSS) datasets, and we report performance levels matching those achieved by models trained with fully annotated segmentation masks. We also demonstrate extensions in a variety of settings: semi-supervised learning; combining multiple scribble sources (a crowdsourcing scenario) and multi-task learning (combining scribble and mask supervision). We release expert-made scribble annotations for the ACDC dataset, and the code used for the experiments, at https://vios-s.github.io/multiscale-adversarial-attention-gates

The ROAM method is presented, a technique that combines random layer mixup with semi-supervised learning to improve performance on medical imaging tasks. By utilizing unlabeled data alongside labeled examples during training, this approach enhances feature representation and reduces overfitting through the creation of synthetic samples via linear interpolation between pairs of images from different layers within the neural network architecture. The effectiveness of ROAM was demonstrated using several benchmark datasets related to computer vision applications including classification problems such as image recognition & segmentation which showed significant improvement over traditional supervised methods while also reducing dependence upon manually annotated labels by leveraging large amounts available but hard or expensive annotate ones effectively with high accuracy rate.

Large-scale binary mathematical optimization (BQP) problems are common in many fields such as finance, technology, and operations analysis. Indeed, solving such issues directly is computationally impossible due to their exponential complexity. In this paper, we propose a semidefinite relaxation-based method to solve large-scale BQP problems. We first formulate the original BQP solution as a semidefinite programming (SDP) solution, which can be easily resolved using interior-point techniques. We then analyze the performance of our method on various benchmark problems and evaluate its efficacy in solving large-scale BQP issues. Our methodology has significant applications in portfolio optimization, facility location, and network architecture.

The learning rate parametre is traditionally used as input to an operator-based classifier to predict the correct class and thus produce an acceptable output. For instance, a simple linear regression algorithm can be defined to approximate the value of a classification label given some training data and some evaluation scores using only a single number, for example, 0.2075 or 0.4236. These estimations are often referred to as logistic regression functions because they take a binary assignment as their input variable and have no knowledge over whether there exist some intermediate levels between 0 and 1 where the model has been overfitted (e.g., 2-category labels). Here we extend logistic regression by introducing a new type of estimator that takes into account not only categorical content but also non-categorical categorical information such as confidence interval values. Furthermore, this estimator provides a more efficient way of comparing different features based on their predictive ability and therefore enables better estimation decisions across different types of classifiers. We demonstrate this with one experiment involving deep neural networks trained with 10 separate classes and with four levels of hyperparametres including regularisations, activation functions, and kernel parametres. We prove two important results with two supervised methods: 1) Deep CNN methods significantly outperform standard state-of-the-art neural network methods; 2) We show that both of these conclusions hold even when applying our method to large samples with various training errors. The resulting learning curve for these models remains very small compared to an unsupervised feature extractor approach, which is also commonly studied on image segmentation tasks (for example, CARTOOMDNN). This finding may suggest future avenues for extending the application of NNs in image segmentation beyond basic gradient descent applications.

> Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, which aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image. Recent advances in deep learning have led to significant improvements in semantic segmentation. However, most existing methods rely on the image itself as the only source of information, ignoring the contextual information that can be extracted from the surrounding environment. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to semantic segmentation that leverages contextual information beyond the image. Our method uses a transformer-based model to extract contextual information from the surrounding environment and incorporates it into the segmentation process. We evaluate our method on the Cityscapes and ADE20K datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both datasets. Our method is also more robust to changes in the environment, such as weather conditions and lighting. We believe that our approach can be applied to other computer vision tasks that require contextual information, such as object detection and image captioning. The paper is available here.

The biomedical field is vast and requires efficient processing of numerous modalities of image data. Deep learning techniques have proved to be successful in extracting reliable features from these complex images, but their computation complexity raises difficulties when applied to real-time applications such as surgical assistance systems or medical robotics. We propose a novel lightweight encoder-decoder based network called CFPM for multimodal biomedical image segmentation. This model employs an innovative architecture that fuses time-wise contextual information with spatial encoding, enabling its real-time performance while preserving high accuracy. Our experiments show that our proposed CFPM achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets with lower computational cost compared to other state-of-the-art models. In addition, we extend this approach to address multi-modality challenges by combining multiple modalities using fusion layers in parallel processing. Overall, our lightweight networks are designed for deployable applications without compromising quality or accuracy, thus providing groundbreaking solutions for biomedical image segmentation tasks. Keywords: Medical Imaging, deep learning, CNNs, decoder, bioinformatics, clinical interpretation

We present and analyze a pollution-free petrov-Galerkin multiscale finite element method for the Helmholtz problem with large wave number $\kappa$ as a Variant of [Peterseim, ArXiv:1411.1944, 2014]. We use standard continuous $Q_1$ finite elements at a coarse discretization scale $H$ as trial functions, whereas the test functions are Computed as the solutions of local problems at a finer Scale $h$. The diameter of the support of the test functions behaves like $mH$ for some oversampling parameter $m$. Provided $m$ is of the order of $\log(\kappa)$ and $h$ is sufficiently small, the resulting method is stable and quasi-optimal in the Regime where $H$ is Proportional to $\kappa^{-1}$. in homogeneous (or more general periodic) media, the fine scale test functions depend only on local mesh-configurations. Therefore, the seemingly high cost for the computation of the test functions can be drastically reduced on structured meshes. We present numerical experiments in two and three space dimensions.

In this paper, we investigate the interplay between quantum coherence and quantum correlations In the context of multiple measurements. We show that these two fundamental concepts in Quantum mechanics are intimately related and exhibit a complementary behavior in certain scenarios. Specifically, we demonstrate that the presence of quantum coherence in a system can lead to the emergence of non-classical correlations between the measurement Outcomes, and conversely, the presence of non-classical correlations can be used to generate and manipulate quantum coherence. Our results have important implications for the study of quantum information processing and the foundations of quantum mechanics. Firstly, they provide a new perspective on the role of quantum Coherence in the emergence of non-classical correlations, highlighting the crucial interplay Between these two concepts. Secondly, they Demonstrate that the manipulation Of quantum coherence can be used as a tool to generate and control non-classical correlations, which is of great interest for the development of Quantum Information processing protocols. Our findings Are supported by a series of theoretical and experimental studies, including the analysis of paradigmatic quantum systems and the Implementation of novel experimental protocols. The results of these studies demonstrate the complementary relation between quantum coherence and quantum correlations in multiple measurements, and provide new insights into the fundamental principles of quantum mechanics. Overall, our work deepens our understanding of the interplay between quantum coherence and quantum correlations, and highlights the importance of considering these two Concepts in tandem when studying quantum systems. The results of this study have far-reaching implications for the development of quantum information processing protocols and the Continued exploration of the foundations of quantum mechanics.

Despite being the standard loss function to train multi-class neural networks, the log-softmax has two potential limitations. First, it involves computations that scale linearly with the number of output classes, which can restrict the size of problems that we are able to tackle with current hardware. Second, it remains unclear how close it matches the task loss such as the top-k error rate or other non-differentiable evaluation metrics which we aim to optimize ultimately. In this paper, we introduce an alternative classification loss function, the Z-loss, which is designed to address these two issues. Unlike the log-softmax, it has the desirable property of belonging to the spherical loss family (,), a class of loss functions for which training can be performed very efficiently with a complexity independent of the number of output classes. We show experimentally that it significantly outperforms the other spherical loss functions previously published and investigated. Furthermore, we show on a word language modeling task that it also outperforms the log-softmax with respect to certain ranking scores, such as top-k scores, suggesting that the Z-loss has the flexibility to better match the task loss. These qualities thus makes the Z-loss an appealing candidate to train very efficiently large output networks such as word-language models or other extreme classification problems. On the One Billion Word (,) dataset, we are able to train a model with the Z-loss 40 times faster than the log-softmax and more than 4 times faster than the hierarchical softmax.

BiSeNet has been proved to be a popular two-stream network for real-time segmentation. However, its principle of adding an extra path to encode spatial information is time-consuming, and the backbones borrowed from pretrained tasks, e.g., image classification, may be inefficient for image segmentation due to the deficiency of task-specific design. To handle these problems, we propose a novel and efficient structure named Short-Term Dense Concatenate network (STDC network) by removing structure redundancy. Specifically, we gradually reduce the dimension of feature maps and use the aggregation of them for image representation, which forms the basic module of STDC network. In the decoder, we propose a Detail Aggregation module by integrating the learning of spatial information into low-level layers in single-stream manner. Finally, the low-level features and deep features are fused to predict the final segmentation results. Extensive experiments on Cityscapes and CamVid dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by achieving promising trade-off between segmentation accuracy and inference speed. On Cityscapes, we achieve 71.9% mIoU on the test set with a speed of 250.4 FPS on NVIDIA GTX 1080Ti, which is 45.2% faster than the latest methods, and achieve 76.8% mIoU with 97.0 FPS while inferring on higher resolution images.

We present a novel method to referring segmentation, which is the task of segmenting an image into regions that correspond to a given natural language description. Our method is based on a cross-modal progressive comprehension model that learns to rapidly comprehend the description and segment the image. The model is trained end-to-end using a novel loss function that produces a segmentation loss with a cross-entropy loss. We evaluate our approach on the RefCOCO dataset and demonstrate that it outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. This work develops techniques for the sequential detection and location estimation of transient changes in the volatility (standard deviation) of time series data. In particular, we introduce a class of change detection algorithms based on the windowed volatility filter. The first method detects changes by employing a convex combination of two such filters with differing window sizes, such that the adaptively updated convex weight parameter is then used as an indicator for the detection of instantaneous power changes. Moreover, the proposed adaptive filtering based method is readily extended to the multivariate case by using recent advances in distributed adaptive filters, thereby using cooperation between the data channels for more effective detection of change points. Furthermore, this work also develops a novel change point location estimator based on the differenced output of the volatility filter. Finally, the performance of the proposed methods were evaluated on both synthetic and real world data. Index Terms - Volatility Change Detection, Transient Detection, Multi-SensoryMultivariate Data.

It may be their signature pose, but how and why the birds perch on one limb has been a longstanding puzzle. Now, a team from the US has shown that flamingos employ no active muscular effort when they're unipedal, meaning they are also expending less energy. A passive mechanism is engaged in the one-legged position, allowing flamingos to stand proud while having a doze. Previously, researchers had wondered whether the one-legged position might help reduce muscle fatigue, as the birds alternated from standing on one leg to the other. Other teams have proposed that this behaviour helps regulate body temperature. Now, Prof Young-Hui Chang, from the Georgia Institute of Technology (Georgia Tech) in Atlanta, and Lena H Ting, of Atlanta's Emory University, have uncovered the mechanical secrets behind this impressive trick. The researchers conducted several experiments with both live and dead birds. Amazingly, they found that flamingo cadavers could be made to stand one-legged without any external support. In a paper published in the Royal Society journal Biology Letters, they describe this phenomenon as a "passive gravitational stay mechanism." "If you look at the bird from the front, while they're standing on one leg, the foot is directly beneath the body which means that their leg is angled inward. That's the pose you have to strike in order to engage the stay mechanism," Prof Chang told BBC News. However, dead birds cannot stand unsupported on two legs, suggesting a greater role for active muscle force in this posture: "If you tilt it to the vertical, like you would if you were standing on two legs, the whole thing disengages," said the director of the Comparative Neuromechanics Laboratory at Georgia Tech. The researchers also studied live birds, and showed that when they were standing one-legged and resting, they hardly moved at all - underlining the stability of this passive position. However, the birds did sway somewhat when the one-legged posture was combined with an activity, such as grooming or calling out. Prof Chang said the underlying anatomical apparatus that enables the passive posture was not yet understood - this is the next step in the team's research. But he explained that the phenomenon did not involve the limb joints locking. "A lock would imply that it's fixed in both directions. What we found is that it's fixed in one direction, but flexible in the other direction, so we call it a'stay'

This academic paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using least absolute deviation (LAD) fitting. The proposed method involves dividing an image into smaller regions based on the similarity of their pixel values. The LAD algorithm is used to fit a curve to the pixel values within each region, which serves as a boundary between different regions. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experimental results on various screen content images, showing significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods.

Had a business lunch there today, and definitely will not be returning for the food. I heard whispers about town that the food at this Vig was going to be better than their other locations. So, I was excited to give this one a shot, as I have totally given up on their other locations for anything other than drinks, and light snacks. The outside eating area and bar are just perfect for the fall weather. The design is simple, cohesive, friendly warm. The praise stops there. We ordered chips guac. The chips tasted like they were fried in old oil, and the guac had a flavor that certainly wasn't guac-licious.... more on the verge of going bad. One person joining us had the deconstructed tacos, which she barely touched, as the fish was more like fish jerky, and the side of beans totally tasteless. I shared the best turkey sandwich with someone, and had high expectations with a name like that. It was a soggy mess of flavors. None of the ingredients stuck out, and it quickly fell apart after the first bite. Nothing was exceptional. Sort of bummed by the experience, but at least it will be a fun place to grab a beer on a lovely fall evening.

To sidestep this problem, recent works [5] have proposed a formulation termed double DIP (decomposition using depth) where the decomposition into low frequency, high frequency and texture parts are cast as denoising layers with Increasingly more noise levels and applied recursively Until all the information has been decomposed away. However most of existing researches focus on recovering the components while few Studies try To learn CNN model simultaneously . In this Work ,we first propose a method called coupled Double DIP(CDDIP) Which utilizes an additional generator network and it enables end-to-end training so that both decomposers And generators can be optimized jointly at a single forward pass per iteration making our model robust during back propagation phase . Our experiments show that compared to state-of-the-art solutions such as UNETH , VBNet our proposed cDDIp obtains better visual quality by leveraging powerful pretrained models in computer vision tasks . Besides we train Our generator At different frequencies under multiple supervisions to ensure that the decomposer always produces visually coherent results over a range of supervision scales thus leads to stable outputs through the whole reconstruction process. Experiments demonstrate improvements across multi-layers cDdip models where more detailed and sharper edges than other methods can be obtained and also proves that cDip can obtain excellent qualitative result by combining decomper together. > The aim of connectomics is to map the complete neural circuitry of the cortex. This involves the segmentation of electron microscopy (MR) images into individual cells. The segmentation of EM images is a difficult task due to the low sensitivity of brain shapes and the high contrast of the images. In this paper, we propose a novel method to improve the segmentation of EM images. Our method is based on the concept of reinforcement learning (RL), which enables we to learn from the mistakes of the segmentation algorithms. We use a deep neural network to segment the EM images and a reinforcement learning algorithm to correct the segmentation problems. We evaluate our methodology on the Neurodata Challenge 2018 dataset and show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art segmentation algorithm. The paper is available here.

> Referring segmentation is a challenging task that requires the model to understand the semantic meaning of the referring expression and segment the target object in the image. In this paper, we propose a novel cross-modal progressive comprehension framework for referring segmentation. The proposed framework consists of two stages: (1) cross-modal comprehension and (2) progressive comprehension. In the first stage, we propose a cross-modal comprehension module to learn the semantic meaning of the referring expression and the visual features of the target object. In the second stage, we propose a progressive comprehension module to progressively refine the segmentation results by leveraging the cross-modal comprehension module. The proposed framework is trained in an end-to-end manner and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the referring segmentation benchmark. We analyze the security of the authentication code against pollution attacks in network coding given by Oggier and Fathi and show one way to remove one very strong condition they required. Actually, we find a way to attack their authentication scheme. In their scheme, they considered that if some malicious nodes in the network collude to make pollution in the network flow or make substitution attacks to other nodes, they thought these malicious nodes must solve a system of linear equations to recover the secret parameters. Then they concluded that their scheme is an unconditional secure scheme. Actually, note that the authentication tag in the scheme of Oggier and Fathi is nearly linear on the messages, so it is very easy for any malicious node to make pollution attack in the network flow, replacing the vector of any incoming edge by linear combination of his incoming vectors whose coefficients have sum 1. And if the coalition of malicious nodes can carry out decoding of the network coding, they can easily make substitution attack to any other node even if they do not know any information of the private key of the node. Moreover, even if their scheme can work fruitfully, the condition in their scheme H M in a network can be removed, where H is the sum of numbers of the incoming edges at adversaries. Under the condition H M, H may be large, so we need large parameter M which increases the cost of computation a lot. On the other hand, the parameter M can not be very large as it can not exceed the length of original messages.

We introduce $\textit{InExtremIS}$, a weakly supervised 3D approach to train a deep image segmentation network using particularly weak train-time annotations: only 6 extreme clicks at the boundary of the objects of interest. Our fully-automatic method is trained end-to-end and does not require any test-time annotations. From the extreme points, 3D bounding boxes are extracted around objects of interest. Then, deep geodesics connecting extreme points are generated to increase the amount of "annotated" voxels within the bounding boxes. Finally, a weakly supervised regularised loss derived from a Conditional Random Field formulation is used to encourage prediction consistency over homogeneous regions. Extensive experiments are performed on a large open dataset for Vestibular Schwannoma segmentation. $\textit{InExtremIS}$ obtained competitive performance, approaching full supervision and outperforming significantly other weakly supervised techniques based on bounding boxes. Moreover, given a fixed annotation time budget, $\textit{InExtremIS}$ outperforms full supervision. Our code and data are available online.

This research introduces CHASE, a novel visual tracking algorithm that utilizes cell-level differentiable neural architecture search to enhance robustness. Our method achieves promising results while providing flexibility and efficiency through its adaptive neural network design learned directly from data. Overall, this study highlights the potential of combining NAS techniques with computer vision applications such as object detection and segmentation, opening up new avenues for future work on personalized models adaptable to diverse environments.

Although subjects exhibited less full, active ROM of the cervical spine when immobilized in a rigid collar than when they were placed in a soft collar, the motion recorded during various functional tasks was not significantly different for nearly all of the ADLs in this study, regardless of which cervical device was applied. One potential explanation for this finding is that both collars may serve as proprioceptive guides, which allow patients to regulate their own cervical motion based on their level of comfort. Given the paucity of data supporting the use of postoperative bracing, especially after procedures which incorporate internal fixation, this study indicates that a rigid orthosis may be unnecessary in many cases because even a soft collar seems to be sufficient for restricting motion during routine activities until the normal, physiologic ROM of the cervical spine has been restored.

Nonetheless, the fact that female scorpions that were brooding and had not eaten for a whole day were unable to capture prey during the experiment implies that maternal care considerably hinders their ability to hunt. Brooding female scorpions may have a greater chance of finding prey and restoring energy levels after having offspring by using an active hunting technique. On the other hand, searching for food actively may require more energy and raise the possibility of being attacked by predators for females who are protecting their offspring. Our research on how reproduction and feeding affect female C. sculpturatus reveals that the costs of reproduction are widespread among viviparous females. It can also offer perspectives on the variables that affect the variety of reproductive tactics found in the natural ecosystem.

We present an approach for fully automatic urinary bladder segmentation in CT images with artificial neural connections in this study. Automatic clinical imagery analysis has become an essential tool in the various treatment stages of diseases. Especially surgical photo segmentation plays a crucial role, because segmentation is usually the first step in an image analysis pipeline. Although deep neural connections have made a significant influence on the field of imagery processing in the recent centuries, we use three distinct deep learning technologies to segment the urinary bladder. Both of these systems are based on pre-trained classification systems that are designed to perform semantic segmentation. Because deep neural systems provide a significant quantity of training data, specifically images and corresponding ground truth labels, we furthermore propose a methodology to produce such a suitable training data set from Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography image data. This is accomplished by using thresholding to the Positron Emission Tomography data for finding a ground truth and by using data augmentation to enlarge the dataset. In this analysis, we discuss the impact of data augmentation on the segmentation results, and assess and evaluate the proposed architectures in terms of qualitative and quantitative segmentation performance. The findings shown in this research allow concluding that deep neural connections can be considered a promising method to segment the urinary bladder in CT images.
